in accordance with rule 12 and other important points in the rules of procedure, i have only a statement for you today on the candidates for the presidency of the european parliament; we are not discussing any other issues. in accordance with the conditions laid down in the rules of procedure, i have received the following nominations for the post of president of the european parliament: mr nirj deva (applause), mr martin schulz (applause), mrs diana wallis (applause). the candidates have informed me that they agree to run. the current composition of parliament is set out in today's minutes. i hereby adjourn this session in accordance with the rules of procedure. thank you, and i'll see you tomorrow for the election of the chairman and then the vice-chairmen and the quaestors.
this court is now in session. i would remind you that, under the rules of procedure, no debate may be held under the chairmanship of the outgoing president other than the election of the president or the verification of the terms of office, and i therefore do not accept any comments or discussions from you today. we can only deal with the election of the president of the european parliament. it's in accordance with our rules of procedure. i am also aware that the rules of procedure require that we elect the president of parliament before noon today. rule 13 of the rules of procedure says that only a political group or at least 40 members may be nominated as candidates. in accordance with the conditions laid down in the rules of procedure, i have received the following three candidates for the office of president of the european parliament: (i presented these candidates to you yesterday, but i will read them again today) mr nirj deva (applause), mr martin schulz (applause) and mrs diana wallis (applause). i just wanted to point out that the candidates have informed me that they're willing to run. ladies and gentlemen! we're going to proceed to the voting procedure. i would like to ask you to not leave your seats prematurely, because most of the voting instructions will be given in polish, so if you move from your seats and don't have headphones, you won't be able to hear me. we now move to the vote. i would remind you that, in accordance with rule 14 (1), the candidate who receives an absolute majority of the valid votes cast is elected. empty or invalid ballots are not counted as votes cast. first, i'm going to draw lots for eight members, eight colleagues, who will be responsible for calculating the votes. they shall be drawn by lot from the total number of names of all members present in the lottery. i'm showing you the urn with the names of the deputies and i'm pulling out the names of the following: borsellino, sógor, panayotov, poc, bagó, kalinowski, kalfin, perello rodriguez. colleagues, please come and stand behind me on the podium. ladies and gentlemen! i'm giving you the exact voting instructions that you received in your inbox. i understand that not everyone has had time to read them, so i'll go over the different phases of the vote. first, the ballot papers and envelopes will be handed out. these ballots and envelopes can now be distributed. we now move to the vote. i would remind you again that an absolute majority of valid votes is required for the election. when you receive your ballot papers, please tick the box next to your name. so the candidate we vote for gets our stamps. you can only vote for one candidate. if there are two or three stamps on the ballot, the vote is void. if there are any letters, the vote is invalid. if you want to improve your voice, you can. then you give this voting card to the people who are giving out the cards and you take the new card, but you have to give the old card back. i will not read the names of the voting members. please remain in your seats. what's the big deal? the names of members who took part in the vote must be entered in the minutes. therefore, i ask that you sign the list of eligible voters before you put your ballot in the ballot box. i'd like you to sign the letter at the urn. at the same time, i would ask that you have your id and show it. you have to put the ballot paper in the envelope, before that, we fold the ballot paper into four. the members designated to conduct the vote and to count the votes shall vote at the end. that's all i have to say. i understand your colleague has a question about the voting procedure.

mr president, prime minister, please! denmark is the next country to assume the presidency of the council of the european union, promising to lead the community out of the economic crisis and to ensure economic growth. we only have six months left. it should be recalled that a similar priority was included in the agenda of the belgian, hungarian and polish presidencies, not to mention the lisbon treaty. it is in the interest of all european union citizens that this objective should finally be achieved. however, looking at the efforts of previous presidents and the continuing economic problems, it is almost certain that the next presidency will have to put a similar priority on its agenda. the danish presidency will also deal with the budget for the years 2014-2020. it is therefore particularly important that it maintains such an important cohesion fund, which enables the new members of the union from central and eastern europe to develop. in the 'green europe' area, denmark is committed to sustainable economic growth on the one hand, and to continuing to push for eu climate packages on the other. many experts believe that these two trends are mutually exclusive.
in writing. it is a pleasure to welcome our danish colleagues from the presidential trio. i am also pleased to see a woman, prime minister helle thorning-schmidt, at the head of the council of the european union. the programme you have presented is extremely extensive and ambitious. but seeing the energy your government is putting into it, i'm sure it will be successful. in times of crisis, europe must be dynamic and responsible. the decisions taken at the european summit of 9 december 2011 must now be implemented in order to strengthen fiscal policies and safeguard economic stability in the member states. we must continue to work towards a more secure financial market, a more competitive community market and a greener europe that is safer for all its citizens. in the danish presidency, i am personally pleased to see the continuation of the work on the so-called digital agenda within the framework of the european programme for culture. as the author of the report on the legal use of orphan works, which is one of the priorities for the next 6 months, i am convinced that this project will be completed and will open up to all interested parties the cultural treasures hidden in the archives for years. i wish you perseverance, efficiency and much success in the coming months of intense work.
in writing. the danish presidency faces a very difficult task, especially as the european union remains in a deep crisis. this crisis is not only affecting the budgetary situation of the member states, but above all the identity of the eu. the days are coming when the future of a united europe will be decided. it is becoming increasingly clear that the new intergovernmental agreement being prepared to strengthen the economic union may not only lead to a deepening of the divide between the euro area and the rest of the world, but also to a weakening of the community institutions. the danish presidency should therefore focus primarily on defending the cohesion of the union, its community character and the principle of solidarity. it may be worrying that copenhagen has no immediate plans to adopt a common currency. in addition, the previous government was in favour of reducing the community budget. but i hope that this will not affect the attitude of our danish friends. i am optimistic that they will be able to represent the interests of all the member states during their presidency. my optimism is based mainly on the memory of how brilliantly they handled the finalisation of the accession negotiations preceding the so-called great enlargement. it seems that at such a difficult time, the presidency of the council could not have been more appropriate. it is not only known for its openness to the other side's arguments and a culture of compromise, but also for its ability to use these qualities in practice.
in writing. one of the activities of denmark during its presidency of the council will be to continue the talks on the new multiannual financial framework. i hope that the presidency will negotiate successfully on cohesion policy, which is the most pro-development policy of the european union. i am also pleased that the danish government will be taking up the issue of a european programme for social change and innovation, which is to provide, among other things, greater access to micro-credit to increase self-employment and business development, or greater freedom of movement for job seekers and the possibility of recruiting workers from across europe. i believe that an effective cohesion policy and increased employment are one of the key aspects on the way to generating economic growth in the european union.
in writing. the year 2012, which is the year of the danish presidency, is the european year of older persons and solidarity between generations. i am pleased that the presidency is planning a number of initiatives in this regard. according to un projections, the proportion of people aged over 65 in europe will reach 23.8% by 2030. in poland, it is projected that by 2060 there will be two retirees for every three people in work, and the number of people over 80 will increase four to fivefold. the problem of an ageing population is widely recognised as a challenge that the european union as a whole must address. we urgently need an effective european demographic policy with a particular focus on economic and health issues. i hope that the danish presidency will promote gender equality in the context of the europe 2020 strategy, in line with the commission's strategy on this issue and the adapted european pact for gender equality. i call for the conclusion of the proposal for a council directive on the implementation of the principle of equal treatment between persons irrespective of religion or belief, disability, age or sexual orientation. as the author of the opinion on women in sport and the written statement on amateur sport, i draw attention to the promotion of physical activity to improve the health and quality of life of eu citizens.
in writing. this is the seventh time that denmark holds the presidency of the council. but it seems that this presidency will be the most difficult. however, we believe that an efficient and constructive danish administration, experienced in european leadership, can coordinate the crisis response. at the same time, however, we are aware that, as in the case of poland, the fact that denmark is not a member of the euro area may prove to be a difficulty. the danish presidency will also have to agree on the key elements of the future budgetary framework for 2014-2020. there's no doubt that the negotiations will be very difficult. we expect denmark to be able to find a compromise among the member states to ensure that the funds are at the right level for each of the union's policies. i believe that the slogan "budget for the future" used by danish politicians means that we should focus on new challenges in particular areas, rather than radical redistribution or cuts. i am personally convinced that denmark will be able to meet the challenges and expectations we place on it. it is worth recalling that it was under the danish presidency in the second half of 2002 that the difficult accession negotiations with the group of 10 new europe countries, including poland, were concluded. i hope that denmark can achieve similar successes in the budget negotiations and in the fight against the debt crisis.
in writing. mr. speaker, thank you, prime minister, for your presentation of the programme today. i would like to express my strong support for some of his ideas and to be particularly sensitive to a few issues. i welcome the fact that the danish presidency is committed to supporting strong european institutions, to respecting common principles based on european values and to stimulating dynamic economic development. the important thing is that you want to base your actions on the principle of solidarity. i think this is the most important thing, because it is the only way to avoid serious and dangerous divisions within the union, whatever economic and social turmoil we may still face. budgetary discipline and fiscal austerity are indisputably necessary. but i do hope that, as you come from a country with a tradition of social economy, you will make sure that these cuts are not the most vulnerable. it is particularly concerned about the situation of women, whose employment rate is still low and is likely to fall further, young people who remain unemployed for too long after completing their education, the situation of the disabled and the occupational involvement of people over 50. despite the savings, there must be money and adequate programmes to create new jobs. i wish you success in achieving your goals.
in writing. a responsible, dynamic, green and secure europe - these four adjectives, which underline the priorities of the new presidency, are welcome, as they show that denmark, despite the enormous crisis in which the union finds itself, is enthusiastic about its task. but he is not happy with the start of the danish presidency, especially its role in the most important negotiations currently underway on the fiscal pact. the presidency should safeguard the interests of the union as a whole and oppose any division within the union which would occur without the consent of all its members. i therefore expect her support for the most inclusive and community-wide fiscal compact possible.
in writing. the danish presidency has entered a difficult period for a united europe, with many, often difficult, decisions ahead. the economic crisis, which we are still trying to overcome, has shown us that we cannot rely on european policy to solve problems in the short term. it is therefore crucial to implement the priorities of the danish presidency for a dynamic and responsible community economy, which should become a constant point of reference for each successive presidency. only by deepening cooperation in a spirit of solidarity can we build a truly common, efficient and innovative market that is capable of maintaining its global position in the future, not just for a few years but for decades. but this requires making the difficult choices and setting ambitious political, economic and social targets, which no member state can achieve on its own. this huge workload must be felt at all levels, from the learning and development of children and young people, through social organisations, businesses and all those involved in their operation, to individuals and organisations operating internationally. only in this way can we together, in solidarity and in a lasting way, strengthen the foundations of the european union.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution on the outcome of the european council meeting of 8 and 9 december 2011. i am aware of the deep and still imperfect implications of the proposed intergovernmental agreement. the first concerns the fact that this agreement is in addition to the current structure and the constitutional documents of the european union. it is still unclear how this agreement can work, what references it will make to the lisbon treaty. i hope that this agreement will not undermine the treaty, that it will ensure the proper role of the european parliament and that it will not discriminate against countries outside the euro area, including poland. the agreement must not undermine democracy within the eu or replace the commission, parliament or council with other entities.
in writing. - the current version of the draft fiscal pact raises a number of legal doubts which will affect its effective enforcement. the signing and ratification of the agreement in the form proposed will lead to the creation of an alternative legal order, whose relationship with european law remains undefined in many areas. the issues that remain unresolved include the primacy of community law, the jurisdiction of the court of justice of the eu and the competences of the other european institutions. the question of insufficient democratic legitimacy, which can only be achieved through greater involvement of the european parliament and national parliaments, is also of importance. from the point of view of economic governance, however, it should be noted that most of the provisions of the proposed intergovernmental agreement can be implemented more quickly and efficiently by the community method, using the stability and growth pact as revised in december. the community method formula also allows for the inclusion of non-euro area countries in the decision-making process, thereby avoiding additional institutions within the eu. in this context, attention should be drawn to the european parliament's demand that all parties to the agreement, both current and future euro area members, should have the right to participate in the eurogroup summits. it should be noted that the euro area does not operate under an opt-in formula and that non-euro area countries are only covered by a temporary derogation. inclusion in economic governance decision-making is therefore in everyone's interest, as most member states have committed themselves to joining the euro area.
in writing. − we are aware that the current economic situation in the euro area requires immediate action. although the fiscal compact contains many positive provisions imposing financial discipline on the participating countries, there are also many doubts about its functioning. first, we need to answer the question: how will the pact affect the transparency of decision-making in the eu? it creates a parallel dimension of cooperation and the exact date for its incorporation into the treaties is difficult to determine. will this not weaken integration within the european union? second, critics point out that the fiscal pact duplicates many of the solutions contained in the six-pack or the stabilisation and growth pact. does this not create confusion in the interpretation of individual acts of eu law? thirdly, there is a risk that the pact will create divisions within the union, the consequences of which are difficult to predict. the european council in brussels on 14 and 15 december adopted a resolution on the situation in the former yugoslavia and the situation in the former yugoslavia. fourthly, the recent changes to the draft document have led to the marginalisation of the role of the community institutions. the european commission is deprived of the power to bring complaints against member states to the court of justice of the eu, which has always been its domain, and the european parliament's participation in euro-area summits is very much marginalised.
in writing. - i voted in favour of a resolution which criticises the current draft intergovernmental fiscal pact. the new agreement should not diminish the role of the european parliament in the ongoing negotiations or of the non-euro area member states. the new agreement must include an amendment to the right of future euro-zone members to participate in euro summits. the debate should be between all the members of the european union. the european commission agrees that the union's unity should be the overriding objective. secondly, it is necessary to ensure that the new draft agreement contains a clear statement that eu law takes precedence over the agreement in the pipeline. i am convinced that only the community method can transform monetary union into a really strong economic and fiscal union. we are ready for further negotiations and will seek to reach a constructive and solid agreement that takes into account our key demands.
in writing. - parliament is in favour of the greatest possible communityisation of the agreement, which, in the face of the united kingdom's opposition, could not be concluded within the union. markets want decisive action, and euro area countries need to commit quickly to greater financial discipline. however, this does not mean that it should be done at the expense of the unity of the union and its institutions. hence my support for the ep's demand for the implementation of the pact through community legislation, a central role for the european commission, the involvement of the ep and, most importantly for poland, absolute support for the participation of countries that do not yet have a common currency in the euro summits.

in writing. hungary's membership of the eu and respect for community law and its rules and principles must not be a limitation on its right to self-determination. nor can the democratic mandate of the hungarian authorities to take decisions on the will, de facto, of the hungarian people and in the rule of law be questioned. it is also no secret that some initiatives are unacceptable to many european elites, because, among other things, they infringe the interests of large multinational corporations and business. the actions of the european commission are a demonstration of the means of exerting undue pressure on a democratic state and give a bad name to that institution.
in writing. in the face of the financial crisis, when it is so important to safeguard the independence of policy-making, new rules on the hungarian central bank may cause concern, which deprive its head of the right to elect deputies and increase the number of members of the monetary council elected by the government. the weakening of central bank independence may be contrary to article 130 tfeu, which provides that central banks shall not take instructions from the governments of the member states in the performance of their tasks and that the governments of the member states shall undertake not to influence the members of their decision-making bodies. but we must not forget that the eu is a community of sovereign states, which have the right to self-determination within the limits of the obligations assumed by the treaties. in the event of doubts as to the compatibility of national legislation with the acquis communautaire, a procedure is provided for, under which the member state submits its interpretation. prime minister orbán's open communication strategy and his willingness to listen to the arguments of the european institutions are to be commended. the debt crisis is the main subject of our discussions these days, but we must not forget the values on which the european community was built. in this context, it should be noted that while some are so vehemently criticizing hungary for violating the treaties, at the same time we are dealing with attempts to weaken the principle of the primacy of european law through an intergovernmental agreement and a similar debate, although equally substantive, is not taking place.
in writing. yesterday, the european commission decided to open an accelerated infringement procedure against hungary in three cases concerning the independence of the hungarian central bank, data protection authorities and judicial matters. the commission has given the hungarian government one month to make changes. the procedure initiated by the commission only addresses part of the problem faced by hungary, which is a breach of european law. in addition, hungarian democracy has a clear problem with respect for minorities, guaranteed rights of the opposition, media pluralism. i am grateful to the hungarian people for voicing their views and opinions, and often criticisms, which i listen to with attention. it is not possible to "lock" subjects of public debate, such as tax policy, in the basic law, even when these are the best solutions. the public has a right to seek change on such issues. democracy is majority rule, but it also requires respect for minorities, so now we should all look at the hungarians with concern and pressure the rulers to back off from these changes that are harmful to democracy. i wish hungary and its government success in the reforms that are helping it to emerge from recession, and that their commitment to freedom and democracy and respect for our common european law will be at the forefront of all their actions.
i think after durban we can be sure of one thing - we can be sure that our thinking about reducing emissions is isolated in the world. the extension of the kyoto protocol is just one illustration of this impasse. i think that instead of banging our heads against the wall, we should be reviewing our climate policy so that its costs are distributed more equitably. the entry of the next phase of the emissions trading system in 2013, for example in poland, will mean even more pressure to move paper, glass and cement production outside the eu. in the context of the crisis, climate policy is becoming a thorn in the side of european industry, which will eventually move to countries that are our direct competitors. the european union, by pursuing such a radical climate policy, alone, without a global agreement, is thus taking responsibility for the economic slowdown.
the lack of agreement in durban is a fact which the commission should take note of. the commissioner should also finally take this into account in her decisions and actions, because political action should be rational, pragmatic, predictable and aimed at a clear objective. climate policy is only rational if it is seen in a global perspective. greenhouse gases know no bounds, so if it is the fact that at durban canada is already completely withdrawing from the kyoto agreement, if it is the fact that the other countries which are major emitters, such as china, are not deciding on significant emission reductions together with europe, it means that our policy is a donksoteria, that our policy is not effective, that even if we manage to reduce these limits, as the commissioner and the commission propose, it will not bring the intended effect on global climate change. politics can only make sense if there is global agreement. if the effect of european policies is to reduce the competitiveness of our economy in favour of less developed countries, to which industry and jobs will migrate, this will have fatal consequences for our economy. for poland alone, it is estimated that between 2013 and 2020 this will mean a loss of 250 000 jobs. and energy bills will go up by 30-40% from 2013. this could really mean a crisis both in the european union and in relation to the european union. this is very bad news, commissioner. you have to take them into account. the facts!
in writing. ladies and gentlemen, before the durban summit, many questions were asked - what will be the position of the european union, is there a chance that by 2020 the paths of action of all countries will go in the same direction and will it be possible to work out a compromise, what about the possibility of selling co2 emissions after 2012 from the unused limits set in the kyoto protocol? i personally think, and i always stress, that we must not forget the current economic situation caused by the global economic crisis, where many not only european but also global markets are wondering what will happen in the near future. all these questions are being overlapped by globalisation, the financial crisis and national interests, and i believe that the eu's position should be a compromise, taking into account the current economic situation in europe and the world, the position of both citizens and businesses that create jobs, and the approach of the world's largest economies, such as india, china and the usa. thank you.
in writing. at the durban conference, the european union made another attempt to implement the second phase of the kyoto protocol commitments. at the conference, poland was awarded the 'fish of the day' for its continued failure to reduce greenhouse gas emissions. those who seek and implement ways to reduce emissions have been reprimanded in a way that is completely incomprehensible. the eu's commitments should be conditional on comparable commitments from other world economies in order to maintain the competitiveness of the union's economy. in addition, the largest developing countries should be adequately included in this process, in line with the conclusions of the european council of october 2009. europe currently emits only 11% of its total co2 emissions into the atmosphere and is fully complying with its emission reduction commitments under the protocol. only by acting together can we help to combat climate change. the european union should not agree to extend the kyoto protocol without including these key countries. this scenario would result in only a negligible part of the emissions being covered by the transitional arrangement. the eu's ability to effectively lead the world in the fight against climate change will therefore depend to a large extent on its ability to persuade large emitters to join the fight against climate change in a legally binding way. solidarity and a fair sharing of reduction commitments should be the pillars of the further development of climate policy in the eu.

in writing. − food waste is an example of an inefficient use of resources, with negative consequences for economic efficiency and the environment. moreover, in a world where about one sixth of the population is hungry, food waste is a huge ethical problem. the european union, which is part of the developed world, should therefore improve the efficiency of the food chain, so that food management is improved at every stage, from production to the consumer's table. as a union of states that respects and promotes fundamental human rights, including food security, we should take decisive steps to reduce food waste.
in writing. - the problem of food waste is becoming more serious. according to the european commission, the annual production of food waste in the 27 member states is over 89 million tonnes, or about 179 kg per person. the average european household throws away 20-30% of the food they buy, while 2/3 of it is still fit to eat. and if we don't take decisive action, by 2020, the total amount of food wasted will increase to about 126 million tons. food waste itself has consequences not only in ethical, economic, social and nutritional terms, but also in health and environmental terms, as food waste contributes to global warming. in agriculture, food waste occurs both in the production and storage of agricultural products. the food industry often wastes food at the raw material stage, then during transportation, when food is transported thousands of kilometres away. however, the problem is most acute in households. excessive purchases, expired products, and poor food management can all result in food ending up in the garbage. member states should therefore adopt common strategies to tackle this problem, starting with the exchange of good practice.

in writing. ladies and gentlemen! on monday, after long and difficult negotiations, an agreement was reached on a budgetary pact, which was officially named the 'treaty on stability, coordination and governance in the economic and monetary union'. and although, as is often the case in difficult negotiations, the agreement is not perfect and does not fully satisfy all parties, it has the support of the 25 members of the european union. this is clearly an expression of the conviction that europe does not need disputes, but rather quick and decisive action. one of the key elements of the negotiations was the issue of the participation of non-euro area countries in eurogroup summits. and although the negotiated provision places some restrictions on access to these meetings, it was thanks to the great determination of the non-euro countries that the eu's institutional set-up was safeguarded and the principle of community-ness was not breached. the representatives of the eu institutions, josé manuel barroso, martin schulz and herman van rompuy, also stood up to the challenge and defended the unity of the community. but reaching an agreement does not end the debate on the shape of the union and the place of non-euro countries in the new order. now we have a very important task to do, which is to put the provisions of the pact into practice. what will be particularly important for us is how article 12 of the treaty is implemented, that is, whether the voice of the non-euro area signatory countries is actually heard at the eurogroup summits.
in writing. from the perspective of improving economic governance in the eu, it is positive that the fiscal compact introduces qualitatively new instruments that will contribute to a more responsible fiscal policy in the future. the most important of these are the principle of budgetary balance, the obligation of the signatory states to implement this principle in their national legal systems and the enhancement of the jurisdiction of the court of justice of the eu. however, the effectiveness of the fiscal compact will only be verified in practice once its provisions become binding on the states. there is a risk that the introduction of statutory automatic corrective mechanisms could force excessive pro-cyclical economic policies, which would deepen the debt crisis. the frequency of non-euro area countries' participation in eurogroup meetings also remains a matter of uncertainty. the intergovernmental agreement stipulates that euro area countries will be able to hold meetings only within their own borders when discussing commitments relating to the single currency, the governance of the euro area and convergence within the area. since the scope of the eurogroup's closed meetings can be interpreted broadly, it will be very important to apply a literal interpretation in this case in order to safeguard the priority of the community method.
, in writing. on 30 january, the heads of state or government adopted the text of the treaty on stability and governance in the economic and monetary union, also known as the fiscal compact. the positive aspects of the original text include the commitment to implement the pact within the eu treaty structures within a maximum of five years, the consistency with eu law and the prevention of drastic divisions among the member states. we must remember that the treaty adopted is only one element in the fight to rebuild trust. it remains an instrument primarily designed to increase budgetary discipline, whereas the causes of the current euro area crisis are more complex. structural reforms are needed to restore confidence in financial institutions and improve ratings of credit rating agencies. just as urgent as the financial management of the member states is the change in the european labour market, which must be made more flexible in order to combat unemployment, especially among young people, more effectively. the financial supervision system should be completed. the sme sector should receive additional support, as it is the sector that has created 80% of jobs in europe over the last five years. although the european parliament has opposed any form of intergovernmental agreement, preferring eu secondary legislation, we cannot afford to criticise the fiscal pact sharply. by supporting this document, we will send a clear signal to the outside world that the eu is determined to address the causes of the current crisis.
in writing. to begin with, few people liked the idea of a fiscal compact from the start. moreover, the pact is not really needed by the european union. apart from the obligation on member states to put savings thresholds into their constitutions, there is nothing new in this agreement. it is worth noting, however, that these negotiations were about something far more important than the budgetary commitments of the member states - the future of the european union. we have been debating whether the community's unique method will be saved or whether decisions on eu economic policy will be taken solely through selfish negotiations between states, on the basis of the principles we have known since the 19th century congresses. we also asked ourselves whether new intergovernmental institutions would be created, directly competing with the eu institutions. finally, we had the real possibility that the union would be divided equally and more equally. so far, we've managed to avoid this dark scenario.

rapporteur. − mr president, i am glad that lady ashton decided to participate in this debate. it is an honour for us and especially important because the eeas has now been in action for a year and the time has come for the first reviews and summaries of the service’s existence. the report was adopted in the committee on foreign affairs in december last year by an overwhelming majority. by allocating such an important topic to the foreign affairs committee, the european parliament wanted to emphasise that in foreign policy terms brics is no longer just a catch phrase coined around trade and growth-related indicators, but that these countries have come of age and started a certain form of foreign policy making. the report goes beyond the individual country-by-country approach when thinking about brazil, russia, india, china and south africa, and tries to see in what senses their common points of interest have brought them together. one such common item is the feeling of marginalisation on the global level, especially when it comes to brics participation in the key institutions of global economic and financial governance. that is why the brics countries have decided to strengthen their cooperation on political and foreign policy issues. it could be called a mutual support network, but one that can be a convenient fall-back option when the situation requires concerted action. the report indicates several areas, in particular the number of votes held in the un security council, on libya, on syria, on the status of the eu in the un general assembly and others, like recently in durban on climate change, which show that when the foreign policy objectives of the brics converge they are ready to concert efforts and act jointly. in most cases the brics take positions opposed to those of the european union and they contest our positions and policy. are we ready to react and to act? those countries enjoy – some of them to a special degree, especially democracies like india and brazil – a privileged relationship with us. at the same time, they will not give the union the right to speak in the united nations. baroness ashton, in your report you praise the geographical desk structure of the eeas as the leading source of advice and briefing on respective countries. the report which i submitted encourages a coordination mechanism within the eeas which would allow geographical desk officers responsible for particular brics countries to exchange and coordinate information and positions in cases where concerted action on our side can be expected. such cooperation would have added value for you and your officials in devising future strategies. the mechanism i suggest does not require a modification of the current eeas structure and can be of a purely functional nature. i was told that the first time such coordination took place was in preparation for attending the foreign affairs committee meeting to discuss my report. i am glad to hear that, as it is the best proof that the report has already brought some results. now, it will be of the utmost importance that this coordination is maintained and developed further and does not become a one-time event in the history of your service. the brics as a cross-continental foreign policy actor does exist and the ostrich policy of hiding one’s head in the sand, believing that the brics will stop existing, will not serve the eu well.
mr. chairman, please! the european parliament's report on the relations between the eu and the brics countries. i would like to congratulate the author of this project, because it really captures in a very good way what is the essence of the times in which we live. the world around us is changing rapidly, and one of the signs of this change is the rapid development, especially economic development, of countries that until recently were considered to be only so-called developing countries. the result of this rapid development is, of course, an increase in political importance. today, these are not just economic powers, but increasingly serious political actors, against whom, as mr saryusz-wolski points out in his draft report, the union must develop a coherent strategy of action. but i agree with those who say that these are diverse countries. these differences are clearly visible when we look at domestic political realities, for example, and especially the approach to civil liberties and human rights. these are the values that are important to us europeans, to european politicians: not just economic cooperation, but the care for values that are close to us and the promotion of these values in relations with countries whose importance in the world is increasing. i agree with the conclusions and proposals of the report, which say that we should develop a common strategy for dealing with these countries with our partners who share the same value system, such as the united states. finally, i would like to join in the call for the european parliament to have a greater say in the formulation of common positions and strategies and to participate in summits between the european union and its strategic partners, including those countries we now call brics.
rapporteur. − mr president, first let me thank lady ashton for the openness with which she has received the report, which calls for more action, as somebody has rightly said. i would also like to thank my colleagues, who understood the message and contributed to the richness of this report. i am happy because what has a name exists. it is named – the phenomenon has been named, so it does exist. so we should treat this report as an early notification – not a warning – about forthcoming challenges. i did not deny in this report that there are huge differences between them, but i tried to extract the tiny part which is common to them, even if it is only 1% of the picture and even if it is only restricted to issues on which they have similar positions and act as an entity and foreign policy in the making. you said, lady ashton, that we should avoid a ‘west versus the rest’ confrontation. this is also my dream, but the world is not as we would wish. my comment would be ‘yes, but...’. in some cases, we see that democracies there – india and brazil – were seduced by autocracies regarding their common positions, and regarding human rights and democracy (and i see the convergence with the watson report), libya, syria, the ivory coast and sudan. in some cases they were jointly challenging the current system of international governance. the question of the eu voice in the un was an appalling and most regrettable case. having strategic partners (as we call them with all due respect) means having reliable partners sharing values. very often they neither share nor practice our values. in the policy towards the brics we should avoid the creation of coalitions of the lowest common denominator on democracy and human rights. our policy should be inclusive, in order to involve them in the system of governance – but on the basis of universal values. they should be our partners and not our opponents, as has happened in the past. in the eu we should think strategically. in 2050 they will be immensely bigger than we are. let us be prepared. the eu has to act together under your leadership, lady ashton, to avoid member states’ divergent policies, for example on libya. regarding libya, brics were more united than the union itself. we need strong european foreign policy.
in writing. the eu's policy towards the brics countries is a particularly difficult one. on the one hand, these are countries that are experiencing rapid economic growth. on the other hand, it is worth remembering that more than 70 percent of the world's poorest people live in middle-income countries. there is no doubt that the brics countries differ from the eu countries not only in terms of economic indicators, but also in terms of values that we consider universal and indispensable. the eu and its member states' policy towards brics should also be supported by our citizens. to support something, you have to understand it. i'm afraid that many europeans don't understand why china is the recipient of relatively large amounts of development aid (oda) from europe. it's really hard to explain and rationalize. i believe that the focus of the eu's policy strategy towards brics should be to consistently build common standards that reduce differences in both competitiveness and value. we will not achieve this by unilaterally raising standards in the eu. i mean, for example, plans to reduce co2 emissions. anyone who knows anything about the brics countries knows that they are not going to limit their development in any way. changing this attitude is a major challenge for the eu.

in writing. as president of the polish rugby union and vice-president of the rugby intergroup in the european parliament, i would like to comment on the item on the social role of sport. i appreciate the fact that the rapporteur is calling on the commission to present the possibility of financing european union sports policy in the new multiannual financial framework. i also think it would be a good idea to create the possibility of financing from the esf the employment of instructors and coaches who provide additional sports activities in schools and youth centres. the social role of sport deserves to be highlighted. sport is of great importance for personal development, especially for children and young people, and is also an effective tool for social integration. it also plays a significant role in combating all forms of discrimination and social exclusion. that is why i think it is so important to promote sport and to support all kinds of sporting initiatives.
in writing. as a writer on women in sport, i consider the following issues to be particularly important for women in sport: education and sport. we need to guarantee equal access to sport for women and men, to affordable, age-appropriate sporting activities. in particular, among girls and women from economically and socially disadvantaged backgrounds. disciplines that are tailored to women's needs and aspirations should be provided and promoted. equal access to decision-making positions in sporting activities and to the administrative structures of sports associations, as well as to the positions of sports coaches, is also important. despite the increase in the participation of women in sport that has taken place in recent years, their participation in decision-making and management has not increased. as long as there are no women in leadership and decision-making positions and thus no female role models in sport, the demand for equal opportunities for women and girls will not be able to be fulfilled. in the field of education and sport, i propose to launch awareness campaigns targeting kindergartens and schools to stimulate interest in sport among children and young people. it is important to increase, diversify and complement the physical education curriculum with issues related to women's training, such as differences in pace and athletic performance.
in writing. i welcome today's vote on the report on the european dimension of sport. the fact that, with the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon, this area has become a competence of the european union represents a turning point in the development of sport on a european scale. it is of the utmost importance that the european commission should present a specific budget for sport policy in the future multiannual financial framework. it is also important to establish the basis for the training and education of coaches and their qualifications, to encourage women to become more involved in professional sport and to condemn breaches of the fair play principle. professional competition is often saturated with negative emotions that go far beyond the boundaries of competition. in the context of society as a whole, this situation is unacceptable given the impact of the behaviour of athletes, especially on young people. it is necessary to note the urgent need to rebuild the values that come from pure sporting competition, it is also important to combat doping through prevention and information campaigns and to treat the trade in such products as a drug trade. coordinated action aimed at a uniform approach to the imposition and enforcement of sanctions against fans behaving in an aggressive or discriminatory manner will contribute to raising the level of security in stadiums during sporting events. in conclusion, i would also like to express my support for the creation of a non-public european register of sports agents.
mr. chairman, please! well, on november 18th, i asked the european commission about acta. this is a very important issue, one that is stirring up a lot of emotion and controversy in the public debate in many countries of the european union, including my country, poland. i asked, among other things, whether acta is compatible with the fundamental rights, basic solutions and legal standards of the european union. on 5 january i received a reply from commissioner de gucht on behalf of the commission that the agreement was in accordance with the legislation in force in the european union and, moreover, that it was also in accordance with the general principles of european union law and, as i said, with the charter of fundamental rights of the european union. but on november 24, 2011, the european court of justice ruled, to my surprise, that it was quite the opposite, that acta violated fundamental human rights and rights guaranteed by the european union in one respect. so this is a matter of urgency.
the year 2012 is exceptionally rich in various important events in the european union. the budget pact just agreed is due to be signed in march. other anti-crisis measures will also be continued. in addition, work on the union's multiannual financial framework for the period 2014-2020 is entering a key stage. this year we are also celebrating the 50th anniversary of the common agricultural policy. it was one of the first policies to have a very large share of the union's budget, but its tasks under the treaties of rome were also very important: to ensure that there was enough food at the right price and to guarantee a fair income for farmers. europe experienced famine during and after the war, and the problem of food became a particularly important objective for the union. fifty years of experience in the common agricultural policy is exceptionally rich. this year they will be the subject of a series of conferences and a major information campaign, and the conclusions will be used to make a proper forecast of the cap for 2014-2020.

illegal or unregulated landfills and incinerators are a serious problem. they pose a safety risk to both health and the environment. this also means that there are no savings from smart and efficient waste management and no opportunities to recover valuable missing resources. it's also jobs lost. much remains to be done to raise awareness among citizens about the benefits of responsible waste management. it is important to coordinate waste management at regional and local level more closely and to make it easy to access and transparent for citizens not only how waste should be segregated but also what happens to it afterwards. the modernisation of waste management systems will require significant investments in many countries. the financing of these activities should also be a priority for the union. in addition, it would be particularly useful to step up activities to identify and exchange best practices at national and european level.
in writing. recognising the urgent need for responsible waste management, the european union has created a whole system of secondary legislation, imposing on member states a series of obligations relating to the storage, segregation and recycling of waste. the union is working towards a situation where waste is no longer a threat to the environment but a resource that is used efficiently. i think that this effort is definitely worthy of praise and support. however, it must be admitted that even the most sincere intentions and the most determined action of the eu cannot be effective if the member states do not express a desire to cooperate effectively in this area. despite the december 2010 deadline for transposition of the directive into national law, only six countries have succeeded in doing so. as the european parliament, we should pay particular attention to the opinion of the citizens of the union. it is reflected in the number of petitions submitted to the commission - 114 - which draw attention to the various aspects of waste management that are not in line with eu law. this shows that it is in the interests of the citizens of the union that the member states transpose the directive into their national legal systems as soon as possible. in the interests of the european union as a whole and of its citizens, i call on the member states to bring their national legal systems into line with the directive.
in writing. rapid and dynamic economic growth is inevitably linked to environmental risks. the european union, and in particular the european parliament, must therefore set environmental standards that are in line with changing economic realities. a major step forward in this regard was the implementation by member states of the waste management directive, which aimed to improve and raise the standard of waste management, treatment and disposal. this was necessary because of the huge amount of more than 2 million tonnes of waste produced annually within the union. however, as is apparent from the numerous requests received by the committee on petitions and the visits carried out, which are fully described in mr inturgaiz angulo's report, we can undoubtedly conclude that the purpose of the directive has been achieved only in part. therefore, additional efforts by the community as a whole are necessary to eliminate cases of non-compliance or incorrect implementation of the provisions of that directive. at the same time, we must not forget that the ultimate outcome of these actions largely requires the cooperation and commitment of society and the accountability of those who violate our common good.

in writing. - mr president, the growing role of the brics countries in foreign relations and international cooperation has an impact on the european union. for example, with china projected to become the world's leading economy in the near future, brussels must step up its efforts to effectively influence the emerging multipolar world order. a consistent approach to these countries as a potential bloc and the expansion of cooperation and strategic partnership with each of them, especially the democratic ones, is becoming one of the objectives of the eu's foreign policy. such a partnership will be an excellent tool with a potentially transformative character. brics countries, increasingly in concert, also decide the policy direction of leading international organisations such as the un. taking into account the economic and demographic potential of these countries, only a coordinated european policy can contribute to enhancing the union's role and effectiveness on the world stage. i support the resolution.
in writing. - the crisis in europe is not a cause for optimism. the recession is not abating but deepening, unemployment is increasing and the lack of innovation and new investment in europe is not improving either. instead of being the role model that it has been, europe is falling into a slump, unlike the brics countries, whose fast-moving economies are not feeling much of the global recession, and the economic forecasts are for it to accelerate further. they also strengthen their political standing by adopting common, often controversial, positions on conflicts and problems in the world. i therefore share the rapporteur's view that the union should cooperate closely with these countries, but not at any cost. we must remember their undeniable potential, without underestimating the value and potential of our own economy. this is a difficult challenge because, given the unequal conditions of competition, whether in terms of cheap labour at the expense of human rights, lower production standards or simply better natural conditions and access to natural resources, europe faces a difficult task. but we cannot give in to the pressure of economic rights alone and forget the fundamental european values.
in writing. - the high rate of economic growth in the brics countries and other emerging world powers is changing the balance of power in the world before our eyes. as the rapporteur points out, the combined importance of the seven largest emerging economies (brazil, russia, india, china, indonesia, turkey, mexico) is projected to exceed that of the g7 economies by 2050. these rising economic powers have already shown high ambitions in foreign policy and are likely to gradually take the lead in shaping world order and global strategies. this shows the importance of increasing internal eu cohesion and strengthening our common foreign policy. only by acting as one strong organism will we be able to match the rising economic and political powers and remain relevant in the new, multipolar system of world order and leadership. the emerging new balance of power in the world gives the union the opportunity to take the initiative and lead in the process of changing and reforming the system of world order, including the new powers. we have a chance to build a new platform for international foreign policy, based on mutual trust and shared values, that will facilitate cooperation on trade and economic issues, and in more effective ways to address global issues such as climate change, global peace and security, and sustainable development.
in writing. - mr president, promoting democracy and countering authoritarian and totalitarian regimes around the world is an important task for which we all have a responsibility. in this context, financial transactions and investments by non-democratic leaders in the eu member states are of particular importance. often benefiting from all the benefits of western civilization. given that these leaders are using their wealth, which is often illicit, to consolidate their power and oppress their own citizens, i support the recommendations contained in the resolution. increasing the range of restrictive measures by preventing sanctioned leaders from trading in money in member states, from travelling, from taking lessons and subsidising research centres, or from conducting business activities, are just some of the instruments we can use. i look forward to increased cooperation and synergy between all eu countries to present a coherent position on the condemnation of authoritarian regimes based on a unified and integrated approach.
in writing. − democracy, the rule of law, freedom and human rights are among the fundamental values of the european union. therefore, respecting and promoting them both within and outside the union should be one of our fundamental responsibilities. but it is not an easy task, especially when dealing with countries where these values, which are so precious to us, are marginalized or violated. the european union cannot stand by and watch these fundamental rights being violated by authoritarian regimes. the creation of a strong common foreign policy, with a sound political judgment, capable of skillful negotiation and, if necessary, of coercive measures without the use of force, is therefore necessary. the european union cannot remain indifferent when there is a brutal violation of human rights, when human lives are threatened, when peace is threatened. in order to be a good guardian of our values and at the same time an active defender of the rights of the oppressed peoples or national minorities, it is necessary in some cases to use restrictive measures. however, these measures will only be effective within the framework of a coherent european union policy, in which all member states participate consistently.
in writing. − the eu is the leading donor of humanitarian assistance. of the total eur 9.8 billion of humanitarian aid provided worldwide in 2010, 41% was delivered by the eu (accumulated by funds from the 27 member states in addition to the commission through dg echo). these funds allow the eu to show solidarity and provide immediate relief to regions hurt by natural and man-made disasters. the eu’s growing involvement and importance as a humanitarian aid provider is on the rise, and so are the requirements to ensure proper use of taxpayers’ money; thus i welcome the current report which reviews the budgetary control of eu humanitarian aid management by dg echo. identifying areas of weakness in control over the funds and proposing points where improvements could be made is important for enhancing the efficiency and effectiveness of humanitarian aid money. however, i also believe that the evaluation process should take account of the fact most recipient countries do not have the proper means to provide a full account of how money was spent, especially in a time of emergency. therefore we must also show flexibility and adjust our budgetary control requirements to existing capacities of the recipient countries, in order to ensure our money is properly spent.
in writing. - i am pleased that the european parliament has taken the initiative to introduce legislation in the member states to enable and facilitate the collection of consumer claims. the commission's research and surveys show that one in five consumers in europe would not take a claim under €1000 to court, and almost half say they would not take a claim under €200 to court. the obstacles faced by consumers are mainly high costs, the risk of litigation and long and complex procedures for claim settlement. in the event of a class action, 79% of respondents said they would be prepared to defend their rights in court. we should take steps to empower european consumers as the weaker party to the infringer. in poland, a collective redress mechanism already exists, the solutions to which could be useful in the work on a future european instrument. this is a relatively new instrument introduced by the law of 17 december 2009, so it still needs to be thoroughly checked in practice, but it is undoubtedly a step in the right direction. a common eu-wide collective redress mechanism is necessary to facilitate and enable citizens as well as businesses to exercise and enforce their rights. i congratulate my colleague, the rapporteur, on his initiative and look forward to the commission's proposals.

the rapporteur. - mr president, commissioner, i have to ask you to leave. the programme for the distribution of food to the most deprived in the european union has a long history. it began in 1987 when the council decided to make agricultural products from intervention stocks available to the member states for food aid to the poorest. in subsequent years, when food stocks from intervention were low, it was allowed to buy food for this purpose on the market. the evolution of the agricultural policy has contributed to the reduction of intervention stocks and thus to the need to increase food purchases on the market for this programme. this form of food procurement was challenged before the court of justice, which in april 2011 found that it was contrary to the legal basis and that the scheme should be limited to food from intervention stocks only, which meant that from 1 january 2012 the scheme was reduced from eur 500 million per year to just over eur 100 million. the european parliament then took decisive action and, in its resolution of 7 july 2011, called on the commission and the council to work urgently on solutions for 2012-13 in order not to limit the programme so drastically. it should be noted that the original commission proposal of september 2008 and the parliament's position of march 2009 were not adopted by the council. the commission's further approach of having the programme have a legal basis not only in the cap but also in social policy also did not get enough support in the council. only the active actions of the polish presidency led to the elimination of the blocking minority and the work gained momentum. a trilogue took place on 6 december 2011 in which parliament and the commission agreed to the council's position. the committee on agriculture and rural development subsequently accepted the results of the trialogue on 12 december 2011 at its meeting in strasbourg, and in a special meeting. the special committee on agriculture of the council gave its consent on the same day. this compromise was finally confirmed by the council at its meeting on 23 january 2012. on 26 february, the european parliament's committee on agriculture and rural development expressed its full support for the compromise adopted by the council and accepted the proposal to refer the council's position to the procedure for adoption by the european parliament's plenary. it should be noted that this position concerns the implementation of the 2012-2013 programme. the amount of eur 500 million per year is maintained, which is a very substantial amount. the programme was left to be implemented on the basis of a legal basis under the common agricultural policy. the european parliament's demands to use european products in the first place for the programme were upheld. the full community financing has been agreed. food distribution institutions are required to provide full information on the origin of the eu support. today's debate follows yesterday's debate on the plight of the homeless, many of whom also need free food. it's winter time. the crisis in our countries is felt most strongly by the poorest, who are the main beneficiaries of food aid under the programme. in total, almost 18 million europeans use the internet. these are the people who have the hardest to live with, the homeless, the unemployed, the elderly or the disabled, but also the large families and single parents. in europe, which has expanded so much, the number of poor and needy has increased dramatically. it is estimated that some 40 million people in europe are currently living in poverty, and another 40 million are at risk of poverty. this program has been very welcomed by charities, ngos that distribute food, but most importantly, it's about helping the poor, the people in need. it is good that the european union is remembering them. therefore, every effort should be made to prepare the appropriate legal basis for the implementation of this programme for the period 2014-2020.

mr. chairman, please! milk production is probably the most important sector in the whole of the common agricultural policy. we spend the largest part of the common agricultural policy funds on milk producers and processing. we should therefore be very careful to ensure that the dairy sector can continue to develop in a stable way. over the last several years, we've done a lot of things that have benefited the farmers, but also the consumers. the solutions proposed today are in some ways in line with the expectations of farmers and consumers alike. i would like, however, to see more attention paid in future work to the development of cooperatives and to the foundation of the sector on this type of management. it is good for the farmers themselves and good for the consumers. it is very important that the stability which has been eroded in this sector in recent years be restored to a certain standard, to a certain standard which would be valid for many years to come.
mr. chairman, please! the milk package is intended to improve the functioning of the milk market in the union after the end of quotas. this objective is to be achieved by strengthening the position of milk producers vis-à-vis processing plants and purchasers. it introduces the possibility of collective bargaining, the possibility of creating inter-branch organisations and is intended to improve transparency. but what i want to say here is that in practice, it is very often the case that supposedly better solutions turn out to be worse than the ones that exist today. it wasn't the quotas system that caused the crisis in 2009. the quotation is a proven instrument that gives producers guarantees and security. in other areas, like banking, we are proposing more oversight and regulation, and in the dairy sector we are moving towards liberalization. this will certainly not bring stability to our farmers and will encourage excessive concentration of production and the bankruptcy of many milk producers in the union.
in writing. in the light of the decision of the council of the european union to end the milk quota system, i would like to emphasise my position on the need to maintain the milk quota system after 2015. the commission notes that the measure is not intended to compensate for the additional costs of the milk levy. the annual increase in national milk quotas would therefore help to prepare the sector for the absence of restrictions on milk production. in this context, poland is prepared for such a situation both in terms of organisation and production potential. however, based on the experience of 2008, concerns remain regarding a renewed slump in demand on the milk market and the associated lack of disposal of milk surpluses. i would also like to point out that the date for the abolition of the milk quotas has been postponed in the past for a number of reasons. i therefore hope that more and more countries will join the position i represent, bearing in mind the situation of farmers and the desire to ensure that they are guaranteed a relatively stable environment.
mr. chairman, please! the european union is the world's largest importer of fishery products. given that this is an important source of food, particular attention should be paid to international agreements that compete with indigenous products. the common fisheries policy is of great importance for the environment, the recovery of resources and the fishing industry. the effect of sustainable development is that it is not competitive with products from countries outside the european union. the essence of the negotiations must therefore be, on the one hand, the defence of the interests of the member states in the context of the constraints imposed by the policies pursued and, on the other, the acceptance and observance of the rules by the third countries cooperating with the european union. it must be remembered that unthinking trade liberalization destroys the domestic market and, as a result, leads to uncontrolled, uncompetitive price increases for products.
in writing. the deepening of trade between the european union and the kingdom of morocco will certainly help the economic development of the country. however, the liberalisation of agricultural trade could have disastrous consequences for european agriculture. products from morocco do not meet many european standards in the fields of food safety, sanitation or environmental protection. the increase in imports of fruit and vegetables will cause a huge distortion of competition in this sector, which in times of economic crisis may even lead to the loss of jobs for many producers. it is necessary to strengthen the effectiveness of the community import control and security system, requiring moroccan producers to comply with the same standards as european producers.

in writing. the ongoing financial crisis has exposed the imperfections of the institutional architecture and economic governance of the euro area. this should be reflected not only in the protracted decision-making process and ineffective enforcement of fiscal discipline under the stability and growth pact, but also in the vulnerability to speculative attacks and asset price volatility in sovereign bond markets, which undermine the effectiveness of the common monetary policy. the initial proposal to introduce so-called stabilisation bonds, a form similar to common government bonds issued on behalf of all euro area countries, certainly deserves attention. the potential benefits of such a solution are the main reasons for further consideration. the use of a debt 'mutualization' formula can help to increase the efficiency, stability and resilience of the european sovereign bond market to sudden shocks. in times of heightened risk aversion, the single bond market will facilitate market access for the participating member states and increase the efficiency of the monetary transmission mechanism in the euro area. it should also be added that the effect of scale will reduce transaction costs and strengthen the role of the euro as an international reserve currency in the global financial market. however, a full examination of all the options and a sound assessment of the risks involved is necessary to assess objectively this proposal, the implementation of which has important implications for the global financial market and the future viability of the euro area.

in writing. the european union is experiencing the worst economic crisis since its inception. the rapid increase in unemployment, especially among young people, the collapse of industrial production and trade, and the need for considerable savings at the level of the member states of the community mean that the european parliament too must cut its expenditure. i therefore welcome the report, particularly the second point, which concerns greater integration of the institutions. the analyses show that such an action would reduce the expenditure of parliament on monthly transfers to strasbourg. in view of the deteriorating financial situation of the citizens of the union, i cannot understand the point of monthly transfers which cost around eur 280 million a year and lead to the emission of 20 000 tonnes of co2. we cannot ignore the opinions of citizens who in 2002 collected over 1.2 million signatures in favour of limiting the ep's seat to one city brussels. another important point in the report is the demand for a reduction in the eeas budget. as the practice of this institution shows, despite its considerable expenditure, it does not lead to an increase in the importance of the european union among our external partners. i therefore believe that the expenditure relating to the salaries and allowances of diplomats and the travel expenses of mrs catherine ashton should be reviewed.
in writing. i strongly support the motion for a resolution on petition 0924/2011 by dan pescod, on behalf of the european blind union (ebu) and the royal national institute of blind people (rnib), on access to books and other printed materials for blind people. we should be particularly sensitive to the needs of the millions of blind and partially sighted people in europe. these and other people with reading disabilities need access to publications in accessible formats such as large print, audio or braille. in today's world, especially in the face of the internet, access to information quickly and without additional barriers is in fact a guarantee of the full enjoyment of civil and social rights. the lack of access is in fact a restriction on the rights of citizens already affected by disability. access to cultural goods in the form of books, records and presses is one of the necessary conditions for the proper treatment of blind and partially sighted people and, above all, for their access to education at an appropriate level. we should do everything we can to ensure that the millions of blind and partially sighted people in europe have their fundamental right to read and to have access to books and publications.
in writing. for visually impaired people, the lack of access to books in accessible formats is a significant and difficult barrier to full integration into society. limited access to such publications for blind or partially sighted persons also limits their access to further knowledge, education and, consequently, to improving their position on the labour market. there is no doubt that all the institutions of the european union should support actions which will result in equal opportunities for disabled people and the fight against their social exclusion. i therefore believe that the draft treaty proposed by the world blind union, among others, requires very careful consideration and should not be blocked by the european union. the solutions proposed in the report facilitate the use of existing publications by visually impaired persons on the basis of cross-border exchange, thus preventing discrimination against blind and partially sighted persons.
