in writing. - mr president! - what are you doing? i hereby consent to the conclusion of an agreement on mutual legal assistance with norway and iceland. the unification of criminal procedure, also in relation to european countries outside the community, is in the interest of the security of citizens. the example of anders breivik shows that even in neighbouring countries with a stable political and economic situation, the threat of domestic terrorism is still possible. the investigation, in this particular case alone, required extensive cooperation from norway with other european countries, including poland. the agreement will, inter alia, allow for the interviewing of witnesses, experts and accused persons via videoconferencing, which will significantly improve the criminal procedure conducted by the police in different countries. i therefore look forward to closer cooperation in the fight against crime with the countries that are part of the schengen area.
in writing. − the basic idea of the 2000 convention on mutual assistance in criminal matters and the protocol annexed thereto is to enable member states to take action against persons in criminal proceedings in the territory of other member states and to enable those persons to participate actively in those proceedings in order to protect their interests or to assert their rights. these acts are therefore an essential element in shaping an area of freedom, security and justice. the convention and the protocol define the legal framework within which the competent authorities of the member states conducting the proceedings may operate; they lay down the procedural conditions and the conditions for their initiation. those tools increase the effectiveness of the enforcement of liability for infringements and consequently provide a higher guarantee of the rule of law and the protection of the interests of persons in the area covered by those regulations. they also facilitate the exercise of the right to a trial. extending their effectiveness to all member states and eu-aligned countries, as well as candidate countries, is a natural expression of acceptance of the common idea of an area of freedom, security and justice. the contract presented is the next formal step in its implementation. there is no question about its correctness.
in writing. − i am in favour of the consent procedure to conclude the agreement between the eu and iceland and norway on the application of certain provisions of the convention of 29 may 2000 on mutual assistance in criminal matters between the member states of the european union and the 2001 protocol. this is an important agreement since it is aimed at improving judicial cooperation between the eu member states and norway and iceland. i am confident that many of its provisions – such as those on hearing of witnesses, experts and accused persons by telephone or video conference, controlled deliveries, covert investigations and joint investigation teams and requests for information on banking transactions, bank accounts and their monitoring to combat translational and organised crime – will increase our security and have a positive impact on our efforts to fight crime.
in writing. − the increasing mobility of eu citizens means that they face many difficulties in exercising their inheritance rights abroad. the succession laws of the member states are very diverse and linked to local traditions, which makes cross-border proceedings extremely complex and incomprehensible for the parties. the eu has 27 different succession law systems and some 450 000 succession proceedings of an international nature are brought each year. it is important to create a single, transparent procedural system to make it easier for europeans to enforce their inheritance rights. the report on the regulation establishing common rules governing inheritance in the eu and the creation of a european certificate of succession is a very complex and ambitious project. it will not affect national legislation but will provide a facilitation for persons holding assets in more than one member state. statistics show that about 1.5% of the population of the member states of the union are citizens of other community countries; they will be able to decide, on the basis of the new rules, in which country their inheritance should be disposed of in the future. moreover, the introduction of a european certificate of succession, which will constitute proof of a specific status of heir recognised in all member states, will make it easier for the holder to enforce his rights, resulting in a shorter and less costly procedure. i congratulate the rapporteur and hope that these new legal mechanisms will facilitate a practice which often presents many problems with different procedures and formalities, which are associated with additional stress for citizens in such difficult times for them.
in writing. − cross-border inheritance issues have not been regulated at eu level, which has created many difficulties for those who inherit property. both substantive law and the rules on jurisdiction and applicable law vary considerably between member states, and i therefore welcome the european commission's proposal. issues such as the adoption of a broad definition of inheritance, a broad concept of court, the regulation of court jurisdiction and the introduction of a uniform statute of succession are important solutions that will facilitate cross-border inheritance. progress is also being made with the introduction of the recognition of documents of importance to succession matters and the institution of the european certificate of succession, which aims to speed up the examination of international succession cases. i welcome the report and am pleased that the commission has taken up most of the solutions proposed by parliament as early as 2006 in its resolution with recommendations to the commission on succession and wills. the proposal will give citizens in the european union a guarantee of clarity and legal certainty and a clear basis for the design of their inheritance. these rules will enable europeans to better enjoy their rights in the internal market. legal clarity and legal certainty are the most important elements that should be guaranteed in the field of succession law. the regulation strengthens these aspects, provides facilities for citizens and guarantees benefits for the european union.
in writing. - the ratio legis of the draft regulation is to remove all obstacles to the free movement of persons and their rights resulting from the particular differences in succession systems in the member states. the proposed regulations are intended to increase legal certainty for both the testator and the beneficiary. the regulation is intended to satisfy the model of a uniform status of succession, whereby a single succession, irrespective of the nature of the property and its location, is governed by a single legal regime, the law of the choice of the testator. this avoids the fragmentation of the estate and the difficulty of enforcing succession rights on the basis of different legal regulations. at the same time, it is necessary to consider whether the proposal submitted fully implements the declared possibility of securing assets in the event of death. the institutions of the choice of law for the settlement of succession matters in conjunction with the european certificate of succession undoubtedly allow such security. however, this is a formal aspect of the regulation, which is reduced to its incorporation into the legal system. he has great potential. however, it depends on the material aspect, which is the actual availability of the facilities to the beneficiaries. we need to think about how to popularize the behaviors we've described in these standards. that's the whole difficulty of design regulation. in addition to creating legal tools, the right people must be persuaded to use them.
in writing. − although i am aware of the obvious difficulties and legal uncertainties that this proposal aims to resolve (in terms of simplifying the legal position for citizens in europe by allowing the management of estates of deceased persons where these cover more than one member state to be based upon the law of only one jurisdiction), my abstention in the vote concerned is due to the fact that this regulation presents a certain difficulty which is, mainly, that due to the haste in which negotiations have been concluded in council and with parliament, concerns still exist with the solution found for the varying practices across the member states dealing with administration of the deceased’s estate.

in writing. − the treaty of lisbon gives parliament a co-legislating role in trade policy and its consent is necessary for any agreement to be concluded. in view of the changes which have taken place with the entry into force of the treaty, it is necessary to review and adapt all the procedures relevant to the common commercial policy in order to increase the efficiency and effectiveness of the common commercial policy. transparency of the commercial policy is a very important issue and is reflected in the proposal, as it aligns a number of regulations in the field of the common commercial policy with the new primary law provisions. the treaty of lisbon introduced a new instrument in the form of delegated acts, which allows legislative acts of minor importance to be transmitted to the executive. the parliament and the council play an important role here, as they retain the right to revoke or veto any decision taken in the context of the transmission of legislative acts. the treaty also provides for implementing acts which, together with delegated acts, replace the committee procedure. the introduction of these significant changes in the decision-making procedures for implementing measures urgently requires the adaptation of existing legal acts and i am therefore pleased that parliament has adopted today a report which will allow these innovative solutions to be introduced into the regulations in question on the common commercial policy.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the giovanni la via report because i fully support the rapporteur's view that the 2013 budget should be an instrument that, by supporting coordinated action, will allow us to return to the path of economic growth and to counter the effects of the crisis. i consider the greatest threat to the european union to be the alarming level of youth unemployment, which has already exceeded 20% and in some countries even 40%. moreover, unemployment is no longer limited to the low-skilled but is also affecting the most highly qualified. this situation has both an economic and a social dimension and is a threat to the future of europe's social capital. i therefore believe that emphasis should be placed on financing measures to improve the situation of young people rapidly and to create conditions favourable to the creation and development of small and medium-sized enterprises.
in writing. - i'd like to support the approval of the cocoa agreement. europe is dependent on imports of this product, and there is no possibility of growing it on the continent. it's not a necessity, either, which is why we can afford it. however, the conditions under which cocoa is harvested are disturbing. this is not about sanitation or quality issues, but about the practice of child labor. minors are working too hard for their abilities. not to mention that they do it instead of studying or playing, which is normal for their european peers. the possibility of changing this situation is not easy, but it is not impossible. importers could enforce the age of workers from their suppliers, control the plantations and make compliance with the rules a condition for further commercial cooperation. the european union is the guardian of human rights throughout the world. we must not forget that and we must protect the weakest.
in writing. − i have been involved in activities for people with diabetes in my region for many years. i am therefore all the more pleased that this rapidly growing problem has been brought to the attention of the european parliament. not only are many eu citizens affected by this disease, but the proportion of people at risk is also significant and increasing, which is why raising awareness about this disease is so important. we have to confront this problem, and we certainly need more innovative approaches to diabetes. it will be important to develop an appropriate diabetes strategy, taking into account early diagnosis and research in this area. it is necessary to analyse the data on the disease and the patients in order to understand the problem and be able to effectively address it or significantly minimise it. action will be needed not only by the union institutions but also, and above all, by the member states, in particular in the development of programmes for the prevention of diabetes. in addition, member states should take into account preventive measures to combat chronic diseases. diabetes should be recognised as a priority societal challenge and the strategy to combat this disease should be supported by appropriate funding.
in writing. - diabetes is an extremely insidious and chronic disease. it is estimated that half of those who have the disease are unaware of their condition, and it kills as many as three million people worldwide each year. diabetes, if left undiagnosed and untreated, is a leading cause of blindness, kidney failure, heart attacks, strokes, and amputations. so it cannot be dismissed as a disease that affects a small percentage of the population. i fully agree with the rapporteur that a comprehensive strategy for the prevention, early detection and mitigation of diabetes needs to be developed and implemented in the european union. we need to educate communities, which is now focused on providing information about infectious diseases. the most important thing is, of course, prevention and the provision of free prevention and diagnostic tests: blood sugar, blood pressure, body fat and body weight. a large-scale diabetes counselling programme will also be required. member states should implement comprehensive programmes aimed at raising awareness among eu citizens about the causes of the diabetes epidemic. poor diet, low-nutrient, high-calorie foods, sedentary work, overfeeding of children, and so forth are proving to be disastrous. but the cost of diabetes is very high.

in writing. - the dutch freedom party (pvv) initiative of 8 february has been the subject of much controversy. its highly negative, discriminatory nature is due to the possibility of sending anonymous complaints against citizens of central and eastern european countries who take up employment in the kingdom of the netherlands. the initiative is the party's aggressive populist platform, but the current minority government is dependent on its support in parliament and has entered into a cabinet-back agreement with it. the pvv initiative itself contradicts the constructive discussion on the migration of workers from the eea and does not address the underlying problems, including the prevalent practices of temporary employment agencies. there are appropriate institutions within the dutch administration which deal with all applications and complaints in an impartial manner, without focusing on a particular ethnic group. therefore, pvv's usurpation of the right to duplicate state structures is not justified! the netherlands benefits from the free movement of persons, goods and services within the european union. the pvv initiative reinforces the stereotypical image of polish workers in the netherlands, which is contradicted by the fact that the dutch economy receives tangible benefits from their work. i therefore look forward to concrete action by the eu institutions and to a public and critical statement by the dutch government on the pvv initiative, which would be an expression of its constructive attitude in developing bilateral relations with poland.
in writing. − in february in the netherlands, geert wilders' anti-immigrant group pvv launched an internet portal where complaints and grievances can be lodged about the behaviour of central and eastern european migrant workers, particularly poles. it's a very disturbing phenomenon. the creators of the portal claim that it is only a tool to prevent negative behaviors such as crime, alcoholism, drug abuse or trash dumping, which allegedly have increased since may 2007, when the netherlands opened its labor market to the new eu member states including poland. the portal strikes at one of the pillars of the eu, which is the free movement of people, is discriminatory because it is only directed at specific nations, and potentially dangerous because it encourages hostile behaviour and instills fear among the dutch population. dutch prime minister mark rutte declined to comment on the matter, saying the site was created as an expression of the position of a single political party with which the minority government is not in coalition on so-called european issues. europe is a place of freedom where every citizen should feel safe and equal, no matter where they live. openly inciting people to intolerance and mutual hatred on the basis of subjective comments posted on the portal pages is unacceptable in a free europe. i therefore call for concrete steps to be taken quickly to outlaw the existing portal and to prevent new initiatives like it from being created in the future.
in writing. - i voted for the resolution on discriminatory websites and government responses. i think the dutch government should strongly condemn the website founded by the party for freedom (pvv). the portal encourages the sending of complaints and reports on central and eastern european citizens living in the country. such actions are openly discriminatory. according to the resolution, the dutch authorities should investigate whether the invitation to submit complaints does not in fact incite hatred and discrimination. it is good that in the text of the resolution we have recognised that this party is in breach of the fundamental european values of human dignity, freedom and equality, and respect for the rule of law and human rights. the dutch government should not turn a blind eye to the populist maneuvers of the freedom party. they are contrary to the fundamental values of the european union. the resolution also calls on the european commission and the council to take a serious stance on the prevention of xenophobic attitudes such as those initiated by the dutch freedom party. both institutions should emphasise that the framework decision on combating racism and xenophobia is properly implemented in all member states.

on paper. turkey is an example of a successful economic transformation in the middle east. turkey's gdp growth rate, which has averaged over 6% per year since 2009, is impressive. in view of the eurozone crisis, the development gap between turkey and europe is therefore closing rapidly. according to the imf, in 2010, turkey's economy was the 16th largest in the world. the large advances in economic development are made possible by a favourable demographic profile and continuous productivity growth. turkey's strategic location at the junction of three continents - europe, africa and asia - plays a key role in stabilising this highly volatile region. as a member of nato, turkey is a very important partner for the eu in its efforts to create an area of stability and prosperity in its immediate neighbourhood. turkey's biggest shortcomings remain in the areas of democracy and human rights. the reforms introduced by prime minister erdogan's government seem to be mostly cosmetic and aimed at softening external criticism. the commission has also been active in promoting the rights of women and minorities. in addition, in the case of turkey, there is no real assessment of the past and many legal solutions adopted are not reflected in their implementation. without resolving turkey's historical disputes with its neighbors or its national minorities, it will be difficult to create a prosperous future.
in writing. turkey is a strong and important player in the international arena today. it is an essential part of the puzzle that gives the european community the prospect of energy independence. it is also an important economic partner and a market of 77 million for our products. for all its merits, turkey is still the country that did not condemn the first mass genocide in 20th century europe - the armenian genocide of 1915-1917. it's a very poor country, with a huge disparity between the western and eastern parts of the country. the state of media freedom is inadequate, as is the respect for human rights. the northern cyprus issue also remains unresolved. this is one of the reasons why turkey's accession to the european union seems totally unrealistic and illogical. it would be a failure of the community's pillars of human rights, the common market and cohesion policy. the eu and turkey must remain economic partners, and we should therefore seek to facilitate trade between the eu and turkey, to build joint infrastructure projects such as the nabucco pipeline, but still remain separate legal entities without the possibility or need for further integration.

solidarity and help them in practical and clear ways. the main eu instrument to support the employability and inclusion of the most vulnerable members of our societies will, of course, remain a strong european social fund. that is why the commission proposed a guaranteed minimum budget for the esf representing at least 25% of cohesion policy and that at least 20% of the funding for each member state should be allocated to social inclusion measures. we also proposed that the european globalisation adjustment fund be maintained and strengthened as a way to show real solidarity with newly unemployed workers in particularly difficult circumstances. in the commission’s view, a programme to assist the most deprived people in europe should form part of these efforts. the harsh reality is that there will always be people in our societies in need of a programme of this kind and that is why the commission’s proposal for the multiannual financial framework seeks to allow the eu budget to realistic. let me close by thanking parliament for its very helpful contribution to our work and for raising this point for debate.

in writing. one of the three priorities of the europe 2020 strategy is inclusive development. the number of people at risk of poverty is to be reduced by 20 million by 2020. it will be difficult to achieve this goal by ending the food distribution program for those in need. the european commission has launched a new programme to support the development of the european audiovisual industry. its value will be eur 500 million per year until at least 2013. we have a very well-run programme in our country to help the poor, with 20,000 volunteers, 7,000 ngos, food banks, caritas. the number of people in need in poland is large. in poland, 2 million people are still living in conditions that allow them to satisfy only the most basic needs, and 5 million are living in very difficult living conditions. today, 4 million people in poland are benefiting from the food aid programme. they receive food products, including flour, porridge, and canned goods. in 2011, there were 21 product types. it should be noted that the food aid programme is profitable in several areas. in addition to supporting people at risk of poverty and social exclusion, it is an important component of farmers' and agri-food sector's income, and eu food aid for those in need should therefore be maintained.
in writing. the europe 2020 strategy rightly recognises that reducing the number of poor and socially excluded people is one of the union's development priorities. it is estimated that by 2020 the number of people at risk of poverty will be reduced by 20 million. i believe that it is important in this context to maintain and finance food distribution in the union to those in need. the eu budget currently allocates eur 500 million per year to this purpose, benefiting 18 million people. the main beneficiaries of this programme are the people of poland, where 4 million people receive aid in the form of free food products. these are as basic as porridge, flour, or canned goods. in poland, more than 20,000 volunteers and many non-governmental organisations are involved in the programme to help the poor. it should be noted that the implementation of the union programme not only means concrete, tangible support for many poor people, but is also important for agricultural producers, farmers' incomes and agri-food processing enterprises. all of this is a reason for the union to maintain and finance this programme from its budget.

on behalf of the s&d group. the report on removing obstacles to citizens' rights in the european union, published by the european commission in october 2010, focuses on the 25 biggest problems citizens face when exercising their rights in a cross-border context, identified through an analysis of 300 petitions from the last 3 years. the most common difficulties faced by citizens are caused by complex legislation, excessive bureaucracy, poor law enforcement and a simple lack of goodwill on the part of the authorities of the country concerned. in recent years, we have seen an increasing number of problems with the right to free movement - 25% of all petitions. it is important that every citizen of the union in another member state feels secure, knows his or her rights and is not exposed to any discrimination on grounds of race, nationality, religion or sexual orientation. i congratulate the rapporteur on a good and useful report which i hope will have a positive impact on the situation of the people of our common european home.

madam president! serbia has made tremendous progress, which we have highlighted in this report. i voted in favour of it because i believe that serbia has a place among the member states of the european union. at the same time, i also welcomed the granting of candidate status to serbia for accession to the european union. this decision will strengthen the efforts of all those behind this choice. i would also like to mention a personal moment of mine when i was an observer on behalf of the council of europe in the constitutional referendum. at that time - a few years ago - many young serbs did not believe that the european perspective was open to them. we tried to convince them that. it seems to me that today's report and the granting of the status of a candidate country to the union is precisely the answer to their earlier doubts. i am deeply convinced that their efforts will not be in vain and that in time we will be able to accept them as members of the european union. i wish them well.
madam president! i have a great problem with voting on the so-called enlargement of the european union with kosovo, because i believe that kosovo will be in the european union as serbia will be in the european union, because i do not recognize and i do not find in my conscience any argument for this terrible violation that has been committed against the serbian people through the forced and supported internationally by unfortunately a part of the countries, a large part of the countries, the european union, the secession of this serbian province from its homeland. i want to say that today kosovo is not just a hotbed of organized crime, but also a place where the persecution of ethnic serbs living there is taking place, as well as the persecution of religious orthodox, for whom this land means a lot. so i want to express my absolute conviction that kosovo is part of serbia and as part of serbia it should be in the european union.
madam president! i have one, actually two problems with turkey. i have no problem with turkey's membership of the european union, provided that the problem is solved, which i believe is a clear violation of european solidarity: how can we propose membership of turkey in the european union when it supports the occupation of the sovereign territory of one of the members of the european union, namely cyprus? on the other hand, turkey still has huge problems with the implementation of the rights of national and religious minorities. on the one hand, we have a big kurdish problem, and on the other hand, there is still persecution of christians in turkey. without the resolution of the two problems i have mentioned, namely the occupation of cyprus and the problem of national and religious minorities, there can be no question of turkey's membership of the european union.
madam president! the balkans need to be stabilized. the european union has undoubtedly been expanding everywhere since its inception in western europe. it has been a zone of virtually unbroken development since then. although we are in crisis today, it has nevertheless been a zone of unbroken development and above all of peace. it seems that the balkans also need the development and peace that the european union brings wherever it operates. while appreciating the successes, despite the many difficulties, that have been achieved in the republic of montenegro in the fight against corruption, in simply introducing better governance, i support and endorse this report.
madam president! while i fully support women's access to politics and the professions, i too always have doubts whether quota solutions, if in some sense force, are trying to achieve this legitimate postulate that all sexes are treated equally. the history of our civilization shows that wherever we try to do some kind of social engineering, very often we get the opposite of the intended effect. that is why i voted against this principle. i supported this report despite my initial fears that it would lead to excessive regulation and bureaucratic interference in business and i think that this type of interference is not good. i think this report is a good compromise and that is why i voted for it.
madam president! i abstained on this report, although i very much appreciate the success of the european investment bank's work so far. however, in my view, the main criteria for assessing the bank's performance should be economic criteria, economic criteria, because banks - and i think this should be the case - are supposed to make money by granting loans, but also, in the case of a bank like the european investment bank, simply to promote economic development on our continent. i'm against imposing on banks, or on business in general, even the most ideologically sound solutions. i lived 18 years of my life in a country where economics didn't matter, but ideology did, and the poles and many other middle class and european people learned firsthand that it's very bad when ideology replaces economics.
madam president! i had a big problem with that report. on the one hand, there are things in it that cannot be dismissed. in general, the very fact that we are dealing with civil rights in the european union is something to be respected. but i voted against the report because i think that too often, alongside the absolutely right things, we are also dealing with things in it that i do not even want to judge whether they are right or wrong, but should be the exclusive competence of the nation states. it is dangerous and unfortunate for me that the level of harmonization of our development paths within the countries of the european union should be greater than in the united states, where individual states seem to have more freedom in certain matters than this parliament would like to impose on the member states of the european union.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because it will help to harmonise the law in this area. passenger rights are currently governed by regulation (ec) no 261/2004 and regulation (ec) no 1107/2006, as well as by the judgments of the court of justice of the eu in this context. our aim is to achieve the greatest possible transparency of the binding rules and to strengthen the rights of air passengers. common rules on compensation and assistance to passengers in the event of denied boarding or cancellation or long delay of flights are essential to ensure that passengers using air transport in the union are adequately insured and that their rights are respected. i am therefore convinced that further action in this direction will contribute to ensuring the rights of air passengers.
in writing. − given that an increasing number of european union citizens place a high value on their mobility, both for work and for leisure, it is of the utmost importance from our point of view to ensure the highest possible quality of travel. the air route is of great interest to our citizens because of its significantly shorter travel time and convenience. it is therefore essential to ensure the full range of travellers' rights. the european parliament has already introduced a set of rules to protect air travellers through its legislative powers. as we know, airlines often exploit loopholes in the law by manipulating the final ticket prices. as i, too, as a traveller, believe that everyone has a right to fair treatment on a paid air ticket, i will always support such proposals and i voted for the report again.
in writing. − i have decided to vote in favour of the report on the review of two regulations: establishing common rules on compensation and assistance to passengers in the event of denied boarding, cancellation or delay of flights and on the rights of disabled persons and persons with reduced mobility travelling by air. in view of the ever-increasing number of people travelling by air, it is urgent to adopt regulations to better protect passengers' rights. the report therefore calls for more transparency and clarity in passenger rights information at all key stages of the journey. passengers should be able to correct obvious errors made when placing an order or even to cancel their ticket altogether within two hours of purchase. the commission should also be able to provide information on the progress of the implementation of the schengen acquis, in particular on the progress of the implementation of the schengen acquis and the progress of the union's external action. in addition, the airlines must be obliged to deal with all passenger complaints within a maximum of two months. the european commission should also set up a central website with information on passenger rights available in all official languages of the european union. i am convinced that the implementation of the recommendations contained in the report adopted will contribute to improving the situation at airports.
in writing. - i am pleased to have adopted the document for which i was the shadow rapporteur for the ppe group. during this review, we had the opportunity to draw the attention of the european commission to a number of irregularities at european airports. we want the new commission proposals to address these problems. we should make air travel better, safer and cheaper for all passengers travelling in europe. the most important points for passengers are the possibility to correct obvious errors in ordering or even to cancel a ticket within two hours of purchase, the prohibition of airlines charging unnecessary fees for credit card purchases and the enforcement of the rights of parents travelling with small children. i believe that the european commission will be sympathetic to parliament's proposal.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because administrative cooperation in the field of excise duties can help to combat tax fraud in the european union. my task is to ensure that such actions are of great importance to the european economy and thus to the citizens of the union. the prevention of tax fraud can have a positive impact on the state of citizens' wallets in the long term. cooperation between member states is necessary and desirable in this respect. moreover, the pursuit of a well-functioning fiscal union within the european union contributes to the equalization of disparities in commodity prices and thus to the improvement of the well-being of all union citizens.
in writing. - i voted in favour of another important step towards a single seat for the european parliament, joining the majority of my fellow members. this is another step towards eliminating the costly problem of the three seats of the european parliament. the initiative now rests with the council, the governments of the member states. it is high time to start renegotiating the treaties, which will allow us to focus on the abolition of two of the three seats of the european parliament. in times of crisis and widespread budget cuts, this is all the more necessary. neither the citizens nor the meps accept the current situation. it is time for the leaders of the member states to become intolerable too.
in writing. −we had a discussion on the european parliament's budget for 2013. the european parliament's expenditure is forecast to reach eur 1.759 billion, an increase of 1.9% compared with 2012. the vast majority of this expenditure concerns parliament's staff, which will be 6,713, and the maintenance of the ep's buildings in brussels, strasbourg and luxembourg. i think there are ways of reducing this budget and looking more radically for savings. first, the leadership of parliament and the council of the union should limit the seat of parliament to a single place where not only members but also officials can be gathered. the current situation generates additional costs of several hundred million dollars a year and is unsustainable. secondly, i cannot understand why, with the scale of the movement of mps and officials - tens of thousands of flights a year - parliament cannot negotiate airline fares for the biggest european carriers. we pay more for tickets than we do for tickets purchased individually, like online. i think that needs to be changed radically.
in writing. the lisbon treaty establishes a new institutional balance. it is based, among other things, on the assumption of the parity of parliament and the council in the legislative and budgetary functions. the logical consequence of such a regulation is the need to bring the ep's rules of procedure into line with the treaties. there is no doubt that it is necessary to exclude from the existing powers of parliament the possibility of addressing questions to the council which relate to those functions, since the institutions are equal in those fields and work closely together. the procedure for successive readings and the submission of amendments is a de facto mechanism replacing and reinforcing the 'control' questions to the council. the continued operation of these provisions would be an unnecessary duplication of legal institutions. the proposed amendment also leaves parliament with the power to ask specific questions to the council concerning its other functions, namely policy-making and coordination. it's the right thing to do. it protects parliament against excessive council arbitrariness in this respect. it strengthens the democratic control of the council by an institution that is the expression of the will of the eu's citizens. in view of the need to democratise the eu, an important element of which is the strengthening of the institutional position of the parliament, such amendments should be adopted.
in writing. − this is not the first time we have discussed human rights violations in belarus. the repressive measures imposed by president lukashenko’s government on the people of belarus were the subject of the last five resolutions we adopted on the country. last month we debated the trial and verdict of mr dzmitry kanavalau and mr uladzislau kavalyou, two men who were dubiously found guilty in the terrorist attacks of 2005 in vitebsk, and 2008 and 2010 bomb attacks in minsk. these men are two victims of the oppressive regime, but sadly not the only ones. belarus is today the only country in europe that still carries out the death penalty. its active prosecution of political opposition, civil society, the media and human rights defenders further contributes to the country’s isolation. we prefer diplomacy over sanctions, thus the eu is ready to use the assistance and cooperation tools available to negotiate with belarus. but we are also ready to maintain sanctions imposed on belarusian officials and on companies that directly finance the regime, and further extend them if our calls remain unanswered. the current resolution confirms our commitment to the belarusian people, as well as our affirmative approach towards the government, therefore i voted in support of it.
in writing. - i consider the vote on the resolution on the situation in belarus to be one of the most important of the day. i supported the joint motion for a resolution that was postponed two weeks ago. for reasons i cannot understand, my colleagues from the s&d and ppe groups postponed the vote, considering that the regime of alexander lukashenko should be given time to change its policy. the two boys accused of the attack on the minsk metro were executed the day after the plenary session. i therefore considered it extremely important to support the resolution which calls for the relocation of the world cup of hockey from belarus, the release and rehabilitation of political prisoners and respect for human rights, and condemns the expulsion of eu and polish ambassadors from belarus.
in writing. − there can be no progress in the eu-belarus dialogue unless minsk makes progress on democracy, human rights and the rule of law, and unconditionally releases all political prisoners. the deteriorating situation of human rights and fundamental freedoms in this country must change. unfortunately, despite the territorial proximity, the european union and belarus share a wide gap in political and social standards in many areas. the persecution of human rights defenders and members of the democratic opposition, and the politically motivated harassment of civil society activists and independent media in belarus, shows us that cooperation is impossible, despite our deepest desires. how can you work with someone who just doesn't want to work with you? today's resolution is a democratic and peaceful expression of our views. it is therefore important to make clear our disapproval of any acts that violate fundamental values. the strong cooperation between the 27 eu countries and non-eu countries is a solid basis for promoting these values. and through our engagement, we can achieve the goal of starting the process of democratization in belarus.
in writing. − the polish presidency was actively involved in the idea of establishing a european endowment for democracy. such action by an institution independent of eu diplomacy seems to be highly desirable, especially in the face of the increasingly rapid changes in the community's neighbourhood. i consider the creation of a new fund to be a more effective measure than making changes to existing programmes. experience shows that parliament's involvement is conducive to similar initiatives, and that it is therefore a good idea to involve meps in the work of the governing council. this will also guarantee a voice for all member states. by voting in favour of this report, i am voting in favour of democratic change in countries around the world. through the fund, we will be able to support specific associations and groups playing key roles in the political transformation processes in their countries. it will also be an excellent instrument for sharing european experience in this field.
in writing. − the european endowment for democracy (eed) will be a key institution for europe's contribution to the democratisation of authoritarian states, both in the immediate neighbourhood of the union and around the world. the report adopted today gives the rapporteur, mr alexander lambsdorf, to whom i extend my warmest congratulations, a strong negotiating mandate in the work of the edf working party chaired by the european external action service. the edf should be a fund that works closely with the eu but is independent. the edf should have an expert structure allowing for a rapid and flexible response. it is intended to serve the building of civil society and the political capacity of the democratic opposition before and during the transition from authoritarianism to democracy. therefore, the edf should also support unregistered opposition circles, which are often not recognized and opposed by non-democratic states. the lack of such an instrument was exposed by the events of the arab spring, when it became clear that the only strong opposition political players in the countries of the region are religious groups. in the eastern dimension, the opposition in belarus, for example, needs significant assistance. i wanted to remind you that the eed is a proposal of the polish ministry of foreign affairs. the idea of establishing the eed was based on poland's experience of democratic transformation. thanks to western financial support, polish solidarity and other opposition groups - not recognized by the communist regime, formally non-existent - were able to develop and fight for democratic change. we should give others the same chance now.
in writing. − the creation of the european endowment for democracy was an initiative of the polish minister for foreign affairs and one of the main priorities of the polish presidency. i am pleased with the progress made in its creation and implementation. i supported the report on this fund because i believe that the recommendations contained therein will be of particular value to the council. parliament must have a guaranteed influence on the fund from the planning phase to the possibility of bringing it to justice. as vice-president of the committee on budgetary control, i place particular emphasis on 'designing' the instrument with full respect for the division of budgetary responsibilities. like other eu institutions, the fund should be obliged to submit annual reports to parliament and to publish a list of its beneficiaries. this will facilitate transparent financial administration.
in writing. −the unilateral declaration of independence of kosovo was a violation of all international rules, and i cannot therefore agree with the provisions proposed in the introduction to the report. today's kosovo is a parapality that is still a bone of contention between serbs and albanians. we cannot accept further integration of the balkans without dealing with this issue and without listening to the arguments of the serbian side. the central government is unable to maintain order within the borders of the state, and the spread of crime, especially organ trafficking, is a threat to the european union. the first thing we should do is to solve the problems and stabilise the situation, not to integrate the balkans without regard for the consequences.
in writing. - turkey remains a strategic partner of the west in both security and the economy. as a member of nato for 60 years, it has worked together for stability and peace. it is also an important access channel to the caucasus and caspian liquid fuel deposits and the planned nabucco gas pipeline is a key element of the union's energy security. the economic potential of this country determines the development of the entire region. although the neighbourhood policy is mutually beneficial, turkey remains the only candidate not to benefit from visa facilitation. i believe that it is in the interest of the whole union to extend this programme. last year's parliamentary elections showed ankara's ability to emerge as a democratic power based on the participation of the vast majority of the population. the integration drive was expressed in the creation of a ministry for eu affairs. i welcome all the measures taken to protect religious minorities, especially christians. cooperation with turkey is an important pillar of europe's security strategy. i support the resolution.
in writing. − promoting the development of the single market, reducing disparities between regions and supporting projects that contribute to the achievement of european union policy objectives are important objectives of the european investment bank. the approved business plan for the bank for the coming years identifies three main areas: the implementation of the europe 2020 strategy, the fight against climate change and the support of the european union's external policy. these issues should be the focus of the bank's most active strategies and activities, which should focus primarily on being a 'european bank'. the prolonged crisis and the associated credit constraints have a strong impact on the demand for funds to finance modern development and job creation. without adequate funding, the objectives of the europe 2020 strategy for smart, sustainable and inclusive growth will be difficult to achieve. the bank's capital needs are therefore not limited to the capital needs of the bank, but also to the capital needs of the bank. it is also worth looking at the issue of small and medium-sized enterprises. the current eu policy emphasises their important role in job creation. supporting the sme sector is crucial to the recovery of the european economy. finally, it is worth considering the report's considerations as to whether the european union should become the next shareholder of the european investment bank, alongside the member states, which could result in enhanced cooperation between the bank and the commission.
in writing. − for years, there have been calls for the eu to become more democratic, with a citizen element to be added to ever closer economic cooperation. the next stage was the lisbon reform, which clarified the concept of 'european union citizenship' and established an open catalogue of the rights deriving from it. given that the introduction of amendments to the treaties is only the beginning of the 'opening up of the union' to citizens, the institutions face the important task of creating legal arrangements to enable the treaties to be implemented. the commission's report summarises one year of these activities. it identifies 25 basic obstacles to the exercise of civil liberties and rights. it is important to stress that the lack of exercise of citizens' rights results in a situation where citizens do not fully enjoy the freedoms of movement and the benefits of the 'european project'. the report identifies the obstacles and sets out the actions that the commission should take to remove them. the commission and the rapporteur agree that the main reasons for this are the low level of awareness among eu citizens in the member states and the insufficient enforcement of existing rules, especially those resulting from directives. the lack of legal form seems to be a secondary factor, although this does not mean that it is invalid. the proposed actions, such as the creation of information points, the launch of the e-justice portal and the adoption of subsidiary legislation on family and succession law, are appropriate ways of addressing the problems discussed. the resolution must be unanimously supported.
in writing. - we are all citizens of the european union. there is no doubt about that in the field of declarations. the problems arise when we come to concrete, detailed solutions. the citizenship report is a very good guide to the main problems faced by union citizens in countries of which they are not nationals. the report also contains a number of important recommendations for the commission and the member states, the implementation of which will contribute to the more complete implementation of the principle of free movement of persons. all of this has led me to support this report. at the same time, i would like to take this opportunity to appeal to the polish government to fully ratify the charter of fundamental rights, that is to say to withdraw from the so-called british protocol to the treaty of lisbon. only this will ensure that polish citizens can fully exercise their rights in poland and throughout the european union.
in writing. - i supported the eu citizenship report 2010. it has been 20 years since the creation of citizenship of the union. today, we can enjoy, among other things, seamless border crossings, cheaper telephone calls, study, work and live in another member state. however, eu citizens still face difficulties abroad when exercising their rights, and these have to be overcome. a large number of complaints concern matters relating to access to social security benefits. in addition, 48% of eu citizens feel that they are not sufficiently informed about their rights. eu institutions must focus on better, appropriately funded communication with citizens and member states at local and national level in their efforts to strengthen eu citizenship. it is necessary to promote online information points, such as 'your europe', information and problem-solving networks set up by the commission, such as direct, solvit, european consumer centres. the new eu portal 'e-justice' is also a valuable compendium of information on legal mechanisms in the member states. the year 2013 has been declared the european year of citizens. this is the right time to inform european citizens of their rights, especially the new ones resulting from the entry into force of the lisbon treaty. i also draw attention to the promotion of the european citizens' initiative, which will give citizens the opportunity to be actively involved in shaping european policies and european legislation.
in writing. − citizens often face obstacles in their daily lives in a united europe. these include healthcare formalities or simply the registration of a car. the european union should help to eliminate the problems involved. in addition, eu citizens are often unaware of their rights when they are outside their country of residence or of the laws on basic consumer protection rights. as a result, they are not satisfied as consumers. the current rules on consumer protection should be adapted or, for example, a so-called common set of rights for travellers should be provided. in some eu countries, eu law is not applied properly to the right to free movement within the union, and burdensome administrative procedures are being created by some countries in contravention of eu law. other important obstacles to working in another member state are the existence of different social security systems and insufficient cooperation between national social security institutions. eu rules on the free movement of persons and the dissemination of information among union citizens should therefore be strictly respected.
vice-president of the commission/high representative of the union for foreign affairs and security policy. − madam president, since 1983, when the european parliament began adopting an annual report and resolution on human rights, this house has done more than any eu institution to focus on such issues. while we may sometimes disagree about how best to champion respect for human rights globally, we stand united in our aim: to see a freer world, where people’s dignity is respected – wherever they may be from – and for the eu, and the external action service in particular, to play a key role in supporting people’s struggles for their rights. allow me now to turn to the report by richard howitt which is before us today. first of all, i want to congratulate him for achieving consensus across the political spectrum on this report. i believe it is essential reading for me, my colleagues in the commission and my colleagues in the council. the very first paragraph of the report is about coherence between the internal and external policies of the european union – one of the main themes from the communication of december. it is a particularly important theme for parliament this week, since on thursday it will hear statements from the council and the commission on the european union’s accession to the european convention on human rights. honourable members, ‘coherence’ might sound dry, but this really does mean that human rights can be woven into everything we do, in europe and beyond. it means making sure that people everywhere benefit from the same universal rights, regardless of who they are or where they live. the report also highlights the importance of accountability and the importance of our work in developing, in serious situations, the accountability that we have. i will pick out two themes that in a sense are very important both for coherence and accountability. firstly, the role of women, especially as yesterday i met michelle bachelet to talk about the role of women and to sign agreements with un women on how to go forward and support women across the world. secondly – especially at the present time – discrimination against people of faith, including christians, and those who have other beliefs. tolerance is at the heart of the european union, and that is why we need to strengthen our policy on the freedom of religion or belief, which is fundamental to a free society. the european union must work continuously for the widest possible ratification, acceptance and approval of, and accession to, the rome statute. that work is progressing. so far, we have signed three bilateral agreements, including icc clauses, and initialled another three, and we are negotiating another 15. we have also included icc clauses in many of our enp action plans. we have the power to promote human rights by placing countries and regimes on a scale stretching between engagement and isolation and using human rights as a method of measuring how we should address our relationships with different countries. human rights have never been more important than they are now, nor indeed have they ever driven so many changes. if we simply look, for example, at what is happening throughout the middle east and north africa, men and women, young and old, representing the whole of society, have found the courage to assert their fundamental human rights. some have been prepared to give their lives for freedom, dignity and a better future. i should like to pay tribute to all of them now. the changes that they have brought, as mr howitt has said, required the eu to develop a new response to a changing neighbourhood. i believe we have risen to that challenge. human rights and deep democracy are at the heart of our new approach, and i believe our partnerships with our neighbours are stronger and healthier as a result. our work at the un human rights council has also helped to reinforce and support these positive and domestically-driven developments. at the 19th session, which concluded on 28 march, the european union resolution on syria was adopted with a record vote of 41 in favour, out of a possible 47. our resolution on human rights in burma/myanmar was adopted by consensus, as was the resolution on freedom of religion or belief. the session was a success for the rights of individuals, who too often find themselves marginalised and ostracised. the successful panel on ‘violence and discrimination based on sexual orientation and gender identity’ was a remarkable achievement, for which all credit is due to south africa’s leadership, together with ban ki-moon. it is unacceptable that 80 states still criminalise same-sex relations between consenting adults, and that seven even foresee the death penalty. this is totally incompatible with international human rights law. i believe it is very, very important that barbara lochbihler and laima andrikienė were able to attend the human rights council, where they addressed eu heads of mission and met with a wide range of international representatives. this is just another example of the important role of the european parliament and the important way in which it is seen to promote human rights in the world. my communication of last december was designed as a contribution to what is an ongoing discussion within and between eu institutions on a more effective and comprehensive approach to human rights and democracy. now that there has been time to consider what i put forward, i look forward to working with you on the shape of our future strategy. as i confirmed to the committee on foreign affairs on 20 march, work is in hand to pave the way for the appointment of a special representative for human rights as part of a package to put into practice the joint communication. it is important that this person be someone with a strong track record on international human rights. at the same time, as was discussed at the ‘gymnich’ meeting of foreign ministers, we want to agree a political declaration on what we want to achieve, and we want an action plan on how to put this into practice. this will bring together new initiatives as well as others that we have already launched. i am happy to confirm that the network of human rights focal points is nearly complete: 116 eu delegations now have someone, and many have two, in both their political and cooperation sections. on all of this, i want to work closely with the honourable members. the review of eu human rights policy was first announced in this house. the appointment of a special representative was championed by this house. it is therefore natural that ongoing work on human rights and democracy should be in full cooperation with this house. i have written to the chair of the human rights sub-committee to ask her to work with me to ensure the fullest possible participation in the drafting of the joint declaration. to end as i began, i pay tribute to mr howitt for his work and i pay tribute to the european parliament for its continuous work in support of human rights.

on behalf of the ecr group. madam high representative, ladies and gentlemen! this year's report on human rights in the world is a clear step forward in some areas compared to previous documents. this is especially true of the way in which religious freedom is viewed. religious freedom is an inalienable human right, its fundamental character being reaffirmed in the un and council of europe conventions. the widespread violation of this right, especially among christians, is a dramatic violation of human rights in the world. one year after the arab spring, we can speak of increasingly real threats to entire christian communities in the middle east. we must constantly remind our political partners in the region of this. it would be tragic if christians were the first victims of the democratization that is so desired in this part of the world. we find it difficult to agree with the criticism of france and the united kingdom on the accession of the european union to the european convention on human rights. this operation threatens to create a clear conflict of jurisdiction between the luxembourg and strasbourg courts, and could lead to an uncontrolled expansion of the jurisdiction of the european tribunals. the report should be free of any reference to so-called reproductive health. these records are a pretext for promoting and funding abortion worldwide, even in countries where the practice is illegal. this is a huge abuse of the trust of citizens and member states, who have never given the european commission such powers.

in writing. – human rights, democracy and the rule of law are core values of the eu and its founding treaties. the union’s commitment to supporting democracy and human rights in its external policies is affirmed by the eur 1.1 billion committed to the european instrument for democracy and human rights (2007-2013). while the eu’s contribution is certainly important, so is our interest to ensure that tax-payers’ money properly serves citizens of recipient countries and the eu’s interests and values. our past experience shows that eu funds allocated to this purpose, in many cases, have yielded limited results for various reasons concerning time and effectiveness of the instruments used. with this in mind i welcome the review and analysis of the union’s policy on related matters, as presented in the eu’s annual report on human rights and democracy. one desirable outcome from the annual report would be the formation of a common eu strategy on human rights with clear definitions of the actions, timetables and responsibilities of each of the european institutions. such a strategy will certainly point the way forward to setting and attaining ambitious goals while holding the eu and recipient countries to greater accountability on the usage of funds and the results accomplished.
in writing. in line with the eu's core values, the european parliament promotes human rights in an international arena that is clearly facing new challenges in a changing world. parliament called for the inclusion of human rights and conditionality clauses in eu-supported programmes, and called on eu member states to fully engage in this process and to apply its results in national action as well as at european level. in this context, the eu's priority is to support and actively involve governments, parliaments and civil society in the process of respecting and monitoring human rights. the key is to learn from past mistakes and to move swiftly, transparently and in an inclusive manner towards an ambitious final eu common strategy with clear actions, timeframes and targets, developed with the full involvement of stakeholders, to make a positive contribution to this interinstitutional process. this process should culminate in the adoption by the institutions of a common strategy and a framework which clearly defines the roles and tasks of each institution and provides a framework for continuously assessing their implementation.

in writing. the european union rightly considers respect for human rights in the world to be one of its most important tasks. i do not want to talk about the union's activities in this area, but i do want to point out the problems that are emerging. the first problem is that the union is actively involved in this area in its contacts with small and medium-sized countries. it's much more restrained when it comes to big countries. secondly, despite the establishment of the european external action service, there are still problems in coordinating the policies of all the eu institutions. the union's representations in individual countries, including diplomats specialised in human rights, should play a key role in this area, liaising not only with local authorities but also with opposition representatives and activists fighting for the protection of fundamental human rights. thirdly, the union should support, through its scholarship and research programmes, those scientists, journalists and students who want to devote themselves to the protection of human rights.

the next item is the debate on:- report by marianne thyssen, on behalf of the committee on economic and monetary affairs, on the proposal for a council directive on a common consolidated corporate tax base (com (2011) 0121 - c7-0092/2011 - 2011/0058 (cns)) (a7-0080/2012).
in writing. no one doubts the importance of solutions that help boost growth and jobs in europe in times of crisis. the idea of introducing common european rules for the calculation of the tax base of companies operating in the european union is a solution that would undoubtedly contribute to improving the competitiveness of the european market, reducing the administrative burden and the costs associated with complying with the various national tax regimes. unfortunately, the draft directive on the common consolidated tax base, in addition to good and fair solutions, also introduces provisions which, especially in times of crisis, we should not accept. the idea is to allow the consolidation of profits and losses within a group of companies, which will result in a drop in tax revenues in many member states and divide europe into 'winners' and 'losers'". this solution interferes too far with the tax systems of the member states and the possible compensation of losses by raising tax rates threatens tax competition in the internal market. instead of creating rules that go against the principle of solidarity and favour certain member states, we should encourage countries to define a common tax base as soon as possible, as some member states have committed to do under the euro plus pact.' it is one of the revenue-neutral ways of ensuring the coherence of national tax systems while respecting national tax strategies.
in writing. the project to create a single basis for taxing cit throughout the european union is ambitious and necessary. the commission has also proposed a new tax on the use of energy from renewable sources, which is ambitious because the legislation of eu countries on this tax differs significantly not only technically but also in the level of detail and economic priorities of the countries concerned reflected in this tax. this is a necessary step, as it will save significantly on the costs of cross-border activities and will make it easier for companies to operate. however, the idea of introducing revenue consolidation is no longer clearly positive. at least not for all countries. the formula for the division results in a group of 'winners and losers', i.e. those whose budgetary revenues will increase and those whose revenues will decrease after the introduction of this solution. this makes it extremely difficult to reach a compromise that satisfies all parties, and even if it is reached, it may have a negative impact on relations between countries. i therefore believe that the creation of a single tax base should be a priority and the idea of consolidation should be abandoned. this would be a much more advantageous solution as it would accelerate the process of building the common market without undue delay, especially in the context of the fact that there is a broad consensus, in the form of the euro plus pact, to undertake such action.

rapporteur. − mr president, commissioner, dear colleagues, over the last two and a half years, i have started most of my statements in this house by saying that europe needs growth, and once again i say it today. austerity packages in those economies most strongly affected by the crisis have not generated growth because of a dysfunctional banking sector and high risk-aversion. therefore, there is an urgent need to unlock eib loans and guarantees to enable the private sector to become involved in important growth and job-creating projects, especially those co-financed by the eu cohesion policy. in this context, mobilising all the potential resources that can become growth triggers requires special measures, and this is what this legislative proposal is about. it provides for the establishment of a risk-sharing instrument with a view to facilitating the absorption of the european regional development fund and the cohesion fund resources allocated to member states covered by eu and imf financial assistance programmes. in these countries – and primarily in greece – there are infrastructure and productive investment projects whose implementation has been blocked by the lack of private co-financing. this is particularly the case with transport and environmental infrastructure projects which generate revenue from the collection of charges from users and whose value cannot be covered by grants financed through the cohesion policy. this is also the case with those productive investments for which the maximum allowable public aid is capped by state aid rules. these projects are at risk of not being implemented because private sector investors and banks either lack the liquidity to lend to projects and project promoters or are no longer willing to bear the risks of investing in the present circumstances. the measure also foresees the possibility of financing other projects which are not co-financed by cohesion policy programmes but which contribute to the achievement of the objectives of cohesion policy and bring important added value to the union’s strategy for smart, sustainable and inclusive growth. the proposed measure will be implemented by the commission at the request of the member state concerned in agreement with the eib or with another public or private institution with a public mission. the member state concerned should address a formal request to the commission identifying the projects and the funding needs to be covered by the risk-sharing instrument. the commission will assess the request and will set up and manage the facility jointly with the eib. the regulation provides a detailed description of the procedure to be applied for the establishment and implementation of a risk-sharing instrument. we have also specified the budget ceiling for the risk-sharing instrument, and we have specified that there are no contingent liabilities for the union budget or the member state concerned beyond the financial allocations dedicated to the risk-sharing instrument. the commission shall ensure that only projects for which the eib or another interested institution with a public mission has taken a favourable financing decision are eligible for financing through this instrument. i hope that, following tomorrow’s vote in the european parliament, the council will adopt this regulation promptly, allowing for joint signature by the european parliament and the council in may, as well as publication in the official journal of the european union and entry into force on the same day.
