in writing. − i voted against this motion for a resolution, as did the ecr group. the directive on a common consolidated corporate tax base (ccctb) was to have a positive impact on ‘completing the single market and enhancing competitiveness’; however, the econ vote on 21 march 2012 called for a mandatory ccctb for all eu27. the resolution adopted in econ proposes a road map for the ccctb implementation: as soon as the directive comes into force, all companies would have the possibility to opt into the ccctb system. after two years, it would be mandatory for all transnational companies, and after five years, it would apply automatically to all companies operating on european territory, with the exception of smes.
in writing. − there is a broad consensus in favour of introducing a uniform cit tax base in the eu. it has been expressed on several occasions, including by the signatures of the signatories of the euro plus pact. this would be a major step towards the construction of the common market and a great help to european businesses. this would significantly improve the competitiveness of the european economy and would also allow savings for businesses. however, the consolidation project breaks the consensus built around this idea by creating artificial formulae for the distribution of cit revenues, which in turn leads to a division of eu countries into 'winners' and 'losers', i.e. those who benefit from the formula and those who lose. moreover, the document voted at the econ meeting mentions the possible harmonisation of the cit tax, which significantly distorts the original purpose of the directive. in view of the above arguments, i was forced to vote against this proposal in the hope that it would be rejected.
in writing. - i voted against the report on the common corporate tax base because i believe that this system should be voluntary and that its adoption should be long-term and dependent on the will of the companies that want to be covered by it. the report not only proposes to bring all multinational corporations under a common tax base within two years, but also to bring all large companies operating in the eu under one after five years. tax matters remain and should remain the exclusive responsibility of the member states. i object to any attempt to change that.
in writing. − the current energy directive only set minimum tax rates for energy products used as motor fuels and heating fuels, as well as for electricity, with the amount of taxation dependent only on the consumption of the raw material. the commission proposal amends the existing rules by proposing changes to the taxation of energy products to eliminate the existing disparities and to take account of co2 emissions together with the energy content of these products; introducing a 10-year transitional period for this change in order to fully harmonise the taxation system. in the case of poland, the newly proposed solutions are practically impossible without significant costs, which unfortunately are borne by consumers. within 10 years, there is no real possibility in poland to obtain enough energy from renewable sources, or to build nuclear power plants as is the case in france to move away from coal. coal has less calorific value than gas, but twice the emission, which means more taxation and thus more price for the average citizen. the new rules will also affect the competitiveness of poland, which generates up to 90% of its electricity from coal. moreover, the shift from a taxation system based solely on the amount of energy consumed to a new fuel, also dependent on fuel efficiency, may lead to the introduction of a so-called carbon tax, dependent on co2 emissions, which in my country means an additional increase in the excise duty on coal, which will be introduced in 2013. i voted against because i believe that the report adopted today and the legislative changes that follow will cause more problems than benefits.
in writing. - i dare say that the commission officials preparing this scandalous project did not consult him and did not properly analyse the impact of their proposals on the social situation in the countries of central and eastern europe. the commission's draft also calls for a comprehensive consultation of all interested parties. who's that? i want to know who these consultations were with in my country. in poland, coal is the main source of heating in households, especially in small towns and rural areas. one ton of coal burned is about three, three, five tons of co2. if you multiply this by 20 euros per tonne of co2 (how did you get this number? - i think it's from the ceiling. and why in euros?), assuming that the price of coal is currently between 500 and 700 pln per tonne, its price will increase by about 300 pln to 800 and 1,000 pln per tonne. on average, a farm uses six to seven tons of this fuel a year, and even more when it comes to farmers. did these 'consultations' take this into account? i don't think it was. that's why i voted to reject this reprehensible bill.
in writing. − the amendment of directive 2003/96/ec aims to align the european energy taxation system with the objectives of the eu's climate change strategy. the new fuel taxation system proposed by the european commission suggests a two-tiered tax rate, which is to be composed of the co2 emissions and the amount of energy that can be extracted from the raw material. the current draft envisages that each country will be able to decide on the shape of its rates, adjusted proportionally to the thresholds agreed at eu level. these changes are expected to lead to the increased use of biofuels and other renewable energy sources, gradually reducing the use of fossil fuels, thereby increasing energy efficiency while reducing carbon emissions. however, we cannot ignore the impact that higher fuel prices will inevitably have on the industry and economy of the member states. the automobile industry, the transport industry, and the energy industry, which in some countries is almost entirely coal-based, will suffer huge losses. in times of economic crisis, is this a step in the right direction? not surprisingly, this issue has become increasingly divisive and controversial. however, it should be borne in mind that the european parliament has only an advisory role in this matter, and the final decision is up to the governments and must be taken unanimously by all member states.
in writing. − i voted against this report because i believe that member states should have the right to set their own co2 taxation levels. in addition, the commission’s proposal for a revised directive on energy taxation changes the existing directive adopted in 2003 with respect to the structure of the energy taxation. i do not agree that, by 2025, the commission should make legislative proposals aimed at harmonising car purchase taxes, car registration taxes and car ownership taxes based on co2 emissions, or issue a report explaining why it has not done so. that is a matter for member states to decide.
in writing. - i voted against this report. it is clear that measures and instruments must be taken to help protect the environment, which is our common good, the good of not only eu citizens but of citizens all over the world. taxation of carbon emissions could be one such instrument. however, from poland's point of view, taxing coal emissions could have dramatic consequences, including, in particular, a huge increase in coal prices, which in turn could put many polish households in an even more difficult situation than before.
in writing. - energy taxation is a very sensitive subject. this is because energy prices are linked to the prices of other products and without adequate energy at a decent price, economies are immediately uncompetitive. so i'm skeptical of the idea of additional energy taxes, especially if they're done in the name of climate policy. it is important, of course, but not as important as a sound energy policy. we cannot afford to increase the taxation of an energy product, which generates 30% of the eu's energy, by a factor of six in the run-up to 2018. that product is, of course, coal, which has been attacked by many members of this house. since the amendments proposed by myself and the group of 40 members, which called for the optional nature of the emissions component, have failed, i have decided to vote against this directive. i did so despite the fact that the epp voted to scrap the principle of proportionality, which is unfavourable to all users of diesel cars. however, this was not enough to make the directive beneficial for poland and its citizens.
in writing. - there are many arguments against taxing fuel and heating prices. this is clearly damaging to the competitiveness of both the polish and the eu economies. taxation will cause heating and industrial products to increase in price in poland, which will in the long run result in the elimination of many jobs and the deepening of the disparity between eastern and western europe. energy-intensive industries in central europe have to pay twice for the same activity simply because coal is the dominant energy source in these countries. it seems that poland is still being punished for having large coal reserves. already, the costs of climate policy in poland amount to €5.4 billion a year, which is more than half of the pre-tax profit of the entire polish industry. that is why i voted against this report.
in writing. - in my country, poland, nearly 3 million households use coal-fired heating. the average consumption per farm is between 5 and 7 tonnes of coal per year, and far more for farms. one ton of coal emits about 3.5 tons of co2 when burned. so if we add, as mrs lulling reports, a €20 tax per tonne of co2 emitted, we get an increase in the price of coal of about pln 300 per tonne on average. it is a decidedly unacceptable and unacceptable increase in the cost of living that my countrymen cannot afford. i also see the continuation of the climate and energy package. that's why i voted against this report.
in writing. − the implementation of the solutions contained in this document leads directly to an increase in energy prices. in the economic crisis we are in, it's shooting ourselves in the foot. that is why i am all the more surprised that the european parliament allows such strong intervention in the market. our actions should be directed in the opposite direction and should lead to lower energy prices and easier energy production. we must finally resist the new european disease of green energy policy and the one-sided, pointless reduction of co2 emissions.
in writing. - the grey area in poland concerns about 25% of gdp. in the european union, the average is 15 percent. this means a huge loss of revenue to the state budget. this results in more debt being placed on individual countries and less money being spent on essential public services. at the same time, a grey area indicates a serious lack of inflows into member states' pension systems. this is particularly important as public debates are taking place in many countries about the possible raising of the retirement age. mass tax evasion was one of the causes of the greek crisis. the greek case should be a lesson for the european union as a whole and force the community institutions and the member states to make rapid legislative changes to tighten up the tax collection system. the resolution by parliament on the call for concrete measures to combat tax fraud and tax evasion is an important gesture to mobilise the other community institutions and the member states to work towards changes in the legal system that will improve the collection of taxes. i therefore voted in favour of the resolution with full conviction.
madam president! i think there is no one in this room who would argue that the european union should not promote the protection of human rights, but in the case of the union's accession to the convention we have - and i personally have - some doubts about the wisdom of such a move, of such a step. first, i would like to know what guarantees there are that this will not lead to increased competition between the two tribunals. there are already competence disputes between strasbourg and luxembourg, which creates some difficulties. another important issue is the scale of the financial support that the union will provide to the european court of human rights. it should also be borne in mind that each member state of the european union has already signed the convention. what, then, will be the added value of the eu as a whole joining? how will this affect the internal legal system of each eu country? i have the impression, unfortunately, that the only purpose he has in mind is to emphasise the european union's status as a major player on the international stage.

on behalf of the ecr group. mr president, i would like to thank you for your kind words. i join the voices that have been raised about the lack of maps. indeed, we cannot rationally proceed if we do not have such documents. as regards the criteria we should use to define lessfavoured areas, i think that these criteria should relate primarily to soil conditions. soil moisture, which mr. nicholson talked about, is a very important condition and it should be taken into account. conditions relating to labour intensity are also important. there are areas where it just takes a lot more work to get a crop than other areas. that's what the highlands are like. and so is competitiveness. areas with greater distance from the market, where additional costs are incurred to either sell their products or to obtain means of production, should be taken into account. these should be the main criteria for identifying less-favoured areas.
thank you very much, mr. chairman! despite the considerable efforts of the commission and the member states in developing the method for the designation of areas with natural constraints, the proposed biophysical criteria do not meet the basic expectation of an objective designation of areas with actual natural constraints at community level. nor, as can be seen with the naked eye, is there sufficient justification for adjusting administrative units such as lau 2 municipalities, whose size varies widely across the european union. the average size of lau 2 for the union as a whole is 3,5 thousand hectares, and in poland this average is 12,5 thousand hectares. for some countries, the difference in lau 2 is as much as ten times greater than the eu average. in my view, small administrative units, such as recording ranges, which are homogeneous in terms of soil and thus better reflect natural constraints should be used. moreover, the application of the lau 2 level in combination with a high threshold of 66%, especially in countries with different soil and climatic conditions, such as poland, will result in the exclusion of areas with natural constraints whose eligibility criteria will not reach the appropriate level. in the case of poland, areas with scientifically proven low productivity and a risk of silting would not qualify as areas with natural constraints. this is really a reversal of fortune and, for the time being, it would be best to remove this issue from the reform of the agricultural policy in the union under discussion. thank you very much. thank you.
on behalf of the ecr group. mr president, i would like to thank you for your kind words. in reference to what mr bové said and to the interesting exchange of views between mr deß and mr jahr earlier, i would like to say that in the report on the transport of animals which i am currently preparing - which will shortly be put to the vote in the committee on agriculture - i am very much raising the issue of local slaughterhouses, which really should be supported, developed. and this is one way to reinforce this idea of regional products, so that they are actually local products, produced in a particular region. and to get back to the main theme: well, we're seeing a process in the world and in europe of displacing traditional agricultural production based on natural methods by industrial agriculture. an increasing share of agricultural production comes from large industrial farms. natural farming based on family farms, using traditional production methods is in reverse, and this is a very unfavorable process leading to a deterioration in the quality of food, a deterioration in animal welfare conditions, negative consequences for the environment and many other negative consequences. i am strongly in favour of local products being defined as those products that are entirely produced in a particular region using traditional production methods for that region and that are environmentally friendly and animal welfare friendly. this should be a condition for treating such products as local products. i can't imagine calling a local product, for example, a product from a large-scale farming, as in some regions in poland we have large-scale farms run by businesses from e.g. denmark, that meat produced in such a farm would be called a local product from a specific region in poland. it's not supposed to be like this.

the rapporteur. - mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, i would like to thank you for your kind words. the report i am presenting to you concerns the effects of decentralising the management of external aid. this process has been going on for several years and involves transferring management from brussels to the european union delegations in the countries benefiting from our development aid. the long-term objective of decentralising external aid, which is managed by the european commission, is to increase the efficiency of development actions, their speed and the accuracy of financial management procedures, which is why this report was considered by the committee on budgetary control. another objective is to improve the quality of aid in partner countries. i am sure you will agree that a decentralised approach to development cooperation has many advantages: it makes decision-making closer to reality, closer to the direct beneficiaries, more efficient in terms of operations and in terms of coordinating and harmonising the work of different donors. at the same time, this approach ensures accountability at local level. it should be added that decentralisation of management will not solve all the problems. in the report i have tried to identify additional tasks which are a prerequisite for increasing the effectiveness of aid. the aid managed by the individual delegations continues to cover a very wide range of areas which are too broad. this is why it is so important to improve coordination between the european union, the member states and partner countries, but also to improve the coordination of development activities and to improve their efficiency and effectiveness. a better division of labour, focusing on those areas where the union has a competitive advantage and a real capacity to add value, is the way to increase efficiency. decentralisation also reduces the transaction costs of the aid provided - this is good, but it is not the only way to reduce these costs. one such method is budget support, which focuses more on the quality of aid, partnership and needs of beneficiary countries. i also think it is worthwhile to highlight a number of issues that are important for aid effectiveness. in recent years, the composition of the staff of the delegations has changed, with an increasing number of staff holding political and commercial functions. the report therefore calls for a proper balance to be struck between the functions of aid management and the other functions performed by the delegations in respect of staff in the delegations. the high level of staff turnover in the delegations is also a cause for concern, as it weakens the continuity of the institution's functioning, the so-called institutional memory, and has a negative impact on the effectiveness of the activities carried out. the report reiterates the call for the designation of policy cohesion contact points in each delegation, the obvious aim being to monitor the impact of eu policies on the partner country. i believe that the union's financial instruments and the european development fund should focus more on poverty reduction. the ultimate eradication of poverty is the main objective of european development cooperation, as set out in article 208 of the treaty of lisbon. the draft report also stresses that neither the european commission nor the member states should use the current financial crisis to justify a focused approach to get more for less, which means, among other things, reducing the level of employment in bilateral aid agencies. i ask for your support for this report and thank you for your attention.

in writing. - i supported the report on women and climate change. research indicates that climate change is not gender neutral and its effects are differentiated for women and men. this is confirmed by the intergovernmental panel on climate change (ipcc) in its 4th assessment report 2007. women account for 85 percent of climate change deaths and 75 percent of environmental refugees. women have a higher mortality rate due to natural disasters (over 70% of those killed by the 2004 tsunami were women). therefore, climate change research should take greater account of gender. i'm looking at the situation of women in developing countries, who are taking the brunt of climate change. women and girls are disproportionately more vulnerable to the consequences of climate change, due to pervasive gender inequalities. traditional gender roles and discrimination against women reduce their ability to adapt their lifestyles to climate change. the effects of climate change will have long-term consequences for gender equality. they are exacerbating inequalities in access to the wealth, the land, the new technologies, the education, the information that are essential elements in the fight against climate change. i call on the european commission to develop aid programmes which take account of the situation of women. women should be more involved in the development of adaptation strategies.
in writing. - the environment is the greatest treasure of our planet. it is by means of it that we live, breathe, are born, and die. it is thanks to nature's kindness that the human species has survived from generation to generation, surrounded by other species of living organisms, fauna and flora. it is vital for all citizens, since we all want to live in a clean, well-kept environment. unfortunately, today, according to scientific data, more than half of the natural ecosystems on our planet are being degraded, non-renewable resources are being over-exploited, and our age-old industry and consumer lifestyles are leading to ever greater climate change. to ensure the survival of the environment for future generations, we must do all we can to support actions to protect biodiversity and ecosystem security. the right financial resources, cooperation not only at international but also at intercontinental level, coordination between different policy areas and, above all, the awareness that without nature life on earth cannot exist, are essential factors for the rapid and effective implementation of pro-environmental strategies that ensure a bright future for our heirs.

in writing. reducing charges on public mobile networks within the union is the next step in the process of market harmonisation, bringing europe closer to the ideal where consumers have free and affordable access to mobile telephony services throughout the eu. this regulation represents an innovative approach, as it not only proposes price caps but also a structural change in the market. it will also increase competitiveness between operators, stimulate the internal market and contribute to the mobility of citizens and the development of small and medium-sized enterprises. the unification of roaming charges is very beneficial for eu citizens, as many europeans face high costs for their calls when living or travelling outside their own country and calling their families. from july, calls to mobile phones abroad will cost 29 cents, or just over 30 pence, and the price of an incoming call will be a maximum of 8 cents. mobile phones should be mobile, yet many eu citizens turn off their mobile phones, smartphones and tablets, fearing the high cost of data when travelling within the union. competition is still weak and operators continue to benefit from excessive margins, especially in data transmission. now, customers have to pay a few euros for 1 mb, and this holiday they'll pay no more than 70 cents. moreover, they will be able to choose the foreign operator they wish to use.
in writing. current prices for roaming services bear little relation to the costs of providing them for mobile networks. we're not talking about the profits of these companies, but the sheer cost to european consumers, who are still overpaying for phone calls, text messages, not to mention data transfers, as soon as they leave their country. the cell phone bill is now the guaranteed ticket to any foreign vacation. thanks to parliament, roaming charges have been reduced again. for the first time, this also applies to data transmission.
in writing. the cost of telephone calls between eu countries is still too high. i therefore welcome the proposals in the 'roaming 3' regulation to reduce them. it should be borne in mind that the removal of barriers to the internal market and the reduction of costs within the union not only lead to greater savings but also strengthen the community's competitiveness abroad. it is also one of the main assumptions of the theory of common currency areas which underlies the european community. we should therefore go further and, instead of setting a maximum price ceiling, we should aim at the total abolition of roaming within the european union. companies are technically prepared for such actions and therefore their balance sheet will not be affected by such decisions. similar rules should also be introduced for the transmission of internet data and internet access while travelling within the european community.

on 9 may 1950, french foreign minister robert schuman called on the democratic countries of europe to come together to prevent a future repeat of the tragedy of world war ii. this day is widely regarded as the beginning of a united europe. the reconciliatory nature of the declaration towards germany and the openness to the participation of other european countries set new standards of political life in europe. today, 62 years after the schuman declaration was issued, it is still relevant. however, in the wake of the economic crisis that has hit europe, we are increasingly witnessing a worrying resurgence of local nationalism, racism and xenophobia on our continent. this is accompanied by a significant loss of confidence in the european union and the idea of integration. the union itself is currently facing the biggest identity crisis in its history. so what is the future of europe?
in writing. i believe that a well-developed network of regional airports and related services is definitely one of the determinants of the source of economic growth in the european union as a whole. in my amendments to the transport committee i have tried to emphasize from the outset that regional airports have a dual purpose within the european connecting system. first, they provide a convenient network of links between distant agglomerations with smaller populations, which cannot be marginalised. secondly, the well-developed network of airports, with the increasing number of connections and flights within existing ones, creates many risks. therefore, regional airports can provide an additional efficient network of emergency airports. looking at it from the perspective of the problems that were created by last year's icelandic volcano eruption. the creation of such a network is certainly a matter of some importance in terms of viability, and the inclusion of some airports in the ten-t core network will facilitate their co-financing. in conclusion, i would like to stress that the restoration of balance and thus competitiveness in the transport market should be at the heart of the regional airport network being established.

in writing. − generally speaking comitology procedure refers to the mandate of the european commission to execute its implementing powers delegated to it by the legislative branch (the european parliament and the council). this delegation of power is now based on article 290tfeu. the entry into force of the lisbon treaty changed the comitology procedure, turning it into a new system for adopting delegated acts and implementing acts. the new rule 87a,in combination with the new rule 88, lays down the standard procedure to be followed where consideration of the proposed delegated act or implementing act by a committee responsible, are involved, this without being associated committees or committees jointly responsible. the procedure applicable in cases involving associated committees or committees jointly responsible is laid down in a new rule 88a. the revision of the rules of procedure is welcomed for it allows for the rapid approval of a delegated act or implementing act; it provided more flexibility in the process, all while strengthening the democratic principles of separation of power. for these reasons i voted in favour of the report.
in writing. - the amendments to the ep's rules of procedure were necessary because of the revolutionary changes brought about by the treaty of lisbon in the comitology procedure.

in writing. − ensuring internal security is one of the key elements of the eu's internal policy. to ensure this, it is necessary to have qualified staff in the fields of both the internal security system of the union and the security of information network systems, crisis management and civil security. however, this cannot be achieved without taking into account the comprehensive approach to the european security strategy, which is based on a holistic concept of human security based on human rights, freedom, democracy, the rule of law, good governance and peace. a comprehensive approach to human security must be skillfully combined with relations with third countries, in particular in the areas of border management, migration, the fight against organised crime, terrorism and trafficking in human beings. and looking at the recent arab spring experience, it is important to remember that the eu's internal security is inextricably linked to the security situation in its neighbourhood, and in particular to highlight the importance of the european neighbourhood policy and to develop synergies between the eu and its neighbours.
in writing. - i support the report on the internal security strategy of the european union in its broad outlines. it is a fact that the threats are international in nature, in particular terrorism, cybercrime and organised crime. this is why they must be tackled not only at national level, but also through better coordination within the eu. in this context, however, i believe that the report is too vague as regards the role of europol and the union's ability to respond to natural disasters that may threaten security. i am strongly in favour of increasing the union's capacity to respond to disasters. today, the union relies mainly on national resources. in my view, common resources should also be created at union level, and this should primarily concern transport capacity, the available fleet of aircraft and helicopters that would reach the disaster sites quickly. it's not good today.
in writing. - consumers are a very important part of the internal market, and some of them require special attention. the assumption that we are all vulnerable consumers at some point in our lives is a valuable insight that should be taken into account in shaping eu policy, and in particular in initiatives to strengthen the internal market. i emphasise this, for example, in the context of the discussion on the development of social entrepreneurship. social enterprises pursue not only business but also social objectives, which means that they better understand the needs of sensitive consumers and can meet those needs more effectively. therefore, by recognising the role of social enterprises in the internal market, we will contribute to improving conditions for particularly vulnerable consumers. in this context, i would also stress the need to better inform consumers in general, which is even more important for sensitive consumers. reliable information makes consumers more active, more aware of their rights and more willing to use the procedures provided for them. for sensitive consumers, the type of information provided is of great importance, as this group of consumers needs more information to be able to participate fully in the single market. the report identifies the sectors most affected by the current crisis. identifying the areas that may pose the greatest risk to consumer safety is an important step towards strengthening consumer protection.
in writing. − in the age of the single market, european consumer rights are a matter of vital importance for all citizens. many people still do not know their privileges, do not know how to claim their rights, and are not familiar with the requirements that a salesperson must meet when selling their product. if consumers had this information, they could make quick and accurate decisions when choosing a product and, if they purchased a defective product, they could easily and quickly get their money back or exchange the item they had purchased. the european commission stresses the importance of informing consumers about their rights, returns and complaints. however, as the rapporteur points out, an information campaign may not be a sufficient means of support, especially for consumers who are particularly vulnerable to abuse by retailers. these consumers are children, the elderly or the disabled. that's why we should provide adequate legal protection for our most needy citizens.
in writing. - consumer protection is a very important element of the european union's economy. in the present day, when producers are fighting each other to sell their products (sometimes illegally, at any price), consumers are often the victims of various ways of circumventing consumer law. in particular, this type of case concerns the failure to inform consumers of the exact composition of a product (in the case of food). consumers themselves are often not fully aware of their rights to compensation or to complaints for obvious misleading information from the manufacturer. consumers are particularly unaware of their rights in the case of distance selling, electronic commerce or cross-border sales. it goes without saying that disabled people in particular have additional problems with the proper enforcement of consumer law and are often disadvantaged as a result. and research shows that groups that are particularly vulnerable to this are discouraged from taking action when problems arise. it is therefore very important that there should be regular information campaigns in the community countries to make consumers aware of the law which they can avail themselves of. i hope that in the long run, this will ensure that the seller/consumer relationship does not lose out (as it often does) in the event of disputes.

in writing. in view of the significant disparity in trade between the eu and china, we believe it is essential to take appropriate steps to extend the principle of reciprocity to eu-china economic relations. one source of this inequality is the chinese state's favouring of its own economy by creating certain obstacles for eu investors, including by limiting the forms of doing business in china to joint ventures. this is sometimes protectionist in nature, as it makes it difficult for foreign investors to take majority stakes in chinese companies and requires technology transfer, which reduces the competitiveness of eu companies. another major problem is the respect for intellectual property rights (ipr). until china implements regulations to ensure the protection of ipr, there will be no level playing field. furthermore, i would like to note that there is no substantive basis for china to express regret at the existence of alleged barriers in the eu in the form of subsidies for farmers or tariffs on agricultural products, given that there is a whole range of similar legal instruments on the chinese side. we will support any changes that bring the chinese economy closer to meeting the wto criteria of a market economy and to eliminating trade imbalances with the union.
in writing. the european union has found itself in need of redefining its relations with china, which has become a key player in the international arena in almost all areas in a relatively short time. the key to europe's relationship with china should be a partnership based on reciprocity. in this spirit, the chinese could expect equal and unfettered access to the investment and public procurement market from europe, to the benefit of european consumers. but at the same time, the european union must demand the same rights for european investors and entrepreneurs operating in the chinese market, i.e. to provide them with appropriate training, guidance, support in finding partners and help in solving specific problems. in my view, such functions should be actively carried out by the relevant eu diplomatic representation cells in china, without discrimination. at the same time, the eu will only have a chance to compete with china on a level playing field if it invests fully in research and innovation, thereby developing the sectors whose products are most in demand on the chinese market. the transfer of technology to china should be constantly compensated by the creation of new solutions that will provide a lasting and sustainable demand for european industrial production. this should be taken into particular account in the process of negotiating the sectoral financial allocations in the multiannual financial framework for the period 2014-2020.

in writing. the global economic and financial crisis has had a serious impact on the economies and public finances of the member states. there is no doubt that the financial sector played a significant role in causing the economic crisis, while the cost of the rescue programmes was borne by central budgets, that is, by de facto european taxpayers. there is a strong consensus in europe and internationally that the financial sector should be more involved in the cost of rescue programmes. the fiscal intervention is also justified by the relatively low taxation of the financial sector compared to other sectors of the economy. the commission proposal for a directive on a common system of financial transaction tax is a concrete expression of these demands. the european union is thus the first g20 country to come forward with a constructive proposal for regulation in this area. i consider the proposals made by the econ committee to be useful. the main points to be noted here are the introduction of an additional emission criterion in addition to the residence criterion for the purposes of defining taxable transactions, the exclusion of pension funds from corporate taxation and the establishment of preferential rates for trading on regulated markets. i consider the amendment tabled in plenary session, which excludes investment funds from the taxation in question, to be harmful. in my view, this proposal distorts the idea of a financial transaction tax, since it excludes a large number of financial institutions from taxation and thus reduces the effectiveness of this regulation.

in writing. − the global economic and financial crisis has had a serious impact on the economies and public finances of the member states. there is no doubt that the financial sector played a significant role in causing the economic crisis, while the cost of the rescue programmes was borne by central budgets, that is, by de facto european taxpayers. there is a strong consensus in europe and internationally that the financial sector should show greater commitment, given the costs of overcoming the crisis and the current relatively low taxation of the sector compared to other sectors. the commission proposal for a directive on a common system of financial transaction tax is a concrete expression of these demands. the european union is thus the first g20 country to come forward with a constructive proposal for regulation in this area. the proposals developed by the econ committee, which additionally introduce an issue criterion (a financial transaction is taxable even if the instrument was issued by a legal entity registered in the eu) in the identification of taxable financial transactions and exclude pension funds from the scope of corporate taxation (thus not increasing the cost of long-term savings), should be considered useful. i object to the exclusion of investment funds from the scope of corporate taxation. in my view, this proposal distorts the idea of a financial transaction tax, since it excludes a large number of financial institutions from taxation and thus reduces the effectiveness of this regulation.
in writing. − the economic crisis that erupted in autumn 2008 started in financial institutions. one of the most important lessons we should take from this crisis is the need for immediate regulation of financial markets. unfortunately, that lesson was not learned. speculative institutions continue to threaten the security of individual member states, the euro area and the european union as a whole. however, i very much welcome the european commission's initiative to introduce a financial transaction tax. the demand, which was raised for years by the anti-globalisation movement and then the party of european socialists, has gained the support of an institution that for years was not known for its openness to such solutions. the financial transaction tax should fulfil two basic functions. first, to help curb financial speculation. secondly, to be an important source of revenue for the eu budget. these resources should then be invested in stimulating growth, including through the creation of new jobs. this is linked to a new model for tackling the economic crisis, which the union is very much looking forward to adopting. after four years of crisis, it is hard to be under any illusions about the effectiveness of austerity and austerity. in view of the above, i have decided to support the report on the common system of financial transaction tax.
in writing. - a new tax should be created. it must be a tax that does not affect industrial sectors and employers. the ftt gives you that opportunity. but i think it has to be a rational shape. it should therefore primarily cover only euro area countries or all countries without exception, including the united kingdom and sweden. this will avoid attempts to shift financial activities to ftt-exempt countries. the revenue from this tax should support cohesion policy. only then can we be sure that they will be a stimulus to economic growth.
in writing. - in the context of the crisis in europe, it is essential to seek a balanced trade relationship with an economic power such as china, which has recorded an economic growth rate of 10% for 30 years, mainly due to exports, of which the union is the main recipient. opening trade is clearly more beneficial for china, which reached a peak of eur 395 billion in global trade in 2010, while eu foreign investment in china in the same year was only eur 4.9 billion. in seeking to level trade relations with china, the union must defend the social market economy model, which requires reciprocity and protects the interests of europeans, and promote the concept of development, democracy and human rights in our partner. we should strive to make the chinese market more competitive and open to eu businesses on equal terms and on clear terms. today, this is hampered by government interventionist industrial policies, insufficient protection of intellectual property (ip) and an ambiguous system of standards. we must therefore promote and help implement eu good practices and put pressure on china to respect common trade standards, especially in the area of imps. with 85% of counterfeit goods stopped at eu borders coming from china, it is hard to talk about competitiveness and respect for rights. this must change if we are to be considered equal trading partners. i agree with the rapporteur that we need a new balanced approach to eu-china trade relations that can meet today's market challenges and help to contribute to the economic growth of both sides.
in writing. − trade relations between the eu and china should be based on a partnership of equals. unfortunately, european companies are currently not allowed to invest in china under similar conditions as chinese investments in europe. there are also other trade barriers, such as the granting of export subsidies and credits in certain sectors, the requirement to obtain national certificates, or regulatory opacity. according to the 2011 data, 43% of ceos of european companies operating in china considered that the measures adopted by beijing were discriminatory against them, compared to 33% in 2010. that is why i voted for this report.
in writing. - i voted in favour of an important and well-prepared report on 'the european union and china: imbalances in trade relations'. this report is of great importance for the development of trade between china and the european union. the union is right to be concerned about fair, sustainable and favourable trade. we are aware of the advantages of china and the advantages of the eu, and we want them to be realised in conditions of fair competition, taking into account also the political, economic and social implications of chinese investments in the world, especially in developing countries. opening up chinese markets, complying with wto rules, access to raw materials, technology transfer are all important issues that have been rightly raised.
in writing. - the european union is china's largest trading partner. unfortunately, the situation is not the same on the other side. the trade balance is still negative and is negatively affecting our economy, increasing unemployment, so we should take active measures to protect our market and balance the trade deficit. china must sign declarations on environmental protection and co2 reduction and must accept the imposition of anti-dumping duties on products from the middle east, e.g. cement, building materials and footwear. in times of crisis, we must protect our market more strongly.
in writing. - i fully agree with my group that national parliaments are the right arena for many of the powers provided for in this report. the powers mentioned in the report are not needed at european level, especially as regards the summoning of witnesses and the penalties for those who refuse to cooperate. the powers to carry out on-the-spot inspections, to request documents, to question officials and other servants of the union and of the member states, to call witnesses and to request an expert report seem to go too far.
in writing. - the ep's position is a reasonable introduction to negotiations with the council on the exercise of the parliament's powers of inquiry under the lisbon treaty.

on behalf of the efd group. mr president, i would like to thank you for your kind words. the european union is founded on the principle of free movement of persons and equal treatment. the introduction by switzerland of limits on the number of permanent residence permits is a flagrant breach of that principle. we don't want to think that the intentions were bad, but that's the facts. significantly, this is true of european union countries that have experienced isolation and the yoke of communism in the past. that is why this case is a test whether there are two europeans or one, whether we are together or apart. i am confident that the european parliament will give the european commission a strong argument for further work and action with our swiss friends. we do not allow the language of confrontation, we believe that this is a situation that should not happen, and we deeply believe that it will be resolved quickly, because in a free europe this situation should not take place.
mr. chairman, please! as you can see, the discussion about introducing quotas for citizens of certain european union countries to stay in switzerland is very lively. i am pleased that this debate brings together citizens from different countries - meps from the countries that were members, founding members of the european union and countries that have just joined the european union. in this debate, from right to left, from left to right, from all the parties, between which we argue very sharply every day and have very different opinions, this time we all agree and we all strongly support the draft resolution of member trzaskowski and others. and the reason it's gaining so much support today is because we realize that the closer we work together, the more we open up to each other, the more we all gain. the european union is characterised by a win-win formula, where one gains and the other loses. i have the impression that the swiss people are also aware of this. after all, they voted in the referendum for schengen in 2005 and for the free movement of people in 2009. both decisions have gained widespread public support. why should this administrative decision now drive our friends, a friendly and close country switzerland, away from us and prevent the use of win-win? thank you, sir.
in writing. the swiss government's decision to limit the number of permanent residence permits for citizens of eight central and eastern european countries is particularly worrying in the context of the discriminatory treatment faced by citizens of this part of europe, for example in the netherlands. recently, the citizens of the eu member states have been divided into 'better' and 'worse' citizens, which could have very dangerous consequences in the future. citizens of poland, lithuania, latvia, estonia, slovenia, slovakia, the czech republic and hungary represent only a small percentage of the population of european union citizens permanently residing and working in switzerland. it is therefore difficult to understand the swiss government's decision, taken ostensibly to protect the national labour market. furthermore, it is alarming that this decision appears to be illegal under the agreement between switzerland and the community, a restriction on access to the labour market can be introduced only and exclusively for all eu citizens. switzerland shall enjoy the rights conferred by its participation in the european economic area without restriction. switzerland's exports to the eu-10 in 2010 amounted to over eur 4 trillion, equivalent to exports to china. in this situation, we have the right to demand reciprocity from switzerland in economic contacts. we call on the european commission to take urgent action to clarify the situation.
in writing. the decision of the swiss government to reinstate the quantitative limits for certain categories of permanent residence permits issued to citizens of the eight new eu member states the czech republic, estonia, lithuania, latvia, poland, slovenia, slovakia and hungary introduces an unacceptable and unfair discrimination between eu citizens on the basis of their nationality, which is discriminatory and contrary to european values and law. the european parliament, as recently with the pvv website in the netherlands, has always taken a strong stand against breaking the fundamental principles on which the eu is founded one of them is the principle of non-discrimination on grounds of nationality. i therefore fully agree with the assessment of the high representative catherine ashton that this decision violates the agreement on the free movement of persons, which does not allow any distinction to be made between eu citizens. under the agreement, swiss citizens can move freely within the eu, but the same rights must also be guaranteed to all union citizens in switzerland. switzerland has an agreement with the union and should now comply with it. if the swiss government deems it necessary, it can impose quotas, but they must apply to all eu citizens without exception, because there are no first and second class citizens in the eu, and all eu citizens should be treated equally.
in writing. i am concerned that in the last few months we have once again been speaking out on a matter as fundamental as freedom of movement and residence, especially as this discussion is taking place in the context of highly developed countries with a deep democratic tradition. the decision by switzerland to temporarily introduce quotas for work permits for workers from selected eu member states is simply blatantly inconsistent with the existing agreements between the eu and the swiss confederation. as enshrined in article 9 teu, eu citizenship constitutes the legal link linking any natural person who holds the nationality of a member state to the european union. it gives rise to both obligations and rights, the most important of which is the free movement of persons. european citizenship is based on the principle of equal treatment of all citizens, irrespective of nationality. the resolution voted today in a constructive way, opening the way for discussion and cooperation, reflects our view of the decision taken by the national council of the swiss confederation. the most important thing to remember is that the european union was created for the good of its citizens. their freedom and liberty are therefore one of the main elements of the work that the institutions of the european union should be concerned with. we, as members of the european parliament, therefore have a duty to express our disapproval of attempts to introduce mechanisms which discriminate against european union citizens.

in writing. − the programme of macro-financial assistance to third countries experiencing temporary balance of payments difficulties, which has been in place for over two decades, is an excellent element in the development of mutual relations. in particular, as regards neighbouring countries, this aid has made a valuable contribution to macroeconomic stability. the lisbon treaty has made this easier and i am glad that countries like ukraine and moldova have benefited from this. i hope georgia will benefit as well. i agree with the need to present the appropriate criteria for the selection of beneficiaries. as the programme aims at stabilisation in the immediate neighbourhood of the community and 'europeanisation', the main beneficiaries should be the aspiring member states. the introduction of a faster and more efficient way of deciding on aid with a more precise geographical coverage will allow for much more effective implementation of neighbourhood policy and, in some cases, perhaps a leading role in macro-financial assistance. i voted for the resolution.

in writing. − the resolution on the situation in ukraine raises an important issue of the need for further reform in ukraine. it was stressed that future elections must be free, fair and transparent, and that this will be possible, inter alia, by allowing the opposition leaders to participate. noting the difficult situation of former prime minister yulia tymoshenko, it was stressed that legislative reform is necessary. at the same time, however, the resolution notes that despite the declarations of some politicians about not participating in the euro 2012 celebrations in ukraine, there was no call for a boycott of the championship. i consider this to be particularly important. the ukrainian society should have the possibility of integration into the union, which is at the heart of the european neighbourhood policy.
in writing. − recent political developments in ukraine may be of concern, especially to those who care about ukraine's european future. the european parliament has an important role to play in ensuring that democratic standards are maintained in cooperation with the european union. it is right that attention should be drawn to the situation of former prime minister yulia tymoshenko. however, it is important to choose appropriate means of pressure on ukraine. i'm consistently opposed to mixing politics with sports. this was my position when the demand was raised to take the ice hockey world championship in belarus in 2012. i was very concerned to hear statements from important eu politicians calling for a political boycott of euro 2012. the polish delegation in the socialists and democrats (s&d) group has appealed to all meps to attend euro 2012 in poland and ukraine and this appeal is maintained in the current circumstances. boycotting euro 2012 will have the opposite effect. today, more than the boycott of euro 2012, ukrainian society needs european openness and people-to-people contacts. a boycott of euro 2012 could have the unintended effect of increasing anti-european sentiment. therefore, i welcome the silencing of calls for a boycott of euro 2012 as a sign of political wisdom.

in writing. - we have insufficient resources in the european union to meet our internal consumption needs. the commission has therefore decided to propose a new, more economical model of consumption, and to develop a new approach to economic instruments. the idea is to remove the environmental tax from labour and shift this burden onto raw materials, energy and materials. this will be a good step towards more efficient use of resources. further fiscal reforms and cooperation in the eu single market are needed to increase european competition on a global scale. investment in the eu that is essential for growth should take this into account. i therefore voted in favour of this own-initiative ep project, hoping for a future legislative solution that takes account of the pro-innovation market philosophy in europe.
in writing. −last autumn, the european commission adopted an action plan for a resource efficient europe, setting out the directions and initiatives to ensure that the union can grow economically in a sustainable way while respecting the environment. ensuring biodiversity and healthy ecosystems for the citizens of our continent is a major challenge, requiring concrete, coordinated action from a wide range of policies (such as research, production and consumption, transport and construction) already now. of course, more efficient use of raw materials proper management of natural resources and efficient recycling of secondary raw materials are also necessary. i also agree with the rapporteur that close cooperation with the public and private sectors is a key element in creating the right strategy, and that action at local level is as important as the european level in this regard.
in writing. - i object to the text in which parliament calls on the commission to present proposals by 2014 to introduce a general ban on landfilling at european level. i am also not in favour of calling on member states to introduce an environmental tax. i am in favour of efficient use of secondary raw materials and the creation of appropriate incentives to prevent waste. however, for some member states such as poland the prohibitions, environmental taxes and other constraints will hit the average taxpayer the hardest. i feel that this fact was not taken into account in mr gerbrandt's report.
in writing. − the report on a resource-efficient europe highlights many of the valuable challenges facing the european union today. it is a european strategy for future growth that has an international dimension, and it points to biodiversity, natural capital and ecosystem services. today, not only the european but also the global economy is affected by the economic crisis, but i believe that we should look to the future and develop new programmes and use innovative measures that will ensure economic growth and progress. europe needs ambitious plans that take account of the pace of change and emphasise cooperation with member states, regional authorities and local authorities, which is why i voted in favour of the gerben-jan gerbrandy report.
in writing. - i voted against the resolution, as did the ecr group. i disagree with the statement that 'the youth guarantee must be legally enforceable in order to actually improve the situation of young people who are not in employment, education or training'. we need to find solutions to overcome the problem of youth unemployment in the eu, but i do not think that punishing member states is the right solution.
in writing. − statistics show that there are about 7.5 million young people aged 15-24 in the european union who are not in employment and not in education. in some european countries, youth unemployment is as high as 50%. there is no doubt that the economic crisis is one of the reasons for these statistics. the problem is obvious, and that is why i think we need to take swift and effective action that will point to new tools and opportunities for young people, especially now, in such a mobile, changing society. concrete structural reforms are needed to create new jobs. we should use innovation, european funds, cross-border programmes and improve education systems. the european social fund is one of the most important instruments that will allow the creation of new programmes for young people and will enable them to enter the labour market. that's why i voted for the youth opportunity initiative.
in writing. - i voted for the resolution on the initiative "opportunities for the youth". i believe that three issues are particularly important: the situation of young mothers, the linking of training to labour market requirements and support from the european social fund. the largest employment gap between women and men is between 25 and 35 years of age. employers do not want to hire young women because they fear that they may become pregnant and become a burden (less availability, extra benefits). it is therefore very important that countries implement policies to make it easier for women to reconcile family and work life, so that potential employers are not afraid to hire young women and they do not have a "glass ceiling". member states should offer training to enable working women to work at home. it is necessary to provide access to childcare (nursery, kindergarten). in line with the objectives set out in the europe 2020 strategy, member states need to better adapt vocational training to labour market needs. young people must be trained for the future, i.e. for the requirements of the labour market. i call on the commission and the member states to make the best use of the structural funds, including the european social fund (esf), to implement specific programmes to combat unemployment among women. the esf has a further eur 82 billion to be made available until 2013. increasing youth employment should be a priority.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution because i believe it represents an important voice for the european parliament in the debate on how to combat youth unemployment. a high-quality youth policy, in line with the europe 2020 objectives, should be a priority of the national reform plans. i therefore join the call to member states to focus on developing effective, long-term strategies to align education systems with current labour market requirements. the 'youth opportunities' initiative is a positive example of eu action to prevent early school leaving and to promote vocational skills. the union must, however, be more ambitious in its actions. in order to support more initiatives under the new financial perspective 2014-2020, stronger financial support should be allocated to combat youth unemployment. it is worthwhile for the commission to allocate the unspent funds under the 2007-13 multiannual financial framework to youth programmes and support for professional mobility.
in writing. − the results of the study show that the average gender pay gap in eu countries is around 16% to the detriment of women and is decreasing at an exceptionally low rate. this condition is made up of many factors, such as cultural background, worldview, economic background, and so on. the complexity of the problem and its multiple origins make it significantly more difficult to combat discriminatory practices in the form of lower pay for the same work done by women. however, in the light of the eu directives and resolutions calling for equal treatment for both sexes, including in terms of pay, i believe that any action to increase compliance with these acts should be intensified. this can be achieved, inter alia, by introducing pay audits at workplaces and publishing their reports. the role of equality promotion and monitoring bodies should also be strengthened to provide information and consultation support to victims of discriminatory practices by employers. i also consider the issue of the dissemination of the issue to be particularly important, as it is being pushed into the background of the public debate, which unfairly diminishes its importance and indirectly contributes to the stagnation in the field of improving the situation of women in the labour market.
in writing. - like my group, i abstained on the report by mrs bauer. while the statistics are true and there is no doubt that wage discrimination still exists, i am not in favour of the idea that employment legislation covering wages should be set at eu level, as should social security matters. i think these are matters which should be decided by the individual member states. this does not change the fact that the statistics on the gender pay gap are alarming: within the eu, the gaps range from 1.9% to 27.6%.
in writing. - i voted for mrs bauer's report today. once again, since 2008, when the european commission launched an information campaign on the gender pay gap in several eu countries, entitled 'ending the gender pay gap', we have the opportunity to read a report on the subject. once again, we can also lament the inequalities in the labour market. the existence of a pay gap between men and women for the same work is a fact. it is worth mentioning that women's wages are on average 16.4% lower than men's wages across europe. in some countries, the gender pay gap is even wider. this disparity has a significant impact on career earnings and women's pensions. lower wages mean lower pensions and increase the risk of poverty for older women. it is good that the european parliament considers the elimination of the gender pay gap as a political priority.
in writing. - it would seem that there should no longer be any problems in europe with equal pay for men and women for equal work or work of equal value. but the facts are different. in the european union, the average female wage is 16.4% lower than that of men. the problem is that the report of the commission on women's rights and equality acknowledges these unfortunate facts without presenting any concrete proposals to change the situation. i think it would be particularly important to change the working conditions of those women who have chosen to become mothers. their working conditions and working hours should be much more flexible and the principle of equal pay for men and women doing the same work should be strictly respected. such a policy is not only in the interest of women but also reflects the principle of justice and would, above all, have an impact on the increase in the birth rate in europe and the rapid ageing of our continent.
in writing. - i consider the swiss decision to be discriminatory and illegal. the reintroduction of quantitative restrictions on long-term residence permits for eu citizens who are nationals of one of the eight member states that joined the eu in 2004 (which limits the free movement of persons provided for in the 1999 eu agreement) has no legal basis. the safeguard clause in article 10 of the 1999 agreement, to which the swiss authorities refer, does not provide for any distinction on grounds of nationality. the swiss authorities should withdraw the application of the safeguard clause immediately.
in writing. - the resolution shows that the ep is able to take a very consistent position in situations where eu citizens are discriminated against, including poles. our aim is to send a signal that we do not accept their unequal treatment by third countries.

fundamental necessity for the eu, but also a major challenge. we have made progress in strengthening our policies within the eu. at the same time, a stronger and more assertive external energy policy approach – it is a first step in improving transparency on such agreements. the mandatory submission of existing igas having an impact on the internal market for energy, the confirmation that the negotiated agreements with eu legislation, are all likely to further compliance and consistency with internal market rules, legal certainty for investors and, not least, solidarity among member and products, and energy efficiency. this is important because of the role that energy plays in the overall political and economic relations with many of our partner countries, and because of the transformations we have seen in the energy field. i thank parliament for addressing this in the report. i would also like to take this opportunity to thank the european parliament, in particular the committee on industry, research and energy and its rapporteur edit herczog, for its supportive contribution in this policy area. the report discussed today contains many important points, which the madam president! we regularly encounter cases of illegal arms trade. the apparent lack of transparency, of concrete international legal solutions to the transfer of conventional arms or their components, is a direct route to political instability and fuelling armed conflicts, as well as terrorist attacks and the rise of organised crime groups. all of these factors cause unnecessary loss of life and suffering to millions of citizens around the world. as virtually all countries in the world are involved in the arms trade and its value is systematically increasing despite the crisis, it is necessary to regulate this area at global level. i therefore support the resolution's key call for swift negotiations and the urgent adoption and launching of a comprehensive un treaty on this matter. however, regardless of their outcome, the european union should consistently support efforts to stabilise the arms trade through diplomatic efforts, consultations and information policy.
madam president! the arms trade is one of the great moral problems of civilized nations. on the one hand, the production of arms is a vital factor in the economies of many individual member states of the european union, it is the source of many jobs, because we know that arms are simply necessary - democratic countries need these weapons to protect themselves against the evil that still exists in our world. on the other hand, we are aware that today the arms trade is also, to a large extent, the source of income for dictatorships of all kinds, terrorist organizations, organizations which are simply bandits. that is why global control of the arms trade seems to be a necessary thing and why i have wholeheartedly supported this resolution.

in writing. − the current economic crisis, which has a huge impact not only on the eu but also on the world economy as a whole, has contributed significantly to the slowdown in economic growth. for the time being, the european community is trying to combat the economic downturn. but the effects of this struggle vary from country to country. the eu's peripheral countries, the so-called pigs, are the worst hit so far: portugal, italy, greece and spain, and ireland, and cyprus is also increasingly being mentioned. the growing budget deficits and the rise in the yields of individual countries' bonds (greece's bonds have already reached almost 30%) as well as the problems of banks have led the above-mentioned countries to turn to the european institutions for financial assistance. these actions have led the authorities in brussels to introduce greater economic and budgetary surveillance of these countries that require funding to fight the crisis. the so-called 'double-track' rules, which strengthen the commission's control over national budgets, will give the european commission a very large role in shaping these budgets. i think that in the long run, the transfer of increasing powers to a single authority can be a very dangerous phenomenon. i believe that the lower the decision on budgetary expenditure, the more effectively it is implemented. moreover, the proposed solution is overdue and will not meet the expectations set for it. that's why i'm voting against it.
in writing. − the draft legislation put to the vote today continues the process of deepening the economic integration of the euro area member states and significantly improves the economic governance system. strengthening budgetary surveillance and the role of the commission in that surveillance, in particular with regard to countries with an excessive deficit procedure, and harmonising and increasing the transparency of the budgetary adoption process in euro area countries, will contribute to enhancing the credibility of national fiscal policies, which will improve economic coordination in the euro area and safeguard it against further shocks in the future. at the same time, it should be noted that the benefits of the possible implementation of the proposals in question will not materialise in the short term. therefore, we should not stop looking for solutions on a day-to-day basis. one such solution is certainly the debt amortisation fund. the creation of such a structure would imply an indirect mutualisation of the public debt of euro area member states, which would, in turn, reduce market pressures and ease the refinancing conditions for these countries. nevertheless, because of the significance of the implications, this idea still needs to be elaborated and analysed in depth.
in writing. - ladies and gentlemen! the european union has never before had such economic and financial problems. the economic slowdown, rising unemployment and the growing budget deficits of individual member states (the biggest problem currently facing greece, with increasingly worrying signals coming from spain) have led the european institutions to try to use the situation to some extent to increase their (already large) competences. i am referring to the european commission. the proposal to monitor budgetary plans and ensure the correction of excessive deficits in euro area member states serves this purpose. suffice it to mention the so-called "two-pack". of course, countries that apply for financial aid should be subject to closer scrutiny. however, the commission's proposed action is not in the interests of democracy and is designed to make the community countries more and more dependent on brussels. i think that's not going to meet the expectations. that's why i'm voting against it.

draft opinion of the committee on the internal market and consumer protection - mr president! the amendments to the seveso ii directive are due to the need to adapt to the clp regulation and not to the increased number of serious accidents, so i fully agree that there is no need to change the seveso ii system. however, as a member of parliament with an opinion, i consider it particularly important to supplement and clarify the provisions on community information or consultation and participation in decision-making. it is very important that this information is complete and correct. the point is not to flood the public with information it does not need, but to provide accurate and understandable information. community information is a very important part of building trust, but also of educating the public on how to behave in the event of a major accident. the seveso ii directive is based on annex i, which is an essential element in defining the scope of the directive. therefore, amendments to this annex should be introduced by the ordinary legislative procedure and here i agree with the lead rapporteur.
madam president! the amendment of the seveso ii directive is a necessary step towards more effective prevention of disasters such as those in italy, france and japan, which have claimed many lives. they have caused damage to public and private property and environmental damage, costing billions of euros. this directive is important because it imposes obligations on operators and member states' authorities to prevent and mitigate the effects of accidents. the european union should systematically strengthen its inspection and risk analysis rules. the revision of this directive will improve coordination of legislation and thus put an end to unnecessary duplication of controls. at the same time, it is worth emphasizing that special supervision should be given to subcontractors, as they are often negligent, as we saw in hudson bay. the european parliament, as the representative of the citizens, should be able to be fully involved in this decision-making process, and i therefore support the rapporteur's view that changes to existing regulations should be made through the ordinary legislative procedure. parliament should also be regularly informed by the commission of industrial accidents and their response. the public must also have easy access to transparent and reliable information on hazards and how to deal with them in the event of an accident. the internet is an effective tool for raising awareness. they should be used as soon as possible, starting with an information campaign on the new classification of toxicity and the risks to life of the substances.

in writing. the ries report has fulfilled its primary function of providing consumers with relevant information on food for special uses and food for infants and young children. the qualification and labelling of key foods for certain population groups such as infants and young children and patients requiring specialised dietary nutrition have been clarified. the inclusion of gluten-free foods, foods used in low-calorie and very-low-calorie diets and the exclusion from the composition of food categories of substances with potentially harmful effects on the health of the population concerned are particularly valuable. particular attention should be paid to the provisions concerning foods for low birth weight infants or premature infants who cannot be fed on breast milk or standard formulae. such food will have to comply with the requirements applicable to food for special medical purposes. a major change also concerns the recommendation to limit the use of pesticide residues in formulae intended for the feeding of infants and young children. the implementation of these provisions will have consequences for the operators involved in the production of such foodstuffs in the form of the need to change their labelling. the commission has prepared transitional periods to allow the use of packaging labelled in accordance with the applicable rules. this report will contribute to the health of european society, reduce administrative burdens and promote fair competition between businesses across the union.
