the next item is the report by rodi kratsa-tsagaropoulou, on behalf of the committee on economic and monetary affairs, on the attractiveness of investing in europe (2011/2288(ini)) (a7-0190/2012).
mr. chairman, please! europe remains an important destination for foreign direct investment. but there is a growing emphasis on developing countries in the fight for investor attention. so how can we fight to keep europe's position as a strong place to invest? the main advantage of the european market is a stable and predictable business and legal environment. economic activity in europe is very well regulated compared to some parts of the world, and the orderly political situation guarantees the possibility of conducting business in stable conditions. another major asset of the member states is the high quality of their human capital. then what's the problem? in europe, there is a growing emphasis on socially responsible business, which, in addition to the general objective of increasing shareholder value, also focuses on environmental, environmental and social issues. these requirements are very expensive. but to compete for investors' money, we need to keep our financial system so that banks can continue to finance investments in times of uncertainty. investors are concerned about europe's low growth, its accumulated debt and its high tax rates.

in writing. six months ago the then newly elected danish prime minister helle thorning-schmidt presented the priorities of the danish presidency for the first half of 2012 to the european parliament. today, looking back at copenhagen, we can congratulate denmark on its successes in many areas, such as the eu budget, the union's multiannual financial framework for 2012-2020, climate policy and energy. the commission has also been asked to provide a report on the implementation of the new legislation in the member states. as rapporteur for the report on the lawful use of orphan works, i can only speak of the positive experience gained from this cooperation. however, the recent moves by the danish presidency on the proposed schengen reform in the context of the possibility of reintroducing border controls by the member states have caused a great deal of stir in europe, in particular the proposal to deprive the parliament of its existing right to vote and participate in the relevant legislative procedure. the case will be further examined by the next presidency, but it has cast a shadow over the perception of the danish eu presidency's achievements. in conclusion, given that the danish presidency has been in a difficult political period in the union, linked to the economic crisis and the financial difficulties of the successive member states with which cyprus will now have to contend the balance of the copenhagen achievements seems positive.
mr president, important steps have been taken in the right direction and growth packages welcomed, and stabilisation measures for the euro debt crisis are coupling both flexibility and conditionality. the move towards banking union is to be welcomed, and the road map for genuine monetary union is a good starting point. however, closer integration should preserve the unity and integrity of the union of 27 and its single market. agreed initial measures – some would say half-measures – should evolve into full measures of banking, fiscal and political union. measures addressed to the eu of 17 only – some would say half-union solutions – should evolve and be open for all members, at least those which are willing. we should avoid being satisfied with half measures for a half union. we should not accept the logic of differentiation and a two-speed integration of the eu. eurozone ‘ins’ and future ‘ins’ are and should remain in the same boat. only those who opt out should practise derogations. advanced integration of 17 at the expense of the disintegration of 27 is not an acceptable solution. we need an inclusive, not exclusive, format. we should preserve and cherish a single institutional framework and avoid having 17 restricted institutions in parallel, separate for ‘ins’ and ‘pre-ins’, resulting in interinstitutional cleavages. we should avoid two-level solidarity, two parallel budgets and double macro-economic standards. collateral political damage done to the european project by half-europe anti-crisis measures would be great. there is huge potential for growth in the eu maintaining integral economic and political unity. unravelling this unity will not bring us closer to winning the battle with the crisis.
in writing. the continuing rise in unemployment is the most dramatic indicator of the difficulties facing europe. i therefore consider the elements of the council conclusions directly linked to the promotion of employment and entrepreneurship to be crucial. i consider the national employment plans to be an important step towards the effective implementation of reforms that will improve the situation on the labour market, especially with regard to young people. i believe that linking national strategies with the initiatives contained in the employment package offers a chance to improve the situation. i also think that further removal of barriers in the area of the single market, agreements on a fund to support social entrepreneurship and progress on the recognition of qualifications are very important. i also share the view that both the european union and the member states should make a determined effort to reduce administrative burdens and move from over-regulation to so-called smart regulation.
in writing. the june european council made ambitious declarations on reforming the institutional architecture of the euro area. however, the importance of the summit in strengthening the zone will only be shown by the determination to implement its decisions. member states supported the proposal to create a common banking supervision for the euro area. this is a very ambitious challenge, given both the time horizon set for the end of october 2012 and the prolonged negotiation process on the supervisory requirements for the banking sector under the crd4/crr package. the arrangements for the conditions for granting financial assistance to the member states are also important. among other things, it was decided that italian bonds would be bought back through the european rescue funds, but without the application of strict monitoring programmes. in addition, it was guaranteed that the loans from the funds to spain would not have the status of non-subordinated debt, which should increase the confidence and demand of private investors in the debt market. the spectacular declarations made at the summit caused financial markets to react enthusiastically, even though the level of rescue funds remained unchanged. i believe that the creation of a common supervisor and a bank recapitalisation fund will strengthen financial stability in the euro area. the new institutions could, in a crisis situation, follow the example of the us federal institutions following the collapse of lehman brothers in 2008, by rapidly recapitalising financial institutions in order to counteract the contagion effect.
mr. chairman, please! the successful functioning of the baltic sea macro-region and the strategy for the baltic sea macro-region bring tangible benefits to the union as a whole. this is achieved through the interaction of partners at national, regional and local levels, which allows for precise priorities and effective implementation. cooperation offers a number of opportunities in the field of cohesion policy, also promoting activities in the area of services and labour. this strategy has often allowed for the complementarity of investments to be increased, thereby stimulating the development of the macro-region. similarly, the mediterranean basin has enormous potential, but its vastness requires a coordinated policy from all the parties involved. the dynamics of such a macro-region can be a great driver of the european economy. in supporting the resolution, i am in favour of including macro-regional strategies in the budgetary planning process. the activities outside the scope of cohesion policy, such as cooperation with third countries, seem particularly relevant here. by drawing on the experience of the baltic macro-region, we will have a recipe for developing similar initiatives.
mr. chairman, please! innovation and the unhindered development of new technologies are possible on the basis of respect for intellectual property rights. their proper protection is essential to compete effectively on world markets and to enable european products to compete with their foreign counterparts. the cost of piracy to european businesses, estimated at over a quarter of a trillion euros a year, alone requires a strong response. in addition, the trade in counterfeit food, personal hygiene products and medicines can have serious consequences for the general public. recently, we were shocked by the use of road salt in food products. the report finds that counterfeit goods for private use are also in violation of the law. in this context, the definition of the activities related to the so-called small consignment is of key importance. the clarifications on the treatment of suspect goods from outside the community give hope for a more effective policy also in resolving disputes in the wto. i support the resolution.
in writing. − the 2009 directive (2009/138/ec) on the taking-up and pursuit of the business of insurance and reinsurance provides a common regulatory framework for the european union as a whole for the risk management and supervision of insurance and reinsurance undertakings, which is appropriate to the level of development of modern financial markets. this directive is important from the point of view of the security and stability of the financial system, as it strengthens the supervisory framework for the insurance sector. it also introduces mechanisms to make the insurance sector better support the real economy by encouraging long-term investment. however, in january 2011 the need to update the directive arose as a result of a change in the institutional architecture of european supervision. therefore, the second consolidated directive contains provisions on the postponement of the date of transposition and the date of application of the 2009 directive. however, the complexity of the proposal for a second package directive means that the legislative process will not be completed before the date of application of directive 2009/138/ec. i support the proposal to change the date for transposition of the solvency ii directive, as this will avoid too burdensome legislative obligations for member states and will allow better preparation of the new system envisaged in the proposal for a second single directive. the complexity and economic importance of the proposed regulation also require that supervisors and insurance and reinsurance undertakings be given a sufficiently long period of time to prepare themselves to operate under the new regulatory conditions.
in writing. - i am positive about the european parliament's directive on the taking-up and pursuit of the business of insurance and reinsurance. those rules are necessary for the safe and sound functioning of the insurance sector. it is important that insurance undertakings and their supervisors adopt a package guaranteeing the solvency of insurers. this will increase legal certainty for citizens and businesses. however, the date of entry into force of a new union directive on this matter cannot be postponed continuously. in my view, this directive should ultimately apply from 1 january 2014 in order to eliminate its temporary character.

in writing. − macro-regional strategies open up new perspectives for territorial cooperation projects based on cohesion policy and offer more effective solutions to the economic and environmental problems of the area. the positive effects of this strategy can be seen in the baltic sea macro-region, which was created in 2009. i think that the same should be true in southern europe. the mediterranean region is home to 500 million people, of whom only one third live in the european union. the european union is also committed to the development of a common policy on the mediterranean, which is based on the principles of the treaty of rome and the treaty of rome. i believe that the dynamics of development around the mediterranean can be a driving force for the whole european economy. that is why i voted for this report.
in writing. − the introduction of macro-regional strategies offers many opportunities. they contribute to faster territorial development, increase social and economic cohesion, focus on the challenges and problems of the region and highlight the role of urban-rural links. they also represent an innovative form of interregional and transnational european cooperation, which contributes to greater coherence and coordination of policies across sectors, promotes job creation and ensures sustainable growth. finally, macro-regional strategies are about building fruitful and concrete relations in the eu's neighbourhood policy, sharing good practices and making progress based on territorial development. i am a strong supporter of the creation of new macro-regional strategies and i hope that in the near future new macro-regions will be created, including the carpathian euroregion. that is why i voted in favour of the report drawn up by mr françois alphonse. thank you. thank you.

in writing. − the creation of a single european railway area undoubtedly opens up many opportunities across the eu, thanks to the harmonisation of member states' rules. i would like to thank all those involved in the preparation of the ep's position. in the context of the amendment to article 2 (2a) which i support, i would like to draw attention to the fact that the creation of exceptions to the general rule is not necessarily contrary to the european interest. all the eu institutions point to the need to create new jobs, help small and medium-sized enterprises, and create special conditions for areas with reduced competitiveness and peripheral areas. in this context, i would like to justify the vote on this report and the amendment in question. i do not understand why the idea of creating a unified railway area would have to cancel the activities of a smaller and at the same time profitable company providing numerous jobs in 4 regions of poland characterized by high unemployment.

in writing. - the adoption of the amendment to the first railway package will make it possible to improve international rail transport. it is of the utmost importance that the railway market is regulated efficiently. this should benefit passengers and companies involved in the transport of goods and passengers. it is concerned, however, that the rejection of the provision exempting the polish broad-strait steelworks (lhs) from certain provisions of the directive. the lhs is the longest broad gauge railway line in the european union. it runs for 400 km from the polish-ukrainian border crossing in hrubieszow to the silesian railway station sławków lhs. the non-electrified single-track route with a russian track gauge is unusual on a union scale and the general package notes are not adapted to it. i regret that most meps have not shown an understanding of the specific nature of this railway. the final text of the revised railway package may have a negative impact on the functioning of lhs, which employs 1300 people. however, in view of the other provisions of the package, which i regard as positive, i have decided to vote in favour of the amendment. it is a document which is favourable to the development of the international rail transport market.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the document today, but i very much regret that the amendment to article 2 (2) tabled by the four political groups: epp, ecr, epp and gue/ngl on the exclusion of broad-gauge railways from the scope of the first railway package has been rejected. in order to ensure free competition on the railway market, we must bear in mind that in some member states there are self-financing railway lines which do not connect to the national and european network, are of regional importance and have a width different from that of the dominant network in the country concerned. the need to apply all the provisions of the directive to those separate lines would impose disproportionate and irrational burdens and would distort and misrepresent the purpose for which they were built. while we are talking about deregulation and the pursuit of a growth europe, we cannot, through the reckless implementation of legislation, impede the functioning of well-functioning businesses, which represent the real, and often the only, added value in the poor regions of the eu.
in writing. - i spoke in the plenary debate, expressing my reservations about the recommendations on a single railway area in the european union. unfortunately, my vote, as well as that of several other polish meps, did not win the support of the majority of the parliament. the recommendations that have been put to the vote, in my view, are an attempt to put the railway market in europe in order in a mechanical way. i think it is wrong not to take into account the specificities of countries such as poland, where the general introduction of competition on the rails could in effect lead to the collapse of the polish state railways. we need more time and more resources to adapt to modern rail transport solutions. competition can and should be encouraged, but only if all players in the market have the same opportunities to compete. with persistent disparities, especially in the quality of the rolling stock, the weaker partner always loses.
in writing. - pkp linia hutnicza szerokotorowa operates in the railway transport sector and is also the infrastructure manager of the almost 400 km section of the railway line. pkp lhs's capital expenditure in the period 2001-2010 amounted to pln 386,3 million. lhs spent pln 421,8 million on renovations during this period. these funds were from the company's own resources, which enabled it to adapt successfully to changing market conditions. the lhs ctr, which as a line is directly connected to non-eu countries and their broadband transport system, should be excluded from the rules on the single railway area. i support maintaining the 12th amendment to article 2 adopted last november and therefore maintaining the integrated operations of lhs. this amendment was adopted by a vote of two to one in parliament and by the same vote in the commission. unfortunately, parliament succumbed to pressure from the commission and the council and rejected the amendment. i therefore oppose the whole report, which could deepen the collapse of rail transport in some countries of the european union.
in writing. − at any given time, an average of around 45 000 vehicles are in breach of eu tachograph rules. it is easy to imagine the consequences of such a state of affairs. failure to respect minimum breaks and rest periods and maximum driving times contributes to an increase in the number of tired drivers and poses a risk to road safety. i believe that effective solutions should be developed at eu and member state level. member states should undertake to enforce this regulation more strictly. at eu level, the harmonisation of the training of control officers throughout europe and the need to validate the relevant technical skills by passing an examination appear to be very important. i support this report.
in writing. − since 1969, the european union has been establishing social legislation in the field of road transport to improve road safety and the working conditions of drivers and to ensure fair competition between transport companies. at the same time, the union has developed a comprehensive strategy for the control and verification of compliance with social legislation relating to road transport. however, social rules are still too often broken and the tachograph system is not effective enough. i therefore agree with the rapporteur that the commission should present a harmonised interpretation of regulation no 561/2006 and the necessary technical specifications so that tachographs are not only monitoring devices but also facilitate compliance by drivers and hauliers.
in writing. − i have voted in favour of the resolution on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending council regulation (eec) no 3821/85 on recording equipment in road transport and amending regulation (ec) no 561/2006 of the european parliament and the council (com(2011)0451 – c7-0205/2011 – 2011/0196(cod)). in doing so i hope to continue and even improve upon the safety for travellers on the road. as we all know road transportation is a vital asset to the european market and allows all of us to move freely from one member state to the next. it is important that we address any or all safety issues that may infringe on transportation. i feel that a revised training program for the member states as well as the use of technology to enforce the drive time provisions will allow for safer and more efficient transport. the unfair gains made by those who violate the drive time provision do to the lack of technology need to stop. i support the rapporteur in her statement, that without complete cooperation by the member states this regulation too will fall short of its goal of protecting road safety.
in writing. − intellectual property law has recently become a hot topic as a priority of the europe 2020 strategy. on 24 may 2011, the european commission adopted a communication entitled 'a single market for intellectual property rights'. this was the start of initiatives that include a new regulation on the enforcement of intellectual property rights by customs authorities, to replace the existing regulation 1383/2003/ec later this year. it's an important topic, and in light of the acta fight, it's become very popular in the public. the fight against counterfeiting is becoming increasingly difficult, with the annual cost to european businesses of piracy and counterfeit goods estimated at €250 billion. between 2009 and 2010, the number of counterfeit goods doubled from 43 572 to 79 112 cases registered by customs at the eu border. the increase in illegal shipments was particularly marked, as 200% of the shipments were linked to online sales, of which more than 69% contained counterfeit medicines that were so dangerous to the health of consumers. the problem is real and must be tackled at the border to prevent these goods from entering the european market. i support the idea of an accelerated procedure enabling customs authorities to prevent the movement of these goods if they are suspected of being counterfeit, but excluding sanctions for consumers and travellers and their luggage and packages for the exclusive use of consumers weighing less than 2 kg. consumers should be protected, but they should also be able to access commercial offers freely without fear of accidental infringement. the commission's proposal is a good first step towards protecting european intellectual property and a sensible alternative to acta.
in writing. − it is high time to take significant action to protect intellectual property in the field of trademarks. we already have a lot of legislation in this area, so the changes proposed should take into account the complexity of the current situation. the protection of intellectual property rights is of particular importance in the context of the far-reaching opening up of the european market and the recognition of innovation as the main means of economic development. counterfeit products are a grey area effect they are not subject to customs controls or do not meet the applicable standards for the required quality standards and therefore health and safety criteria. protecting intellectual property rights and reducing counterfeiting will help level the playing field, increase employment and tax revenues. in international trade, special arrangements are required for the consignment of medicinal products. intellectual property also has a broader formula which is difficult to understand in conjunction with the free common market. further action and solutions are needed in this regard. protecting intellectual property rights is not just about fighting counterfeiting. all of this requires a public information campaign.
in writing. − water is a natural resource, and its abundance may be a future strength for a country. fresh water is scarce, and many people are already struggling to access it. and yet it is essential for both functioning and development. the european union should therefore do its utmost to develop the most effective 'plan for protecting europe's water resources'. a policy of sound management of these resources is key to the continent's sustainable development and food security. investing in new water extraction and recovery technologies is also an investment in world peace. because unfortunately, water could be another resource that causes wars to break out. it is equally important to educate european citizens from an early age on how to conserve and manage water. the european union should therefore do its utmost to promote all investments and initiatives aimed at safeguarding water resources.
in writing. − water is undoubtedly the most important of all public goods and despite the fact that europe collects only 13% of its available water resources overall, the geographical distribution of resources is very uneven and many european countries and regions suffer from severe water scarcity. europe's and the world's freshwater resources are at risk if they are not managed sustainably. factors such as urbanization, population growth, overconsumption, biological and chemical pollution have a negative impact on the availability and quality of safe water resources. i support the publication of the 'european water plan' planned for november 2012. i believe that europe should take a clear position on this issue also in the context of the upcoming sustainable development conference rio+20. remember, over 800 million people still do not have access to safe drinking water. however, i voted against this report because of the fact that it mentions the serious threat to both surface and groundwater caused by shale gas exploration and extraction. i don't agree with that.

in writing. - mr president, the 112 service is an excellent tool in emergency situations. it is available, or at least should be, on all telephone equipment in every member state. however, victims of road accidents are often unable to inform the relevant services themselves. the ecall system has therefore been designed to provide the most relevant information on the accident by itself as a vehicle equipment. unfortunately, the work on implementing the system, which has been going on for almost a decade, is still not producing results. i therefore fully support the acceleration of both the administrative and technological aspects of the full deployment of ecall in the union as soon as possible. i believe it will significantly improve the efficiency of the emergency services by reducing the risk of loss of life and health of those injured. it will also allow for efficient reorganisation of traffic in the area of the accident. this service must be free of charge, public and available to all vehicles, regardless of brand. the system will also bring administrative benefits in terms of reducing the medical costs of the consequences of accidents and the risk of secondary collisions hampering road capacity. i support the resolution.
in writing. - today i voted in favour of a report calling for the mandatory installation of ecall in new vehicles by car manufacturers from 2015. i think this is a good idea, because reducing the time taken for medical aid to arrive at the scene of a car accident is extremely important and will help save the lives of many europeans, poles and opoleans.
in writing. − the benefits of ecall are to reduce the medical consequences of an accident, to reduce the risk of another accident in the same place and to reduce the impact of an accident on road traffic. the golden hour principle means that if emergency services are notified immediately of an accident and know its location, they can arrive quickly, reducing the risk of death and serious injury. for this system to work, we will need cooperation between vehicle manufacturers, mobile network operators and member states. the latter will be required to upgrade their accident reporting points to handle ecall notifications. let us not forget that this will involve considerable expense. another important element that needs to be carefully worked out is the protection of personal data. we have rightly emphasised that the ecall system must not allow the vehicle to be traced under any circumstances, which means that it must be a sleeping system until the alarm is triggered. ecall services shall not be used in any case to monitor or analyse the movements of a person or to determine his or her whereabouts if there has been no accident. i voted for this report.
in writing. − the more effective implementation of the eu-wide ecall service will improve road safety. the motor vehicles would have a system for automatically alerting the emergency services, which is particularly important when the accident participants lose consciousness. the rapid arrival of qualified and well-equipped aid would help to reduce the still high number of fatalities. in my view, however, we must be concerned about the lack of progress in the voluntary implementation of this service by individual member states, as is the case with the delays in the smooth functioning of the european emergency number 112, on which the ecall project in question is to be based. the commission, parliament and the council need to take action to establish such a public service across the eu, provided that it is functional, low-cost and accessible to all vehicle owners. at the same time, it is necessary to adopt legal arrangements so that the creation of an eu-wide ecall system does not in any way lead to a restriction of the civil rights of vehicle users (e.g. by being traceable) or to a breach of the guarantees of protection of their personal data.

in writing. the acta treats three important issues: 1) the commercial right to use a trademark; 2) the rights of internet users to move around in the digital environment (article 27); 3) the rights of creators to benefit financially from the marketing of their works. while the first and third questions are not particularly problematic, although they require clarification, article 27 (1) to (8) can raise many doubts, in particular paragraph 4 which requires an internet service provider to infringe the right to protection of personal data. point 6 is unacceptable, since it refers to the circumvention of an 'effective technical measure' and of devices which 'mainly', but not exclusively, serve that purpose by means of the 'computer programmes' contained therein. i would like to recall that in 2005 the ep rejected at second reading the report of the legal affairs committee on the 'patentability of computer-aided inventions'. this means that computer programs cannot be patented and that the big computer companies cannot prevent our european computer scientists from using their equipment to develop new, innovative computer programs, also for use on the internet. this would inhibit innovation, for example in new it applications. the obvious issue of counterfeiting needs to be separated from acta and copyright and protection on the internet needs to be addressed in detail, but with the condition that the internet is open source.

in writing. − as we well know, the issue on how decisions authorising certain products and substances are taken (by means of delegated or implementing acts) is a horizontal one. in case of organic farming products the authorisation procedure is even more general, because there is no application by individual operators. authorisations are done in a general manner by the commission upon a request of a member state. the commission has proposed in article 16(1) and 21(1) to authorise these substances by means of delegated acts. although parliament supported this position, the council has changed these provisions to implementing acts. the position of the european parliament in the third reading on art. 16 and 21 was to move the list of substances into annexes of the basic act which will then be modified by the ordinary legislative procedure. the ecr is in favour of the committee's approach of supporting the use of delegated acts in as many instances as possible. for this reason, i voted in favour of this report.

in writing. − with the entry into force of the lisbon treaty, the current legislative procedure, known as comitology, has been replaced by a system of delegated and implementing acts. the european commission may adopt non-legislative acts of minor importance, supplementing or modifying existing legal acts by means of delegated acts. implementing acts, on the other hand, apply to legislation which must be implemented in all member states under uniform conditions. for us as meps, the european parliament's involvement in decision-making and monitoring of the implementation of legislation is of the utmost importance. we have more privileges in this case through delegated acts, where we can set out the conditions under which the ec can implement the law (in the case of implementing acts, the ep is in a sense 'removed' from further work after the decision has been taken). i therefore believe that we should aim to qualify as many dossiers as possible as delegated acts, which will allow us to continue to have a view and control over the projects adopted. this, of course, involves an additional administrative burden and may require an increase in the ep's 'labour force', i.e. the employment of legal experts and other staff who can take care of the adaptation of our daily work to the new procedures.

in writing. - the eu exports $9 billion worth of car parts to russia. investors opening automotive plants in russia in the initial period (this is the infant industry) are periodically exempted from the general wto rules due to high initial costs and lack of competitiveness. this means that the russian party which is a wto member may apply protective tariffs on a transitional basis. however, excessive extension of this period and the use of economies of scale by russian producers, for example by expanding the market to kazakhstan and belarus, may lead to a decrease in imports from the union and, consequently, to the delocalisation of production. in order to prevent this, the transitional agreement provided for a compensatory mechanism whereby russia, when importing these parts and assemblies from the union, would reduce the duty rate by the amount of any decrease in these imports when they exceed 3% of certain thresholds. on the other hand, the factories were or are still subsidised by the state, which may artificially increase their competitiveness. hence the need for a compensatory mechanism. this is also a signal to union producers to invest in innovation or, for example, to increase the said economies of scale during the transition period. the agreement is beneficial for eu industry and that is why i voted in favour of it. it would be good if the eu customs zone could follow russia's example and defend the eu economy more effectively.

now. it was mentioned by mr gerbrandy that the eu was isolated. it is really an interesting thing to look at the international stage and see that we, who are in the deepest crisis economically and absolute fact in politics. i think it is important that we start to focus more on the basics of the green economy, on the fact that we should take natural capital into consideration. so the role of in writing. − in view of the partial renewal of the composition of the court of justice and the consequent urgent need to find a solution which would enable the civil service tribunal to function properly, i considered it necessary to adopt the proposed amendments to the statute concerning the organisation of the tribunal and the civil service tribunal. that's why i voted yes.
in writing. - since the accession of the new member states the european court of justice is faced with a problem of limited staff resources in relation to the number of cases that are brought before it. the number of cases reported to the ets is increasing systematically and in 2011 was 11,3% higher than the previous year. the court of justice has also established that the principle of equal treatment applies to all judges of the supreme court, including those who are appointed by the president of the republic. this situation leads to considerable delays in the work of the court, where as many as 1323 cases were pending until 12 october last year. i therefore support the proposal by ets for a regulation which would allow the appointment of ad interim judges to the european union civil service tribunal. the court proposed that, at the request of the president of the court of justice, the council of the european union draw up a list of three persons to serve as ad interim judges for a period of four years, chosen from among former members of the cjeu. such judges would have the powers of a judge only in respect of the cases to which they are assigned, but would not have the right to participate in the administration of the court or in the election of the president of the court or the presidents of chambers. the additional costs resulting from such a solution would be relatively small, as these judges would only receive a salary of 1/30 of the salary of a permanent judge for each day of work. i support the court's proposal because, although this will increase the costs in the budget for next year, ensuring effective legal protection and the possibility of speeding up judicial processes should be a priority for the proper functioning of the union.
in writing. − in view of the growing need to regulate the rules of operation of ad interim judges of the european union civil service tribunal. in view of the circumstances which justify their appointment, i consider that the remuneration of ad interim judges and the termination of their duties should also be regulated. that's why i voted yes.
in writing. − achieving sustainable economic growth is facilitated by modern and efficient infrastructure. its development is also directly linked to the expansion of the internal market and the creation of more jobs. it is estimated that investment in transport, energy and telecommunications will cost around €1.5 trillion over the next decade. on this basis, the solutions proposed by the commission are therefore aimed at attracting private sector investors. such solutions should always be approached with great caution. i therefore welcome the introduction of a six-month pilot programme as a test run for all the capital instruments linked to the europe 2020 strategy. this will allow the degree of acceptance of these activities by the capital markets to be determined and the functioning of the project bond system to be checked. i voted in favour of the report to support the pilot phase, but my position on the whole project, including the bond mechanism, is to be described as moderate and restrained.

in writing. − project bonds are an instrument that was created to finance projects under the connecting europe programme to create a transport, energy and digital network. it is worrying that investment in europe is declining, a process that started before the crisis. furthermore, the networks in the east are disconnected from the networks in the west and they need to be connected. the project bonds are intended to be an additional instrument for financing infrastructure investments, complementing the current financing system. the 2012 and 2013 years are to be a pilot phase for the bonds, with full operation in 2014. the objective of the pilot phase is to examine the reaction of financial markets to the new instrument. the introduction of project bonds could accelerate the implementation of infrastructure projects by facilitating the raising of private finance. the security of the bonds would ensure eu support. the risk mitigation could encourage different market players to invest in infrastructure projects. project bonds are not a substitute for grants. however, they are intended to complement them, ensuring that investments are financed more efficiently and more quickly. in addition to bonds, both private and public funds national and eu should continue to play a significant role.

vice-president of the commission. − madam president, honourable members, first let me congratulate the rapporteur, lara comi, and the members of the committee on the internal market and consumer protection – in particular its chair, malcolm harbour – for the excellent work which they have completed. you all know that standardisation is one of the major instruments underpinning the european economy. the cooperation between industry users, public authorities and the standardisation organisations in drawing up standards has contributed decisively to what i think you will all agree is one of europe’s greatest achievements: the internal market. standards play a vital role in enhancing the competitiveness of european enterprises; they assist access to today’s globalised markets and ensure interoperability, which is vital for competition and developing new products and services. for smes, standards are a key tool to help them retain and attract consumers. the reduced risk and increased trust and satisfaction flowing from the use of standards opens markets for them in a secure environment. precisely because of this importance, standardisation must adapt to the new societal changes that we face: the globalised economy, the need for sustainable development, the convergence of technologies protecting the consumer and improving accessibility and inclusion for disabled and elderly people. to address these issues, the commission adopted the standardisation package in june 2011, and i am glad to see that the european parliament is now discussing the adoption of the final piece of that package: the regulation on european standardisation. this regulation would help to address and solve three problems. first, the speed of mandated standardisation. the planning and transparency of commission mandates asking the european standardisation organisations to draw up standards in support of the legislation and policies will be improved through the annual work programme and by means of financial support. second, the inclusiveness of european standardisation. the opinion of relevant societal stakeholders is today not sufficiently integrated in the process, and this regulation will improve this representation of smes and societal stakeholders at both european and national level. the third element concerns public procurement. you know that many information and communication technology standards ensuring interoperability are elaborated not by the european standardisation organisations but by global forums and consortiums, and these specifications do not then fit into our categories of standards to which public authorities may refer in their calls for tender. this regulation will provide an evaluation procedure, after which public authorities will be able to use such ict specifications in public procurement provided they comply with a set of criteria based on the world trade organisation principles for the standardisation process. the regulation also affirms the existing possibility for the union to use service standardisation as a policy tool within harmonised service sectors. like so many in parliament, the commission regrets the council’s determination to impose bureaucratic comitology procedures on mandates which we think are both unjustified and will undermine the efficiency of the system due to their time-consuming nature. this is why we are going to make full use of the review clause inserted – thankfully – by parliament to evaluate the impact of comitology on mandates, with a view to making possible new proposals within two years. nevertheless, given that most of the key elements of the original proposal have been accepted, and in a spirit of compromise and in order to facilitate a first-reading agreement, the commission is willing to accept the text as agreed between parliament and the council.
draftsman of the opinion of the committee on industry, research and energy. - madam president! - what are you doing? the regulatory requirements for products, services and processes serve to standardise production, i.e. to achieve a scale effect, and also improve quality and promote the protection of health and safety of consumers. however, technical progress is outpacing the standard-setting processes, which leads to market conflicts. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's standards are properly applied and that they are applied in a timely manner. the removal of barriers to trade in goods and services between member states is of great importance, and this raises the need for harmonisation. standardization is a process in which the european institutions are complemented by national standardisation bodies. the commission's draft regulation, however, largely omits the latter, and there are no better mechanisms to create the appropriate link between the eu centre and the member states.

i would like to draw attention to the following fact: for several years now, the sulphur content of marine fuels has been systematically reduced. this is the right course to take, because it improves the quality of life and helps to protect the environment. this also applies to the baltic sea and the countries bordering it, i.e. also to poland. it is worth noting, however, that the reduction in sulphur content will be radical. a few years ago, the sulphur content of fuel was 1.5%, today it is 1%, and in a few years it is expected to be 0.1%, which is a tenfold decrease. this puts many european shipowners in a very difficult position and the cost of fuel, which must be higher to be of better quality, may reduce the competitiveness of transport. the commission has already taken a number of measures to help the shipowners, and this is the mission of the union and parliament.
mr. chairman, please! in reducing the sulphur content of marine fuels, we should seek a compromise between maintaining safe health standards and maintaining economic competition, especially for transport from non-european countries, such as third world countries, where fuel standards are significantly lower. we should therefore stick to the proposed sulphur threshold for fuel for ships coming to europe and give other countries until 2020 to raise their standards and make fuel less harmful. in addition, other emission limitations should also be addressed by the international maritime organisation. the current international arrangements on the sulphur content of marine fuel should be accepted and adopted by the european union.
in writing. with full understanding of the project to reduce sulphur dioxide emissions from marine fuels, i would like to express some doubts about this legislation. i am aware that the commission's calculations are clear: the ratio of the monetary value of the benefits to the cost of implementing this reform is to be between 2 and 25. i'm also aware of the fact that human health is priceless. however, while the benefits of this project will be felt by all citizens to a limited extent, the costs may be concentrated in transport and maritime industry centres. i happen to be from szczecin, the city most concerned about this. if it is true that the citizens of such cities are the ones who are to bear the burden of this directive, then serious consideration should be given to measures or instruments which would be designed to counteract such a situation. in addition, i would note that a tenfold reduction in emissions in the seca areas, which also include the baltic sea, would be expected as early as 2015. this raises the question of whether it is technically possible to provide sufficient fuel until then. i think these are serious enough objections to make us think about how we should vote on this directive.
in writing. i welcome the proposal to amend the environmental legislation. the fact that air pollution is caused by the sulphur content of marine fuels is a major problem, given the issue of existing solutions for sulphur emissions on land. i believe that we need to develop appropriate rules for maritime transport, so that the impact of emissions of pollutants is reduced in both the aquatic and terrestrial environment. the main challenge is to set stricter sulphur limits: within the sulphur emission control areas (seca) cuts to 0.1% by 2015 and outside the seca to 0.5% by 2020. tightening fuel standards and regulations on emission reduction methods is possible while respecting the principles of sustainable development. by promoting high environmental standards, europe will become more competitive. the expected environmental effects will be similar in northern and southern europe, so the limits should not differ significantly. the other important issue that we should not forget is that of passenger ships, which should be covered by stricter restrictions. we want to focus on providing equal opportunities for companies of all sizes, while respecting the environment and the principles of a sustainable economy. in order to avoid distortions of competition with third countries outside the european union, marine fuels exceeding the current maximum sulphur content of 3,5% may only be used by incoming ships, but i believe that this is only appropriate until 2020. from this year onwards, all vessels operating in european union waters must comply with the above rules. in order to ensure a smooth transition, programmes are provided to improve the implementation of emission reduction methods.
mr. chairman, please! the hard-won compromise solves many, but not all, of the problems associated with this directive. one of the outstanding issues is the issue of public procurement. i think that the energy efficiency criterion in public procurement must be clearly balanced by the price criterion. we cannot have high electricity bills today replaced by very high, unprofitable, unrecoverable bills for energy efficiency services and goods. i think our citizens are pretty indifferent to whether they're paying too much for electricity or paying too much in taxes for energy efficiency. the linking of energy efficiency with climate policy is a very damaging one. manual control, administrative adjustment of the emission allowance market simply because it produces unexpected effects is very bad news for entrepreneurs, hurts the profitability of business in the european union and undermines the legal certainty of trading in the european union.
in writing. as the report shows, top-down energy constraints are key to efficiency. this is an obvious mistake. the efficient use of primary energy depends on the efficiency and number of conversion processes, the activation and dynamics of combustion processes (i.e. decreasing the ignition temperature), the transmission efficiency and the ohm losses. objective 3x20 commits to real efficiency gains rather than consumption reductions. it is about stimulating innovation to achieve this, not about limitations, exclusions and price barriers. the greatest reserves of real efficiency lie in thermal upgrading, cogeneration, reducing energy consumption. member states shall measure their efficiency as primary energy consumption per capita in 2020 in relation to the reference year.
in writing. i believe that the directive we are discussing today gives a lot of flexibility to member states, industry and the public sector, while supporting the efforts of eu members to increase energy efficiency at all stages of the energy chain, from processing, through distribution, to final consumption. the energy efficiency index in the industrial sector decreased by 58% between 1995 and 2009, compared to 20% for the eu as a whole. this reflects a significant improvement in energy efficiency in the industry, which is well above the eu average. the provisions on the transition to high-efficiency cogeneration technology are an example of the flexibility of the compromise directive. all newly built or refurbished industrial installations must be equipped with a cogeneration system if a cost-benefit analysis shows that there is a benefit-to-benefit ratio. in addition, member states may decide to waive this requirement for industrial installations, on substantial grounds. increasing efficiency improvements will require huge investments in the short and medium term, as almost half of today's electricity generation capacity and cogeneration systems are over 30 years old. the need to conserve energy has been around for a long time. however, in both industry and households, there are always more important expenditures than the cost of energy efficiency. i hope that the directive will change our perspective and that the increased awareness will bring us closer to changing the situation.

in writing. − the report on the proposal for a directive of the european parliament and of the council on energy efficiency and repealing directives 2004/8/ec and 2006/32/ec examined several key issues that will determine the future of europe. the eu faces a huge challenge of increasing electricity demand, due to the development of new member states, among others. according to the international energy agency, poland will need 50 percent more energy in 15 years than it can produce today. the production of this quantity is hampered by the strict eu co2 emission standards and the need to deploy renewable energy technologies. europe also faces the challenge of increasing energy efficiency by 20% by the end of 2020 (european council conclusion of 4 february 2011). unfortunately, a number of internal and external factors, including the economic crisis and the competition in transport and heavy industry, are making it difficult to achieve this objective. we are facing a challenge that forces us to develop faster, with less damage to the environment, which is not easy to meet! outdated infrastructure and technologies are causing a lot of waste and high emissions, and to change that, investment is needed. in addition, instruments that would reduce energy consumption by citizens should be considered.
in writing. - i abstained on the energy efficiency directive. on the one hand, the legitimate objectives of reducing energy costs are presented, while on the other hand, a system of 'energy-efficient public procurement' is being created, for which the taxpayers will ultimately pay a very high price.
in writing. − although the commission was right to finally focus on energy efficiency after considering the market effects, the report did not address this issue. objective indicators are needed to measure both micro and macro-economic efficiency, i.e. the real gross efficiency of the member states. the latter should be measured by the growth rate as the difference between the primary energy consumption per unit of gdp per capita of the country from year to year divided by the output consumption per unit of gdp per capita, times 100 in percentage. energy policy, defined after the adoption of the right 3x20 political objective in 2007 by the member states, has been distorted by the climate and energy package. it introduces unfair competition, discriminating against countries whose energy mix is dominated by coal as a primary energy source. the package is not based on economic realities: member states are obliged to pursue different objectives simultaneously. the optimal, multi-stage, cost-effective approach to the 3x20 target is lacking. if not only the energy mix but also the policy objective is left to the member states, this will result in more primary energy being wasted and more co2 being emitted than is realistically possible. but it's a matter of trust, and we're seeing a crisis of trust. given the above arguments, i did not support the report.
in writing. − improving energy efficiency is one of the best ways to combat global warming. i am very positive about the measures taken so far to improve the energy efficiency of residential buildings. in the case of poland, support for building insulation or window replacement is one of the most visible signs of poland's membership of the european union. it is clearly viewed favourably by the public. i therefore welcomed the draft energy efficiency directive which requires member states to renew 3% of the total heated or cooled area of buildings owned or occupied by public authorities each year. i regret that parliament has failed to push through its proposal to renovate all public buildings, not just the central government buildings. on the other hand, the solution adopted is a major step forward in achieving the greenhouse gas reduction targets. crucially, the directive will close the gap between us and the target of 20% energy savings by 2020. now we can guarantee that we'll be able to reduce energy consumption by 15 percent. if the current rules were to continue, the realistic prospect would be only a 9% reduction. this is a result far below expectations and needs. in view of the above, i have decided to support the content of the energy efficiency report.

in writing. - in voting on the report, i had several important issues in mind, such as the introduction of a 0.1% content requirement in the seca area (i.e. the baltic sea, north sea and channel basin) from 2015. the mediterranean countries, on the other hand, are not to be subject to such tightening until 2020. we are thus creating a clear division between the north sea and the south sea, distorting competition in the european market. the data presented show that less sulphur fuels are definitely more expensive. the environmental objectives set may therefore not be met, as the increase in cycling is very likely in the event of a higher price of maritime transport. of course, it is possible to equip ships with scrubber exhaust systems, but, given the age of the fleet and the economic situation of countries such as poland, it would be completely unprofitable to install them. the alternative to conventional fuels is the use of lng in ships. it may only concern newly launched vessels due to the technologies used. in addition, a european network of ports where such fuel can be refuelled is needed.
in writing. - given the potential risks involved in implementing the provisions of this directive, i had to vote against it. i would like to stress, however, my understanding of the noble aims of the implementation of this document. however, while the positive impact of this directive on citizens is small, although it affects the majority of eu citizens, the negative effects will be felt by a smaller group of people, but in a more severe way. this is reflected, inter alia, in the fact that the transitional periods proposed in the directive are too short. this means that a large number of fuels meeting the new criteria will have to be rapidly supplied in a relatively short time. this may lead to temporary shortages of supplies, which will raise the price of fuel and reduce the competitiveness of maritime transport in relation to land transport. moreover, the price of marine fuel will increase due to the cost of the additional desulphurisation process, which will be included in the price of the fuel. these concerns are so serious that i have decided to oppose the directive.
in writing. − the international maritime organisation has established that from 2015 the maximum sulphur content in marine fuels in seca areas will be 0.1%. in europe, the seca areas are the north sea, the english channel and the baltic sea. the introduction of a 0,1% sulphur limit for all ships engaged in regular passenger services, as well as the extension of that limit to territorial seas, will result in significant additional costs for the operators concerned by that limit. in addition, the lowering of the sulphur limits may lead to the takeover of goods currently transported by sea by trucks. this will cause additional damage to the environment and congestion on the roads. that's why i voted for "we".

in writing. − in an age when the internet is the most widespread tool for work and entertainment, intellectual property law must keep pace with consumer needs and technological developments. improving services in the audiovisual sector, by supporting online services, is of great importance for promoting european civilisation, linguistic and cultural diversity. european broadcasters finance more than 80% of the production of original audiovisual content and play a key role in promoting the european creative industries. it is important to provide both rightholders and recipients of works with legal certainty in relation to copyright in the european digital space through greater coordination of the laws of the member states. we already have rules for the free movement of goods and services across the union, but paradoxically they do not apply to the digital space, which is precisely the core of freedom and freedom from barriers. that's got to change. the commission should ask digital businesses across the union to allow the purchase of digital services in a member state other than the consumer's country of origin. in order to better protect artists from the illegal sharing of their works online, we need to offer consumers a competitive alternative. as of today, approximately 35.8% of movies are downloaded illegally, and as much as 98.8% of data downloaded using peer-to-peer networks is copyright infringing. consumers often have no convenient legal alternative, so they resort to illicit practices. we have to find a solution to this problem. i support and encourage the commission to continue its efforts to promote and improve access to european culture online.
in writing. − the audiovisual and film industries are not only a branch of the arts but also a market sector that provides many jobs in the eu. the economic contribution of the cultural and creative industries, expressed in terms of value added, is 2,5% of gdp. to ensure the further development of this market, we should create the conditions for the creation of audiovisual material and protect its creators. but we forget that in the age of the internet, the distribution and access to audiovisual material is increasingly done through illegal channels. consumers using these channels are often unaware of the importance of intellectual property rights. therefore, consumers should be adequately informed of any intellectual property law issues that may arise in connection with file sharing in cloud computing services. the widespread availability of audiovisual material should seem to increase the earnings of creators and performers of such material. however, the wages they receive are often very low. it is therefore worthwhile to look at ways of ensuring that authors and performers are adequately remunerated.

in writing. a properly managed maritime policy, which significantly improves the competitiveness of the fisheries sector, can have a positive impact on the functioning of the eu economy as a whole, and the establishment of a maximum sustainable yield (msy) threshold will allow for the rational exploitation of fisheries resources and the establishment of a stable multiannual strategy for the sector. the introduction of conservation measures on issues such as the prohibition of discards or the landing of all fish in port will have a positive impact on the ecosystems of the water bodies used and the survival of endangered fish species. the common fisheries policy must also include provisions to ensure that threats such as piracy and poaching are eliminated. full synergy between the cap and other policies, such as environmental policy and cohesion policy, will improve economic prosperity throughout the community, and especially in regions where the economy is mainly based on this industry.
in writing. fish stocks in europe are projected to be depleted in the coming decades. fishing policies are still not sufficiently coordinated, which means that many species are already on the verge of extinction, including the most popular ones, such as salmon and tuna. therefore, urgent action is needed to prevent this ecological disaster and the voluntary deprivation of humanity of its diversity. it is therefore necessary to draw up immediately multiannual plans to ensure the management of fisheries in an orderly manner, to increase the financial resources for research and fisheries, and to strictly control compliance with the fishing ban during conservation periods. however, the diversity and specificity of the individual european seas must be taken into account when drawing up the legal rules. the fishermen and producers who will be deprived of income as a result of the new regulations must not be forgotten. the new budget should therefore provide for compensation for those who will suffer the economic and social consequences of the reform.

in writing. mr president, i would like to thank you for your kind words. i would like to stress once again today the importance of ensuring that victims of a wide range of crimes receive appropriate protection and support during criminal proceedings, and that they are treated with respect and dignity. equally important, they should be able to count on redress, justice and protection against the repetition of offences, regardless of the member state in which the offence is committed and whether the victims are nationals of that country or not. all this is guaranteed in the directive which the european parliament will be voting on tomorrow. among the provisions of the directive, those that deserve special attention are: the introduction of a uniform definition of 'victim', according to which the status of victim is conferred not only on the injured persons but also on their close family members, and the definition of 'victim of gender-based violence' and 'victim of intimate partner violence'; the introduction of the necessary arrangements for effective coordination between victim support bodies by creating formal and informal structures enabling staff of judicial bodies, law enforcement bodies and non-governmental organisations to co-operate normally and guaranteeing victims access to free psychological, legal and translation and interpretation services. this is undoubtedly a very important step towards the harmonisation of law at european level and above all an expression of concern for citizens throughout europe.

in writing. - the european union has many institutions, each with specific competences. their distribution is intended to help the eu function better. with the end of the three-pillar structure, a reform of the union's derived law was necessary. the treaty of lisbon did this by dividing the category of legal acts into legislative and non-legislative acts. the subject of my comments is delegated and implementing acts which are classified by the treaty on the functioning of the european union as non-legislative acts, as provided for in articles 290 and 291 tfeu. each of these has been established for a specific purpose. delegated acts are intended to supplement non-essential elements of legislative acts. they are issued by the ec on the basis of powers conferred on it by a legislative act. that act should specify the powers conferred on the commission. the second type i have mentioned is implementing acts, which are designed to ensure uniform conditions for the implementation of legally binding union acts. the responsibility for the effective implementation of eu law lies primarily with the member states, but where uniform conditions for the implementation of legally binding union acts are necessary, those acts confer implementing powers on the commission or the council of the eu. i am in favour of the proposal to bring the three council regulations on imports of olive oil and other agricultural products from turkey into line with the provisions of the tfeu.
in writing. − i voted in favour of mr moreira’s report and the proposed amendments to the commission’s proposal. these reflect the changes brought about by the two trade omnibuses: insertion of new recitals on implementing acts/delegated acts into the basic legal acts; limitation of the conferral of the delegated powers on the commission to the period of five years, tacitly extendable by a period of identical duration; and the extension of possible prolongation of the period for objection to a draft delegated act from two to four months, thereby extending the period of scrutiny from four months (2+2) to six months (2+4). i support the involvement of the european parliament during the preparation of delegated acts.
in writing. - the three regulations governing imports of olive oil and other agricultural products from turkey should be brought into line with the system of delegated and implementing acts introduced by the lisbon treaty. to that end, provisions on committee procedure should be added to each of those regulations. this will allow the international trade commission to scrutinise the implementing acts based on those regulations. that is why i voted for the regulation.
