the rapporteur. - madam president! - what are you doing? a large number of works held in european archives or libraries cannot be made available because it is not possible to identify the authorship of these works or to reach the rights holders who need to give consent to their use. such frozen works often account for as much as 45% of the collections of these institutions. cultural heritage should be a public service, not a prison of copyright. the case involves all publications: books, newspapers, photographs, radio and television recordings. as someone who has worked for years in the cultural world, i was keen to tackle this problem at the legislative level across the union and to bring forgotten works back into the public domain by digitising them. i am pleased that the legal affairs committee accepted my report on the accessibility of orphan works in march this year. the project provides that works after a so-called due diligence that shows that the author or the rights holder cannot be identified can be given the status of orphan, which means that they can be made available to the public as part of non-commercial activities, i.e. without a profit motive, and also be preserved and restored through digitisation. in addition, a work considered orphan in one country will be automatically considered as such in other countries. if the author or the rights holder is found, he or she can claim adequate compensation if he or she can prove that he or she has suffered real losses as a result of such disclosure. i think this is a great example of how mitigating copyright, not tightening it, can be beneficial for all parties. i negotiated this issue on behalf of the legal affairs committee with the council, first under the polish presidency, then under the danish presidency, and today my report will be put to the vote in plenary, which will mean that one of the priorities of the cypriot presidency has been achieved. the creation of an exception to intellectual property law for the sharing of cultural heritage by public institutions for purposes of education and cultural promotion will open a new chapter in intellectual property law. this is a very important directive because it is the first to establish a legislative basis in a new area of law that has not been regulated so far. it gives beneficiaries who have so far avoided digitization for fear of potentially being sued for millions of dollars if the author is found, a breath of relief. the compensation in the form of a settlement provides legal certainty in this respect. works with multiple owners, so-called 'semi-orphans', will also be able to be digitised and made available to a wide range of audiences. libraries, archives and museums have long been waiting for clear rules that would allow them to share treasures that have been hidden for years and prevent them from being forgotten or destroyed. digitisation, which will finally be fully possible thanks to this directive, solves these problems. most importantly, however, and i consider this the most successful part of our negotiations, the new article 6 (2) will give public authorities a real chance to generate revenue from the use of orphan works, which will support the modest budgets allocated to digitisation processes. commercial use of the work is strictly defined in the text and is linked to the issue of possible compensation for the author, if any. i believe that we have also struck a balanced compromise here between copyright protection and the possibility of exclusive use of orphan works. moreover, we included in the review clause a provision for the commission to examine the effects of the directive one year after its entry into force and to make any necessary changes or improvements, or to introduce a wider range of beneficiaries, including, for example, private institutions. the negotiations were difficult, we did not always agree on all issues, but i am pleased with the final compromise solutions and i am convinced that this directive will be a useful and effective tool for making hidden culture available to a wide audience. i would like to thank all the co-rapporteurs, as well as the commission and the council, for the fruitful negotiations.
madam president! first of all, i would like to congratulate the rapporteur and my colleagues on the legal affairs committee on the great determination and great negotiating skills that have been required in the work on this directive. the directive, like all other projects on the protection of intellectual property rights, has generated a lot of excitement and a lot of controversy. regulating access to works, the real cultural treasures that now line the shelves of libraries and many archives, may seem like a small step, but it is certainly a step in the right direction. in the current atmosphere of general confusion about the very definition of intellectual property and the rights that this definition gives, in the atmosphere of a discussion of little substance fuelled by various parties interested in defending the freedom of access to almost everything that someone else has created or invented, especially if such sharing is to take place in the internet sphere, i see the report by mrs geringer as a light in the tunnel. a light that gives hope for a more substantive and properly argued discussion on the protection of creative thought in the european union. the work on this dossier has shown that it is possible to bring together views that at first seemed very far apart. it is enough, or perhaps it should be said, that we have a dialogue based on rational arguments that take into account the positions of both creators and users. i therefore hope that future ip projects will be conducted in the spirit of substantive discussion, and not used for populist behaviour and political games of various kinds.
i would like to congratulate my colleague from the region, mrs lydia geringer de oedenberg, on her excellent work and the compromise she has reached. i think today we can send two very serious, very significant signals to our citizens. first, there is a huge opportunity to accelerate the digitisation of cultural works in europe, those hundreds of thousands of works that today are stored in the archives of museums and libraries and cannot - because of legal conflicts and legal problems - be made available to the wider public. and today, young people, especially young people, are mobile, and the issue of finding cultural works is absolutely relevant and accessible only and exclusively through the internet. second, actually, with the legal norms that we're regulating today, there will be an opportunity for all public institutions, libraries, educational institutions, to give these works the ability to be published. i believe that all the measures that have been taken here, including the mutual recognition of works, can be a good step towards making cultural heritage very widely accessible in the european union. congratulations to all those who worked on this directive.
madam chair, i apologize for the delay caused by the extension of the previous meeting. madam president, ladies and gentlemen, ladies and gentlemen, ladies and gentlemen, ladies and gentlemen, ladies and gentlemen, ladies and gentlemen, ladies and gentlemen, ladies and gentlemen! i would like to begin by thanking the rapporteur's colleagues for their work on the amendments and on the text as a whole. i hope that it will succeed in filling the legal gap that we are currently in and allow for a wide access to so-called orphan works. this is particularly important in the context of protests by knowledge-dissemination organisations. they have long reported problems with the use of such materials, for example in audiovisual processes. the directive and the proposed amendments make this possibility more flexible, especially in the context of non-profit activities, but these provisions seem to be poorly adapted to the needs of the market. as many as 69% of those surveyed on one side were in favour of the possibility of using orphan works in for-profit activities. it is therefore worth considering the possibility of further amendments to the directive to open the way to the commercial exploitation of orphan works. this would be a strong impetus towards their wider publicity, and such a change would also increase the number of potential beneficiaries. the amendments themselves safeguard the interests of potential heirs to the works, but on the other hand they impose legal conditions on the institutions wishing to use the works which are difficult to fulfil. in the long run, this may extend the distance that books, photographs and paintings travel before they reach the general public.
member of the commission. − madam president, honourable members, before you proceed to the vote, let me underline once again the importance of this directive. the text is a major step in our mutual objective to create a digital single market. it will define the right rules for the promotion of knowledge and culture across our borders for the benefit of all european citizens. the european parliament has played a constructive role in ensuring a successful conclusion to our negotiations over the past year.
the rapporteur. - madam president! - what are you doing? i thank you all for a fruitful debate and i thank all the members for the great work we have done together over the last year and a half. i am glad that soon many of the hidden gems of our culture and heritage will be brought to light and made available to the general public, and i also think that this is a first, perhaps small, but important step towards the future of full harmonisation of copyright across the european union. i would like to thank the danish presidency for the very fruitful cooperation, and i would like to thank in particular ambassador jonas bering liisberg. i also thank commissioner barnier very much for the many fruitful meetings and discussions, and commissioner neelie kroes, who, i must say, was a good omen for this project. i would like to thank in particular my colleagues on the committee on legal affairs, the colleagues of mrs angelice niebler, who was the co-rapporteur, and of mariella gallo, who was very involved in the work, and i also thank mrs alexandra thein, who is here with us today, and christian engström for their support, although we differed on some points, but it was a very important discussion. i thank the secretariat of the legal affairs committee and all the assistants who have worked with us. i am surprised at the position of the gue, which throughout the negotiations has supported our work and expressed support or has not participated in the negotiations. so i'm surprised at your last-minute position that you want to abstain. i encourage you to support a good first step towards harmonising the very part of copyright law that concerns orphan works. thank you very much and i encourage you to vote yes.
the rapporteur. - madam president! - what are you doing? my position on the negotiations was with your representatives in the legal group, the legal affairs committee. your members in the legal affairs group have supported my initiative, i understand with the support of your colleagues in the culture committee. so it's an intra-group problem, if you're in the negotiations, as far as the legal affairs committee is concerned, you're in favor of the proposal, then i understand that the whole group is in favor, and if not, then you have a problem within your group. however, i ask you to support this initiative because your position is completely incomprehensible at this moment.
mr president, commissioner, i have to ask you to stop this. the report by mr karim on the evaluation of the state of the law in the european union this year is very specific, because it is produced in the european parliament every year. every year we try to show where we still have a lot to do, and i hope that the guidance that comes from the european parliament is taken into account by the parliament itself and by the other legislators, the european commission and the council. however, this year's debate is special in that we are talking about a time of economic crisis, but also a crisis of faith in the possibility and the usefulness of the development of the european institutions and their effectiveness. our task is to restore the effectiveness of the european union and to rebuild trust in european law, which is reflected in national legislation. this is the key element of cooperation with our national partners, with national parliaments, with regional parliaments. the importance of this is shown by the use, for the first time, of the yellow card procedure vis-à-vis the european commission in respect of the monti ii regulation, and by the european parliament's 'quick and efficient' behaviour which led to the commission's withdrawal from this regulation. another key issue today is the need to further reduce the administrative burdens and barriers that make small and medium-sized enterprises - the driving force of the european economy - expect us to legislate better so that they can operate well, freely and wisely, creating new jobs that will be the most important element in the fight against the crisis. so i thank my colleague karim and the other colleagues for this year's report and i hope that its conclusions will be implemented quickly.
mr. chairman, please! if you ask the average citizen of any eu country what eu law means to them, one of the most common answers is probably 'too complicated or too bureaucratic'. it is true that many european union legal acts are written in difficult-to-understand specialist language, which makes it difficult to better understand the meaning of the decisions taken. of course, this is partly justified by the subject matter of the act or by other factors that influence the final shape of the document. nevertheless, the report we are debating today is an important step towards bringing the european union closer to ordinary citizens. we need clear, simple and understandable legislation for all and a reduction in the regulatory burden on small and medium-sized enterprises. we must draw the attention of the european commission and the council to the fact that the proliferation of legal acts written in inaccessible and specialist language will not help to increase the popularity of the european union among its citizens. finally, the law enacted by the community institutions should be based on facts, verified and tested as often as possible for effectiveness and usefulness, because in the end it is created for the citizens and that is what it should serve.
mr. chairman, please! i would like to congratulate the rapporteur on his contribution to the democratic control of the legislative process in the european union. it is not without reason that there is often talk of a growing deficit in this area. under the existing treaties, both the european parliament and national parliaments play an important role in the decision-making process. however, as mr karim's report shows, these prerogatives are not always reflected in practice. the rapporteur's conclusions show that the european commission does not always apply the principles of subsidiarity and proportionality adequately, for example through, as the national parliaments point out, the absence or insufficient justification of the subsidiarity principle in its initiatives. the involvement of our national parliaments in the process of scrutiny of legislative proposals in the light of these two principles should therefore be welcomed. furthermore, as stated in the forewords, i would like to stress the urgent need for better scrutiny, including by our house, of delegated and implementing acts, where important issues often escape democratic scrutiny.
mr. chairman, please! the commission states that it is not aware of most of the member states' energy agreements. this means that it has no ability to react to extremely unfavourable contracts for supplies from outside the union, which directly reduce the energy security of the country concerned. the increased powers and the associated involvement of the commission in the process of negotiating and evaluating the legal aspects of intergovernmental agreements are undoubtedly justified. i believe that these measures will lead to a rational pricing policy and will help to reduce the colossal disparities that exist, for example, in the agreements between individual countries and the russian gas powerhouse. energy agreements with third countries also affect the functioning of the internal energy market. the development of the transmission infrastructure requires a high level of investment. in the context of these conditions, the necessary expertise and assistance of the commission should be put to good use, and the sharing of information on concluded agreements and negotiations is a key means to this end.
mr. chairman, please! virtually every region of the european union has developed its own traditional agricultural production methods, which has an impact on the diversity of agricultural production throughout the community. the region's own food products are often of great value. farmers and consumers alike should be aware of their quality, which also affects the presence and recognition of products on european and world markets. quality control systems, supplemented by distinctive markings, contribute to this. the resolution calls for the introduction of a european standardisation body to ensure that the quality of products is not compromised. the transparency and ease of use of these mechanisms will make them less burdensome for producers. i hope that more and more excellent polish food products will be protected. i also agree with the rapporteur that the quality assurance system should also cover unprocessed products. this would allow producers of apples from mazovia, for example, to apply for guarantees.
mr. chairman, please! the resolution on syria is simply our moral duty. while it does not change the situation directly, it draws the attention of the entire civilized world to what is happening in syria, to the fate of thousands of refugees and the scale of human suffering caused by the deaths of those killed and those at the center of the conflict. at the same time, the use of military force against civilians is reprehensible. the exodus of refugees. the lack of agreement in the un security council, especially between china and russia, also makes this a politically difficult situation to resolve. so we also call on these countries to join the international response that is adequate to fundamentally change the situation in syria. there is another issue that we rarely talk about, namely the risks of large chemical weapons stockpiles, which have been raised by agencies around the world that study the situation. if the weapons were left unprotected, it could be a huge humanitarian disaster in the region.
in recent years, we have become increasingly aware of abuses in the russian justice system. this is evidenced, for example, by the large number of cases brought before the european court of human rights. the cases of political interference by the judiciary, which should be completely independent, are particularly significant, and i would point out that the russian constitution guarantees the full rights and freedoms of its citizens. the commission has also been actively involved in the implementation of the eu's common foreign and security policy (cfsp) and the implementation of the eu's common security and defence policy (csdp). it is concerned about the legal restrictions on freedom of expression and association and the use of severe penalties for breach of these restrictions. russia, as a member of the council of europe, is obliged to respect civil liberties. in supporting the resolution, i call on the authorities in moscow to restore the rule of law, to end political persecution and to lift restrictions on public rights. i call for an end to discrimination against ngos and for them to be given the right conditions to operate. i also condemn all acts of repression against civil society and the democratic opposition.
mr. chairman, please! russia is too important a country, too important a partner, also a political partner, in the world, but also a strategic partner with whom the european union has a privileged relationship. so if these relations are privileged, if they are placed on the level of strategic partnership, then we too have the right to expect our partner - and there are relevant provisions - to apply principles that are acceptable in a democratic world in matters of human rights, including the judiciary. at the same time, we were dealing with the new issue of russia's accession to the world trade organisation, which also entails some kind of commitment. of course, each country has the right to build its justice system on the basis of acceptable standards, but it cannot be that political pressures, as in the case of magnitsky or other cases, such as the aforementioned platon lebiedyev, or the earlier estemirova, politkovskaya case, overshadow all this. we therefore call on russia, as a great country with great potential, to adopt standards that are acceptable in democratic societies.
president barroso's speech yesterday, and our work on the draft resolution, are a confirmation of the plans for a banking union. in fact, the eurozone crisis is accelerating this process. at the same time, the presentation of the project and the legal basis which has been invoked indicate that it is addressed only and exclusively to euro area members. all the member states of the european union should have the right, if they want, of course, to join this banking union. after all, for example, banks in hungary are 90% external capital, poland about 70% is external capital, including from banks in the member states of the european union. at the same time, the proposal of close cooperation for non-euro area countries is a second category of membership in the banking union with obligations, but no possibility of influencing these decisions, and with serious consequences for the country and its savings, deposits, the guarantee of these deposits, and possibly rescue funds. this is a straightforward path to the two-speed union and we would not want to accept that.

in writing. − i consider it appropriate to conclude an agreement between the european parliament and the council on the transmission and processing by the parliament of classified information held by the council on matters other than those of common foreign and security policy. this agreement is a necessary instrument for enabling parliament to exercise its powers and functions fully, particularly in the context of the provisions of the treaty of lisbon, which has increased parliament's powers in the field of international agreements. the agreement sets out in detail the definitions and classification levels of classified information exchanged between the council and parliament, the security measures for individuals and the procedure for accessing and protecting classified information. it is also worth noting that the agreement also lays down the specific conditions for the transmission of classified information to parliament by the commission.

in writing. − i voted in favour of this report. the eu imports over 60% of its gas and over 80% of its oil. this import tendency is increasing and makes us very vulnerable. energy supply contracts are usually concluded between commercial entities, but there are some situations when intergovernmental agreements (iga) are requested of an eu member state. sometimes, however, the aim of the third country is to bind an eu member state to assure the commercial contract or to secure a monopolistic position in energy supplies via particular infrastructure. i believe that in order to avoid a breach of internal market rules in the field of energy, we must enhance our internal eu cooperation regarding igas. we know that gasprom does not always play by the rules and the russian federation uses political pressure to try to get what it wants. this has recently taken place in bulgaria. for this reason, member states need all the help they can get and i believe that the commission’s involvement in negotiations with third parties has had positive effects in the past.
in writing. - the agreement i voted for is designed to eliminate incompatibilities between eu law and intergovernmental agreements concluded between member states and third countries. it will significantly improve the functioning of the internal energy market. it is also important that it contains clauses requiring member states to exchange full information on intergovernmental agreements that affect the volume of energy imports into the union. the adoption of this agreement will ensure a high degree of transparency of agreements concluded between member states and third countries.
in writing. - the european union has been struggling with energy security for years. this is particularly true in the countries of central and eastern europe, which are often dependent on a single supplier. slovakia gets 100% of its gas from russia, as does hungary, poland and lithuania. of course, this allows the supplier to unilaterally set prices. it is important that the european commission has information on the price member states pay for gas and oil. it is important that the eu should seek to help others to establish better gas contract terms, by drawing on the experience of some countries. there are many positive examples of this, such as the negotiations of the polish gas agreement with gazprom. however, we should not forget that the only solution to reducing hydrocarbon prices is to develop alternative connections between suppliers from different regions of the world.

in writing. - both of the products discussed in today's report concern a so-called sensitive product which needs to be covered by a specific legal framework. bananas, as they are known, enter the union market mainly through imports from third countries (not to mention, of course, the peripheral regions of the eu such as the canary islands, martinique and guadeloupe), and are therefore subject to the relevant tariff regimes. trade agreements with colombia, peru and central america are to be covered by appropriate safeguard clauses to counter any disruption that the introduction of bananas on the european market may cause. the european commission's suggestions, however, do not address the issue of close monitoring of trade or the protection of european producers who may suffer as a result of excessive trade liberalisation. as a member of the parliament's committee on agriculture and rural development, i am in favour of allowing the european globalisation adjustment fund to be used in this case. we must also not forget the respect of environmental standards in the production process, and - and this is particularly important - the enforcement of human rights, which are often violated in the countries with which we have agreements.
in writing. − i abstained because, while fully recognising the need for a bilateral safeguard clause to safely implement on the eu side the free trade agreement concluded between the eu, colombia and peru, i consider that some of the amendments adopted in the international trade committee require further redrafting for the sake of clarity and feasibility. for example: definition of ‘threat of serious deterioration’ for the activation of the bilateral safeguard clause and the stabilisation mechanism for bananas; extent of the commission’s monitoring and especially the inclusion of additional socioeconomic indicators on top of colombian and peruvian export and import statistics, to assess the impact of the fta on the banana production in the eu; involvement of the european parliament in initiating an investigation in the framework of the bilateral safeguard clause and the stabilisation mechanism for bananas; the commission’s room for manoeuvre with respect to the activation of the stabilisation mechanism for bananas. these issues need to be clarified.
in writing. −the legislative initiative to allow the use of orphan works is right and good. such works account for as much as 45% of all works in the collections of various institutions and archives. the impossibility of identifying the copyright owner should not be an obstacle to the general use of such a work. orphaned works are often the foundation of our culture. their use in non-profit activities is necessary, especially when it comes to knowledge dissemination processes.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because i support the directive which will allow those works which fall into the ‘orphan works’ category to be used by libraries and other public institutions within the member states for broadly non-commercial purposes such as digitisation and preservation. this will help facilitate access so that these cultural works can remain available for future generations. i support the safeguards that were introduced to protect those rights holders whose works are accidentally designated as ‘orphans.’ it is also important to carry out a diligent search for each individual work to appropriately respect the intellectual property rights of its authors and creators.
in writing. - in the era of global digitalisation, we must take special care of all copyright, preventing its illegal use, but we must also take care of works whose author is unknown. the creation of digital possibilities for cultural heritage is a duty and must be supported at european level. the many amendments that have been made during the work demonstrate the degree of difficulty in achieving a uniform text of the directive without prejudice to the arrangements in the member states for the mass digitisation of works. with all due respect to the members of parliament working on this issue, i voted to accept the motion.
in writing. - the text we voted on today contains important and long-awaited solutions. so i hope that it will succeed in filling the legal gap that we are currently in and allowing wide access to so-called orphan works. the report by ms geringer de oedenberg offers a great opportunity to accelerate the digitisation of cultural works in europe, which will of course lead to a wider public reception. i hope that this will be a strong impetus for the cultural development and wider dissemination of works by, for example, julius korczak and other artists killed during the second world war. the new regulations also allow us to regulate the use of works by galleries, museums and public libraries. in doing so, they shall ensure adequate protection for any heirs of the authors. this is a big step forward.

in writing. - the situation in syria is still very complex and ambiguous. a large number of syrians, even about 70%, still support president assad. moreover, he can count on the total loyalty of the alawites and the christians and druze who live in the area and make up about 34 percent of the population. therefore, there is no chance of any ceasefire at the moment, especially since the situation on the front is still favorable for the government forces. the rebels control only the northern regions of the country and are unable to take up any fighting outside of mountainous or heavily urbanized areas. for over two months, there have been no signs of any serious cases of desertion from the ruling camp. meanwhile, reports are coming in of fighting between aleppo residents and rebels. the opposition forces have no military oversight and act more as a representation of the refugee camp than as the real voice of the syrians. the conflict has been worrisome with the increasing number of rebel attacks on christians and christian places of worship. unfortunately, the resolutions put to the vote give too superficial a picture of their situation.
in writing. − the resolution on the use of the judiciary for political purposes in russia recalls the difficult internal situation of the country and the harmful human rights laws that have been passed in the state duma of the russian federation. as a co-author of the draft resolution, i consider it extremely important that it recalls specific cases of human rights violations, such as the convictions of mikhail khodorkovsky and platon lebedev and taisa osipova, while at the same time mentioning the tragedy of sergei magnitsky. the situation of human rights defenders and activists who disagree with the current authorities is very difficult. despite some cases being reported in the media, most cases are ignored by the prosecution. it is in the european union's interest to cooperate fruitfully with neighbours whose social life is governed by the principles of democracy and the rule of law. that's still missing in russia. it is therefore the duty of members of the european parliament to constantly remind them of what needs to be improved and changed. for these reasons, i supported the resolution.
in writing. − this year, the european parliament adopted a series of resolutions on russia, most of them focusing on issues related to respect for human rights and the rule of law. sadly, instead of getting better, the situation in this country seems to be getting worse. the persecution of human rights defenders, independent journalists and ngos is intensifying. worse, special legislation is being adopted which, under the guise of fighting extremism, allows for an effective strike on civil society representatives. the european parliament rightly expresses its concern once again about the situation in russia, pointing to a long and growing series of abuses and violations of fundamental freedoms.
in writing. - we voted on a very important resolution today. russia has a long history of poor law enforcement. the judiciary, which should have remained independent, has become the perfect tool for the authorities to hammer out opposition with harsh sentences in isolated siberian detention centers or to wash away inconvenient cases by leaving them unresolved for years. examples are not to be found far away. the russian security services and prosecutors have not been able to find and prosecute the killers of anna politkovskaya and natalia estemirova. the sixth anniversary of the first one will be celebrated on october 6th. there are also very worrying signs about the russian election monitoring organization "golos". a moscow court fined her 30,000 rubles for creating a negative image of one of the parties. in addition, her colleagues have been subject to formal restrictions on movement within the russian federation, as well as detention. signs of change in the functioning of russian law are also worrying. i will just remind you that in 2011 a draft was published, which would give the constitutional court of the russian federation the right to block the execution of judgments of the european court of human rights in strasbourg. in the light of these developments, the key question is how has the european external action service responded to these unlawful and rule-of-law-destroying cases?
in writing. − the document published in june by the president of the european council is a highly desirable initiative, which represents the implementation of the european council's overriding function of defining new directions for integration and political priorities for the union. i strongly support a comprehensive strategy of building an integrated financial, budgetary and economic policy framework in parallel, while maintaining an appropriate level of democratic legitimacy. the implementation of this bold plan should be carried out by means of a community method which guarantees adequate transparency of the decision-making process and the accountability of the new institutions to the citizens. i also believe that the new integrated financial framework should cover all the member states of the union, so as not to undermine the achievements of the common financial market and at the same time to frustrate the achievements of others. in my view, it should also be borne in mind that before the ambitious vision of a banking union can be put into effect, negotiations on the remaining necessary components of an integrated financial framework, such as the deposit guarantee scheme and capital requirements, must first be concluded quickly and effectively. without these elements, it will be impossible to restore the stability of the european financial system.

in writing. − this is a particularly important budget, as it concludes the financial framework for 2007-13. during that time, the european union allocated considerable funds to the cohesion fund, which has led to many infrastructure and environmental investments, including in the kujawy-pomeranian voivodeship, where i come from. most of these investments have already been made, and now it is time to pay them back from the eu budget. therefore, the 2013 budget cannot only take into account the projects planned for that particular year, but must also contain the means to settle the investments of previous years. this is a matter of the credibility of the european union.
in writing. - the advantage of the preliminary report by mr böge and mr kalfin is undoubtedly the investment nature of the eu budget, whether through the funding of the lifelong learning programme, including the erasmus programme, or the recognition of the eu's cohesion policy, of which poland is the main beneficiary, as a pillar of european solidarity and a strategic tool for sustainable growth. the continuation of the programme for the most deprived and the opposition to the uk rebate are also commendable. on the other hand, however, the solutions for financing the climate package, which is extremely harmful to the polish economy, and the eu agencies, including the eeas, decided that i could not support the above report, and therefore abstained.
in writing. − the negotiations on the eu budget for 2014-2020 are entering a crucial phase. in a few days, the cypriot presidency will present a new proposal for a seven-year budget with concrete figures. the union budget, although systematically reduced over the past few years, continues to be a symbol of solidarity with the community's poorer countries, as it supports their structural changes and their efforts to promote investment for growth and jobs throughout the community. the eu budget for 2014-2020 must above all include adequate resources to continue to address development gaps, research and development and to support competitiveness and innovation. the amount for cohesion policy, which is a key instrument for investment and reducing macroeconomic disparities between eu regions and countries, must therefore be kept at least at the same level. it is also essential to continue the eu programmes targeting young people and those that have been very successful in promoting culture, education and the media. it is important for integration that the european globalisation adjustment fund and the existing financial resources for co2 reduction and climate change mitigation are maintained at least at their current level.
in writing. - in the vote on the multiannual financial framework, i voted in favour of the ep's position, which calls for a guarantee of the sustainability of agricultural expenditure and structural policies, in particular cohesion policy. we cannot vote against growth policies and investments to improve the quality of life, education and job creation. we have set ourselves targets in the europe 2020 strategy and we must achieve them. we must be credible and fight for what we promise to 500 million citizens. spending cuts in the eu's next multiannual budget will slow its growth and make it harder to get out of the crisis. remember that the eu budget is an investment budget and cannot be compared with national budgets. given the need for rapid budgetary decisions, which are the basis for all union action, i voted in favour of this resolution.
in writing. - i believe that the report by mr boege and mr kalfin represents a balanced position of the european parliament towards the future multiannual financial framework, and i have therefore decided to vote in favour of this document. i am pleased that the report highlights such important aspects as the investment nature of cohesion policy and the role of the eu budget in achieving the europe 2020 objectives. however, one of the proposals in the report concerned me, and i decided, together with 40 other members, to table an amendment for the plenary, which i would now like to explain. i believe that allocating 25% of cohesion policy resources to the esf not only imposes unnecessary constraints but also runs counter to the need to increase the flexibility of the multiannual financial framework proposed in the remainder of the report. i would also like to thank the members who voted in favour of this amendment today.
in writing. − some member states try to use the current financial crisis in order to reduce their contribution to the eu budget. they bow to or even consciously exploit the anti-european sentiments which arose in some countries. however, reducing the european budget means hurting one’s own economy as much as that of the other member states. the eu budget redistributes 94% back to the member states and is largely devoted to investments. those investments are proven to boost economic growth, not only in the cohesion countries but also with the so-called net payers. the european parliament has to make a stand for this investment budget and has to oppose any cuts. the budgetary austerity which some member states also want to impose onto the eu is a self-defeating strategy. the eu does not have any debts to pay off and has one of the lowest rates of spending on its own administration. therefore it makes no sense to apply budgetary cuts to europe’s most efficient mean of investments. therefore i supported this interim report.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution on the multiannual financial framework, as it emphasises the need to guarantee that agricultural expenditure and structural policy are maintained at least at current levels, which is beneficial for poland. the position of parliament has been consistent and clear on the new perspective for several months, and this strengthens our position vis-à-vis the council. attempts to limit money for cohesion policy are incomprehensible, especially when there is a lack of investment spending in europe. net payers should be aware that most of this money comes back to them in the form of investment or additional exports.
in writing. - the debate on the size and shape of the budget is also a debate on the methods of combating the economic crisis. more and more people are coming to believe that cuts and belt tightening will kill the patient rather than cure him. the socialists and democrats (s&d) are calling for a large budget to be earmarked for investment. it would be the equivalent of the marshall plan, but funded by europeans, for europeans. i am pleased that president josé manuel barroso has taken a similar position. the defence of cohesion policy, which can best serve the role of the european marshall plan mentioned above, is particularly important today. the second pillar of the common agricultural policy can also fulfil a similar function. it should be given special protection against the budget cuts announced. and there is great concern about the announced cuts in spending on science and research. they are clearly at odds with the objectives of the europe 2020 strategy. i think the european commission's budget proposals are optimal. any attempt to cut back should be met with resistance. the european parliament should also take care of its own subjectivity when working on the multiannual financial framework. at the same time, it cannot be ruled out that the european parliament's rejection of the narrow multiannual financial framework will be a decisive step.
in writing. − the budget of the european union is a key instrument for the sustainable and inclusive development of the union as a whole. in the current crisis, the eu budget is part of the solution to europe's recovery, by supporting investment and job creation. however, the proposal to freeze the 2014-2020 mff ceilings at the 2013 level will leave insufficient funds to finance these priorities. that's why i abstained.
in writing. − we are moving ever closer to adopting the 2014-2020 budget. unfortunately, there is a growing controversy here. most net contributors want the budget to be frozen at least, or even reduced if possible. i'm very much against it. the european union's budget for 2014-2020 should be well in excess of eur 1 trillion. let us remember that this budget is for new infrastructure investments, for boosting production and for creating new jobs. it must be a pro-investment budget, not a budget to limit the eu community. for countries such as poland, it is also of additional importance it makes it possible to close the gaps which unfortunately still exist. without a high budget and directing it to the relatively less developed countries, we will never eliminate the differences in living standards among the people of the european union.

in writing. - almost 20 years ago, european citizenship was introduced and automatically granted to citizens of all member states. this gave them many rights within the european union. they can vote in local elections in the countries where they live, they can stand for election to the european parliament, they can reside, live or study in all the member states. unfortunately, as the report shows, only 43% of eu citizens say they are familiar with the term 'european citizen', and as many as 67% feel not very well informed about their rights. in addition, there is all kinds of abuse and discrimination on the basis of nationality by officials and employers, which effectively discourages many people from going abroad to work. diplomas and qualifications are not recognised, and language barriers effectively hinder the exercise of their rights. the current economic crisis and unemployment have further highlighted these problems. i am therefore very pleased that the european commission has proposed to designate 2013 as the european year of citizens. we must do everything we can to make the most of this time to raise awareness among citizens about their rights. we cannot allow the european solidarity and sense of belonging that we have built up over the years to be destroyed by a temporary financial crisis. i agree with the rapporteur that we need to give european citizenship more visibility.

in writing. − consular assistance is essential if you lose your identity documents, are arrested, detained or have any other problems that you may encounter when travelling outside the eu. in accordance with the provisions of the treaty, citizens of the union are entitled to enjoy the diplomatic and consular protection of any other member state in the territory of a third country where the member state of which they are nationals is not represented. this right is an important aspect of eu citizenship and extends the consular protection of europeans worldwide. however, it is becoming increasingly common for citizens to need help not only for everyday problems, such as documentation, but also in emergency situations, which are a major coordination challenge. it is therefore important to designate a single coordinating body which will, among other things, ensure that all eu citizens, including the under-represented, are covered by emergency and evacuation plans. the question of the financing of such protection is also of great importance in this context. it is therefore important that the report draws attention to this. i fully support the report as it will help to increase consular protection for eu citizens and to provide more effective and faster assistance in the territory of third countries.
in writing. − any citizen of the union who is present in the territory of a third country, in the absence of a representation of his country in that territory, shall be entitled to consular assistance from another member state which is represented in that third country, under the same conditions as nationals of that state. this is provided for in articles 20 (2) (c) and 23 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union and article 46 of the charter of fundamental rights of the european union. the new directive provides for the coordination of assistance, in particular by identifying 'leading states' in third countries, to improve consular protection operations in both day-to-day and emergency situations. the access to a diplomatic post defined in the proposal for a directive, which allows one to reach it and return within one day, is a good solution, especially in emergency and frequent situations (e.g. theft or loss of documents, death, arrest). the obligation of the union delegation to coordinate the provision of assistance in preparation for and in the event of a crisis situation will also place a significant burden on the 'leading country' designated in the third country or any other member state present in the area. i therefore consider these amendments to be necessary and extremely helpful for all citizens of the european union.
in writing. − a new legislative instrument may be required to facilitate the access of eu citizens to protection in third countries. i am concerned about additional costs, but i share the opinion that in crisis situations, where the union delegation has the role of coordination, it should have the necessary financial means to provide that coordination. we should not forget about the prerogatives of member states, because it is their consulates and embassies that, first and foremost, have the responsibility of protecting their citizens. nevertheless, these are not always available. there are cases when even though an eu citizen has his or her embassy or consulate in the third country, it is inaccessible. this is where the eu must play a role because, according to article 23 of the treaty of the functioning of the european union, every citizen of the union shall, in the territory of a third country in which the member states of which he is a national is not represented, be entitled to protection by the diplomatic or consular authorities of any member state, on the same conditions as a national of that state.
in writing. − according to the treaty on the functioning of the european union, every citizen of the union has the right to diplomatic and consular protection in a third country by any of the other member states if the country of which he is a national is not represented there. the proposed solutions are intended to facilitate the exercise of these rights by european union citizens. however, they do not take full advantage of the possibilities offered by the lisbon treaty. this is particularly the case with the non-use of the role of the european union delegations. that's why i voted against it.
in writing. − most eu countries do not have, and will never have, embassies and consular posts in all countries of the world. meanwhile, citizens of these countries travel the globe for tourism or business. and sometimes there are unfortunate events that require consular assistance and protection. the proposed directive provides for such protection not only for eu citizens but also for their family members from third countries. this is particularly important as it implements one of the fundamental principles of the eu charter of fundamental rights, which prohibits discriminatory treatment. the draft legislative act also contains a rule on respect for the right of citizens to make their own decisions, which should be reflected in respecting the will of each citizen, for example, in respect of not informing the next of kin about the event or taking into account the wishes of the family as to how the body of a deceased citizen should be disposed of. i believe that the entry into force of the directive will significantly improve the consular assistance process, but it should be noted that it has not yet fully exploited the possibilities offered by the lisbon treaty. in particular, the role of eu delegations, which should play a leading coordinating role and even, in strictly defined circumstances, perform consular functions, has been insufficiently emphasised.
in writing. − in view of the increasing mobility of union citizens across the globe and the legal and personal problems they face in third countries, i consider the directive on consular protection of union citizens abroad to be highly valuable and to give our citizens greater certainty as to where and to whom to turn when the institution of their country of origin is not available. i disagree with the voices that warn that such help will be costly. the draft directive is not about imposing additional tasks and costs on anyone, it is about giving both eu citizens and member states certainty and a legal framework for the procedure. it is also worth emphasising that greater coordination and a more efficient division of tasks between consulates of the member states will lead to a de facto reduction in costs. i am pleased that my opinion has been favourably received by the rapporteur and that many of the comments made by the legal affairs committee have been positively considered and incorporated into the final report. i also hope that the council will work with the necessary efficiency to ensure that our citizens can enjoy the full benefits of eu citizenship as soon as possible.
in writing. - during the inauguration of single market week, i heard that citizens are not aware of the benefits of the single market for them. this year's 20th anniversary of the single market is a great opportunity to reflect on how we can better inform citizens about these benefits and what more we need to do to unlock the full potential of the internal market, in particular to promote growth or create jobs. i am pleased that the report emphasises the need to inform europeans better about the internal market. identifying the problems that citizens and businesses encounter in the single market is certainly an important step towards creating a fully functioning single market. i supported the report because i believe that identifying these obstacles and the concerns of europeans is the key to adopting the appropriate legislation that will effectively address these identified problems. of course, it is not enough to create legislation, because it is also necessary for member states to implement it. only then can it work and bring tangible benefits to citizens. i also welcome the fact that the report calls for the monitoring of these identified concerns and problems of citizens and businesses in the internal market in the future, with a view to updating them. it is the citizens who remain at the heart of the eu, and i am pleased that this report is another expression of this.
in writing. − since 1992, the single market has been strengthening the ties between citizens and member states. its essence is the embodiment of an area without internal borders where people, goods, services and capital can move freely. many citizens of the eu, including many citizens of poland, have benefited from these freedoms. unfortunately, many individuals feel that there is a lack of information, and frequently people do not know – or do not sufficiently understand – their rights. they do not know how to obtain the required answers or assistance. this is something that the eu must try to fix. i believe that involving local and regional authorities in the process of informing citizens about their rights within the single market would be a good start. i completely agree that eu action is necessary and should be targeted and focused on the day-to-day problems faced by citizens. in addition, we have to review of all regulations which negatively impact smes, because they are the backbone of our economy.
in writing. − looking further into the subject, it is gratifying to note that the number of committees of inquiry has given it a special status. each of them has analysed in depth the risks that may accompany the emergence of a renewed single market. the subject is so vast that it is difficult to give any particular theme a special ring. a very wide range of issues, from vehicle registration to the needs of disabled people, shows the need for continuous revision of laws and regulations. there are three areas of concern for citizens regarding the functioning of the single market: lack of information, application gaps and legal gaps. sharing those concerns, i voted in favour.
in writing. − the main objective of the creation of the european single market was to strengthen the links between citizens and eu member states by creating a borderless area of free movement for people, goods, services and capital. today, after 20 years of the single market, we are seeing, in addition to the many important benefits it has brought, a certain disparity in the treatment of citizens and businesses, which is to some extent the cause of many of their concerns. these are mainly issues related to the exercise of rights in the field of professional qualifications, the transfer of pension and social security entitlements, as well as fiscal obstacles. the commission's efforts to stimulate growth and to strengthen confidence and competitiveness in the single market are commendable. however, much remains to be done, particularly in terms of adapting the eu legal framework to the existing economic and social conditions, the expectations of citizens and businesses, the full harmonisation of community law with member states' legislation and the need to inform citizens more fully about their rights. to this end, it is necessary to strengthen cooperation between parliament, the council, the commission and the member states. this seems to be the only way to remove the obstacles to innovation, growth, competitiveness, job creation and the confidence of european citizens in the single market in the midst of the economic, financial and social crisis in europe.
in writing. - having considered all aspects of the case and the opinions of the committee, i have decided to be neutral in this vote. the candidate's qualifications make it clear that he or she is qualified to be a member of the executive board of the ecb. however, having heard the opinion of the committee, which stresses the importance of promoting gender diversity in management bodies, and having in mind the european council's adoption of the gender pact 2011-2020 a year ago, i have decided as above.
in writing. − the international trade commission (inta), after examining the case of brosmann v council, in which the european court of justice (ecj) delivered a precedent-setting judgment on 2 february, has rightly decided to adopt the commission proposal amending the basis of the anti-dumping regulation (ec) no 1225/2009. the case was urgent because, following the ets ruling, that regulation had become invalid for the purposes of applying it to the examination of applications for market economy treatment under article 2 (7) (c). the ets judgment has shown that there is a need to provide that a decision to limit the investigation to a reasonable number of producers by means of a sample pursuant to article 17 of the regulation also applies to parties under investigation for the purpose of granting met pursuant to article 2 (7) (b) and (c). i also agree with my colleagues from inta that there is a need to introduce legal certainty and to align the regulation with the court's guidelines, as well as to add an amendment specifying the time of investigation in dumping cases, which must be more realistic. i therefore support the proposal to introduce a normal investigation period of 7 months with the possibility of extending it by another month in valid documented cases.
in writing. - i was strongly in favour of amending the regulation on the protection of the market against dumped prices. the threat posed by these practices could damage the economic relations between the cooperating countries. the regulation of anti-dumping duties and the use of the sampling technique will curb the incentives of dishonest producers. in the interests of good governance, these changes should be introduced as soon as possible (simplified procedure).
in writing. - i believe that the eu's priority is to deepen economic and trade relations with japan in all areas. today's data leaves much to be desired: the total volume of eu-japan bilateral trade in goods in 2011 was just eur 116.4 billion, compared with eur 444.7 billion in eu-us trade, eur 428.3 billion in eu-china trade and eur 306.6 billion in eu-russia trade. i am convinced that an eu-japan free trade agreement could benefit both economies. we would also like our partners in japan to effectively remove non-tariff barriers in order to remove a significant proportion of the barriers that impede trade between the eu and japan. i am referring to non-tariff barriers to trade in the automotive sector, such as zoning regulations and other anti-competitive restrictions and practices on electric and hybrid vehicles.
in writing. − following a resolution adopted by the ep in june, the inta committee adopted a resolution to contribute to the debate before the council authorises the mandate and launches negotiations with japan on a bilateral free trade agreement (fta). the report supports the launch of the eu-japan fta negotiations under a strict mandate. the fta should be comprehensive and ambitious and it should cover goods, services, investment, iprs and public procurement. special attention should be paid to the removal of ntbs. in this context, i fully support the further advances towards a reasonable eu-japan trade agreement.
in writing. − the european union's 2011 event was undoubtedly the launch of the parallel negotiation process for a binding agreement on global political cooperation, in particular on a free trade agreement, between the community countries and japan. the european union is japan's third largest trading partner after china and the us, while japan is the eu's sixth largest trading partner. the value of bilateral trade in the first 10 months of 2011 was approximately usd 145,2 billion. the eu is also the second largest investor in japan ($175 billion), while japan is the third largest investor in the eu ($75 billion). there are some 3300 japanese-owned companies in the eu, employing some 400 000 people. in view of the above, i am convinced that the potential for trade and investment cooperation between japan and the eu remains untapped, especially since trade between the two markets was supposed to be a stimulus to economic growth, not the other way around. attention should therefore be given both to factors that may currently hamper trade and economic cooperation between the two countries and to those that may stimulate it.
in writing. − given that the eu and japan together generate more than one third of global gdp, and yet bilateral trade is only eur 116 billion, negotiations on free trade and bilateral agreements should be undertaken with determination. following the experience of the eu-south korea free trade agreement, trade with japan should be significantly increased. in the broader context of globalisation, it is also important to have japan as a political ally. the eu's overarching objective is to deepen economic and trade relations with the world's major economies, such as japan, in order to maximise the potential for job creation. that's why i voted to negotiate with japan.

the rapporteur. - mr president! - what are you doing? i'm not going to let you get away with this. from the very beginning of the work on the report on the revision of the regulation on jurisdiction and the recognition and enforcement of judgments in civil matters, i was aware of the complexity of the matter before us. the desire to improve and facilitate the application of a regulation that is generally regarded as a very well-functioning instrument has proved difficult. we have had a lot of issues in the last couple of months, but i think we have been able to work out some satisfactory compromises on all of them, both the more controversial and the less controversial. we have had many meetings in informal trilateral talks during the polish, danish and cypriot presidencies, which have brought us closer together and have allowed us to understand each other's positions to such an extent that today we can speak of an agreement at first reading. the most important issue for which we opened the work on this regulation was the abolition of the exequatur procedure. during the polish presidency we reached a common approach which was overwhelmingly in line with the amendments i proposed in my report. the exequatur procedure will therefore be abolished, which will facilitate the circulation of judgments in civil and commercial matters, reducing the time taken to enforce judgments and significantly reducing the costs of the procedure. at the same time, any safeguards for the defendant which may become grounds for suspension or refusal of enforcement, including the public policy clause, shall be maintained. this change was made possible by a greater level of trust in the legal systems of the member states and today we can consider the abolition of the exequatur procedure as a joint success. the extension of the scope of the regulation to so-called third countries and the consequent 'rebound' has caused a lot of excitement in both the council and the parliament. from the beginning i was very sceptical about this issue - not the idea itself - but rather the rash decision to introduce such broadly defined changes to the brussels i regulation. the compromise reached at our meetings is that the extension of jurisdiction will be introduced for consumer contracts and individual employment contracts. this means that the consumer will be able to sue the seller even outside the union in his member state, including the one in which he lives. this approach has proved very attractive to both proponents and those who consider full harmonisation of jurisdictional rules to be premature. this is undoubtedly a step in the right direction towards widening access to justice for the so-called weaker party. at the same time, the inclusion of the review clause allows us to look in the coming months and years at the state of play of the judgments in these cases and the possible change in the harmonisation of the rules of jurisdiction. the arbitration agreements have been a complicated issue. after much discussion, parliament agreed that the best solution was to leave the status quo in this area, i.e. to leave arbitration entirely outside the scope of the regulation. the european parliament's position was reflected in the final compromise, because in the articles of the regulation we leave the status quo while explaining the application of this principle, in great detail, in the points of the preamble. another issue which i would like to stress is the importance of delegated acts for parliament. they were included in the commission's original proposal but were removed during the negotiations in the council. however, after swift intervention by parliament, the danish presidency restored the delegated acts to our full satisfaction. the question of the agreements on the choice of court also required a lot of thought, and i therefore turn with great appreciation to the cypriot presidency, which has presented specific points of the case in the preamble. i think they are detailed enough to help with any interpretation of the provisions in the articles. in conclusion, mr president, i would like to thank very warmly all the parties to this legislative process: the commission (and commissioner reding in particular), the polish, danish and cypriot presidencies, my colleagues and fellow shadow rapporteurs from the committee on legal affairs, and all those who were involved in the successful conclusion of the work.

in writing. more and more eu citizens are making payments with cards, over the internet or via mobile devices, resulting in a continuous growth of the e-commerce sector. in order to promote competitiveness, it is appropriate to eliminate differences between national and cross-border payments, including the emphasis on transparency of payment costs, which are currently in many cases hidden or exaggerated. this is particularly important to avoid a situation where fraudulent practices by different operators are repeated and where a credit card transaction fee is charged multiple times when several purchases are made in one payment transaction (my inquiry of 26 october 2010 e-8649/2010), as was the case with airlines. it is also necessary to standardise and harmonise the operation of payment terminals so that they can handle all types of cards. a separate and equally important issue to be addressed is the growing confidence of payers, who need to be convinced of the security of their electronic transactions. consumers who choose non-cash means of payment should be guaranteed the protection of their personal data and the security of their banking transaction data. the development of the single european payments area (sepa) requires the continued removal of a number of barriers to the functioning of the european payments market, which were identified by the ec in its green paper.
