the rapporteur. - my dear colleagues! ladies and gentlemen! i'm not going to let you do this. i am very pleased to present today the report on the social investment pact in response to the crisis, which was adopted almost unanimously by the employment committee at its meeting on 10 july. this report is part of a wider debate which has been taking place in europe for several years on the strategy for overcoming the economic and social crisis. as a result of the crisis, which continues to pose a real threat to the stability of many countries in the european union, we have been facing enormous problems in the european labour market for some time now, with an unemployment rate of over 10%, high youth unemployment and chronic unemployment among the low-skilled. this situation is exacerbated by demographic problems, a labour market-deficient education and training system and increasing pressure on the social security system. all the measures to restore the stability of public finances in the european union and the related budgetary cuts were and are necessary to ensure the stability of the european economy. without them, the impact of the crisis would undoubtedly be even more severe. however, these actions should be complemented by well-targeted social investments to prepare citizens for changing economic conditions and labour market needs. the crisis requires member states to rethink their social policies and to transform the active welfare state into an enabling state that invests in people and gives citizens the tools and incentives, rather than merely reacting to emerging harms caused by market imperfections. the budgetary policies of the member states should therefore be complemented by measures aimed, inter alia, at continuous improvement of the labour market, investment in education and training and the fight against poverty and social exclusion. social investment covers a wide range of policies and is therefore essential for ensuring the right level of employment in the future and for increasing europe's competitiveness. since they are designed to reconcile social and economic objectives, governments should not view them as an expense but, above all, as an investment that will yield real returns in the future. experience shows that attempts to coordinate the eu's approach to social investment, such as the lisbon strategy and the european employment strategy, have failed due to poor management. it is therefore necessary to ensure better monitoring of the implementation of employment and social policies in the member states of the european union. the report therefore proposes that member states should join the social investment pact, which would provide a better mechanism for managing and monitoring the implementation of the employment, social and education objectives, including those of the europe 2020 strategy. the monitoring of these policies should also be included in the 2013 european semester. in order to make these actions viable, it is also necessary that the 2014-2020 multiannual financial framework includes appropriate budgetary appropriations for social investment. in presenting the report entitled 'the social investment pact in response to the crisis', i would like to make it very clear that all the recommendations contained in it are the result of a broad consensus among all political groups, and i would like to thank the rapporteurs-at-large very warmly for the constructive and very good work on the report's texts, as well as all the colleagues who tabled amendments. i would like to take this opportunity to thank in particular professor frank van der broek, whose research has inspired me to prepare this report on social investment. i would also like to call on the european commission to take up the recommendations contained in the report and to propose instruments which will allow a number of good ideas to be put into practice, enabling our european society to cope with the difficult situation we are facing today. thank you, sir.
mr. chairman, please! the economic crisis and its negative effects on the economies of all countries force us to face new challenges. in the face of rising unemployment, especially among young people, and the increasing risk of poverty and social exclusion, it is essential to support broad social investment, including adaptation to labour market changes and the acquisition of new skills. we have discussed many times in this chamber the need to create mechanisms to promote labour mobility, the development of vocational training and the need to combat inequalities in the treatment of employees on grounds of sex. all these aspects of our earlier discussions regarding the social investment package are still relevant. moreover, they fit into it. i therefore call on the commission, as a very important element in the response to the crisis, to work with the governments of the member states to create mechanisms to promote social investment.
mr. chairman, please! i would like to begin by congratulating the rapporteur, mrs danuta jazłowiecka, on her excellent report and on tackling the important subject of social investment. the report comes at a crucial time when the european union's budget, both for next year and the financial framework for 2014-2020, is a hot topic. the union budget should be an investment budget, supporting the recovery from economic difficulties and focusing on strategic areas for growth and jobs. social investment, which links the social and economic dimensions, is a good way to implement effective and long-term measures to support adaptation to labour market changes, increase employment opportunities for young people, create conditions for the development of enterprises and develop the social economy. i therefore believe that ensuring that social investment is adequately supported financially is a prerequisite for the european union's economy to return to growth.
madam president, please! we have an italian evening in the european parliament. madam president, the commissioner, the vice-president of the european commission, the italian president, and we are discussing a very important issue. i take the floor as a former member of the transportation committee for two and a half years. i think that the debate today is so important that, although it is true that not everything can be regulated by legislation, and i am against this, it is precisely in this case that legislation is needed. indeed, the number of motorcycle accidents, including fatalities, is staggering, even in my own country. we also have a colleague from poland in this room, a member of the european parliament, who miraculously escaped death in a motorcycle accident. although he is not here today (it's a pity, because he could have taken the floor). i think these regulations are necessary, it's good that we're adopting them, i fully support them.
mr president, once again the union finds itself at a crossroads and this time we have a choice between two paths. one way to go is a more loosely integrated framework for the 28 member states, the second path will take us to a multi-tiered union with a stronger, deeply reformed, eurozone core. recent policy reforms have aligned us closer to the second path. there are, however, risks that come with this multi-tiered approach potentially leading to a more fragmented single market, but also repatriation of some policies back to national level and a weaker role for the union in the global world. an eu dominated by a strong core and a large periphery might give policymakers less firepower for a sound global position for europe as a whole. the question of whether a single voice in international institutions for the core only will be the best solution might emerge. as this multi-tiered europe becomes a reality, we should be alert concerning potential risks. we need to minimise unwanted spillovers to the greatest extent possible, and the core may be strong enough to provide the necessary impetus for this, but on the flipside it might not be sufficiently powerful to keep the eu together. let me conclude by saying that i admire the efforts of marianne thyssen to keep us together and, at the end of the day, which scenario will materialise depends on the way we design and manage this ensuing multi-tiered structure. that is why our work is so important.
in the light of today's discussion, i'd like to ask a few questions and make a few comments: 1. lack of a social dimension among the four pillars of strengthening economic and monetary union. 2.is there a need to amend the treaties? we already have some instruments: the six-pack, the two-pack, the fiscal pact, the european semester. the question of openness to non-euro area countries. 4.the need for the european parliament to be fully involved in its work. there should be no question of creating a separate assembly for the euro area. 5.the problem of further delegation at the level of the european union. this is about the loss of identity by member states. the effectiveness of action planning. is the european union credible in its actions? seven, the public doesn't understand anything we do. how can we better inform the public to communicate our intentions for economic strengthening and the various forms of crisis response at european union level? why at union level and not just at national level? how does the budget for the financial perspective 2014-2020 relate to this? thank you, sir.
in writing. the european union and its member states are experiencing another year of huge economic problems. the crisis that began with the collapse of the us banks in 2008 has hit young people the hardest. we should regard as a personal failure the fact that as many as 22% of them are unemployed and in some member states the unemployment rate for this age group is over 50%. the paradox is that the so-called erasmus generation - the first generation of true europeans - is increasingly being described as 'lost'. therefore, in preparing recommendations to lead to the creation of a de facto economic and monetary union, full use should be made of all the instruments provided for in the treaties. i agree with the rapporteur that the social policy potential of the lisbon treaty is not being fully exploited. strong action is needed to support and complement member states' efforts to integrate people excluded from the labour market. this exclusion is particularly relevant for young people. studies show that if they fail to find stable and fairly paid employment within a few years of leaving school, they will be permanently excluded from the labour market. instead of building the future of the union, they will be a source of instability and many problems. we should therefore do everything we can to ensure that these young people, who are often well educated, can reach their full potential. if we lose this generation, we lose the union and the good future of europe.
i'm not going to let you do this. europe is in crisis. in addition to the economic crisis, we have a social crisis linked to unemployment. the european industry is facing increasingly difficult conditions for further development as we impose more and more obligations on it. if it is a commitment to new technology and innovation, we all applaud it. however, most of the conditions imposed are to increase the financial burden. i have a fundamental question on this matter. the european emissions trading system is currently being revised. i ask: why should they be used, knowing that they will lead to the escape of industry outside europe? thank you, sir.
the worst element for the industry is the lack of regulatory continuity and unpredictability in the long run. it is therefore important that the law that is being created in europe is stable. i also wanted to know whether the commissioner would take steps to ensure that the rules remain stable for longer periods, at least ten or fifteen years. we know that investments in industry have a long investment life and investors in industry need to know that the money they invest will come back to them and that it will actually be used in the future.
mr. chairman, please! my question is directed to commissioner tajani. akio morita, co-founder of sony, said 20 years ago in davos that only manufacturing can provide a solid employment at the right scale, and the service sector can survive if there is an industry that can support those services. it is increasingly clear that the main problem facing europe is the flight of industry to other countries and regions of the world. let us not be deceived: until we rebuild our industrial sector on our continent, we will not eliminate the main causes of european economic stagnation. more than two years ago, mario monti pointed out that the union needed a new industrial policy to stimulate the economy. once again, however, it was all words and papers. does the european commission not think that it may be time to start work on a common european industrial policy? if the united states, china and japan have different types of instruments to support domestic investment, it is worthwhile to explore such solutions for europe as well. what are the solutions that we should be using today to develop european industry?
i would like to address my supplementary question to both of you, although i have the impression that it is really a question, a simple question, which should be addressed to the whole commission. many, especially young talent, european talent, to spread their wings, go outside europe, to the united states, to china. what does the european commission intend to do to keep these talents in europe, so that europe finally becomes the continent that leads in innovation, leads in new technologies, leads in interesting initiatives?
madam president! the changing economic situation and the fight against the economic crisis are creating the need for changes in the european labour market and in education systems. the european union should develop a social investment plan, i.e. targeted actions to activate european society, focusing on investing in individuals, families and social groups. that is why, in my report adopted today, i am encouraging member states to sign up to the so-called social investment pact, which will promote, among other things, investment in lifelong learning, business-school cooperation, and on-the-job training and specific training in sectors affected by labour shortages. social investment should aim to instill in us from kindergarten the entrepreneurial and self-reliance qualities that have been dormant in some aspects of social policy today. that is why i voted for this report and why i prepared it, and i would like to thank once again the colleagues who have worked with me.
madam president! the current complex type-approval structure is primarily a source of significant, largely unjustified costs for operators and thus indirectly for customers. the european commission's proposal to simplify procedures is therefore aimed at reducing costs for citizens. the report also contains desirable solutions, such as the harmonisation of exhaust emission requirements and the introduction of safeguards against unauthorised manipulation of vehicles. the inclusion of four-wheel agricultural vehicles in the scope of the tractor regulation should also result in improved road safety. thanks to the efforts of my political group, the introduction of the ab system in motorcycles will only cover single-track motorcycles with a higher power output, and will therefore not apply to those with a larger engine and to scooters. the impact assessment has shown that the existing cheaper braking systems are sufficient for these vehicles. the sustainability requirements for motorcycles and the timetable for the introduction of new provisions also take into account our comments. i therefore support this report.
madam president! the current multiplicity of regulatory provisions on the production of agricultural and forestry vehicles has created a complex system of market surveillance in this field. the commission's proposal to cover these matters in a single regulation therefore seems to be the optimal solution and that is why i supported the resolution. it is worth noting in particular that virtually all types of tractors are subject to the approval requirement, with the exception of manufacturers of trailers and towed equipment. however, it is worth noting that the possession of an eu type-approval allows the vehicle to be driven throughout the union. the introduction of a distinction between tractors on the basis of speed will also clarify the unclear provisions in this field. the additional requirements will only apply to higher-speed machines. the practical elimination of the competitive disadvantages for off-road vehicles, whose manufacturers will be able to obtain type-approval for all types of category t, will be of major importance. farmers will therefore not be burdened with the potential unjustified costs of any modifications to the vehicles.
in writing. - i am pleased with the results of the months of negotiations on new rules of jurisdiction and the recognition and enforcement of judgments. the most important element of the new regulation is the possibility of automatic recognition of crossborder judgments in civil and commercial matters issued in different member states. previously, the cost of confirming judgments varied between eur 2 000 and eur 12 000, depending on the country. the abolition of this time-consuming and very costly procedure will save over eur 47 million per year and will also make it faster and easier for union citizens to exercise their rights. it is also important that member states have retained the right to suspend or refuse entirely to enforce a judgment where it is incompatible with their legal order. in addition, the extension of the procedures to include the possibility of bringing a case in any country of the union against a company or its employee outside the member states, as proposed in the report, will make it much easier to enforce rights in disputes of an international nature. i agree with the rapporteur that this is a good step towards simplifying and harmonising european legal rules to keep pace with the challenges of the single market. the new regulation, which strengthens the current legal framework, will not only facilitate citizens' access to justice under article 23 tfeu, but also make it more understandable and less costly for them, which perfectly reflects the trend towards a more transparent and friendly community law.
in writing. − the introduction of a new section on jurisdiction in collective action cases in the regulation will improve access to justice, inter alia by allowing employees to bring actions against several defendants in the area of employment at the same time in accordance with article 6 (1). that is why i voted for this regulation.
in writing. − the proposal aims to reduce the frequency and impact of terrorist attacks by limiting access by general users to substances or mixtures thereof that are legally used on a large scale but can be used as precursors to explosives. that's why i voted yes.
in writing. - i have read the regulation carefully. in my country, the threat of explosives has been the headline news these past few days. all this after the special services arrested a man who was planning to assassinate the polish authorities with explosives. i voted with conviction for the document. security is one of the most important values of the european union society, which we should take care of. especially now, in times when we are particularly vulnerable to terrorist attacks. at the same time, i am pleased that the author has taken into account in the regulation that certain chemicals are widely used for legitimate uses by ordinary users. therefore, with a reasonable margin of safety for citizens, the document does not impose disproportionately stringent restrictions. this will not have a negative impact on the economy or civil liberties, and will effectively prevent potential attackers from accessing dangerous substances. i believe that the european commission, the competent authorities of the member states and international services will continue to monitor the market for these substances. it is important that their market is properly monitored in order to add a new substance to the annex or to remove a substance from the annex in a timely manner.
in writing. − the report endorses the arrangements for preparing recruitment procedures for the european institutions before croatia's accession to the european union on 1 january 2013. it is important that the administration is prepared for the enlargement process so as to enable the new member states to have equal representation in brussels as soon as possible. poland also benefited from similar provisions in 2004.

in writing. − the conclusion of bilateral fisheries agreements, known as fisheries partnership agreements, with third countries is a key element of the external dimension of the common fisheries policy (cfp). these agreements commit the parties to promote a responsible and sustainable fisheries policy, which is why i voted in favour.
in writing. − the report approves amendments to the directive on eu citizens standing for election to the european parliament in countries other than their country of origin. article 18 of the eu treaty guarantees that any citizen of the union may stand for election to the european parliament in any eu country. this is an important dimension of european citizenship, established by the maastricht treaty 20 years ago. the amendments to the directive introduce practical arrangements to facilitate the practical implementation of this treaty provision.
in writing. − the next elections to the european parliament are coming up in june 2014. in times of growing euroscepticism, we should be particularly concerned to ensure that the citizens of the union participate as widely as possible in elections and that parliament's mandate is as strong as possible. one of the formal and legal limitations to voting is the difficulty of voting in a country where voters are resident but not citizens. this is a growing group of people who are looking for work or study in other countries. unfortunately, the proposed directive does not solve this problem. it does not extend voting rights, but only introduces administrative facilitation for potential candidates. so it facilitates the candidacy, but it does not support the implementation of the electoral law, which is the possibility of actually participating in elections. this solution is therefore far from sufficient.
in writing. − as some countries have not met the deadlines for transposing the rules on the functioning of financial institutions, it is necessary to monitor their implementation in order to safeguard consumers' interests. for example, differences in the interpretation of the period of notice for a credit agreement require clarification. particular attention should be paid to encouraging financial institutions to provide consumers with comprehensive, relevant and understandable information on the risks of borrowing in foreign currencies before signing any contract. last year's inspection of consumer credit websites revealed that almost half of the websites lacked mandatory information, mainly on the cost and duration of contracts, which is therefore of the utmost importance. the growing popularity of sms lending is also of interest, as it can often put a potential customer in a situation where there is no way out, even though it has many advantages. efforts should be made to ensure effective consumer protection in this respect. i support the report.
in writing. − consumer credit is often a key element in raising the standard of living of citizens. unfortunately, unclear rules, lack of information or even consumer-friendly regulations mean that this instrument cannot really be fully exploited. the consumer credit directive provides consumers with a high level of protection and strengthens the internal market for cross-border consumer credit. the good instrument is therefore in force; unfortunately, it cannot fulfil its objectives unless it is correctly and efficiently implemented in the national legal systems of the member states. i support the report because i fully agree that the correct transposition of eu law by member states, without undue delay, is absolutely necessary for consumers to be effectively protected and for the single market to function properly in this respect. the transposition process was particularly problematic with regard to advertising, pre-contractual information, early repayment and the calculation of the annual interest rate. some member states also failed to meet the deadlines for transposition. i therefore believe that the european commission should monitor the transposition and insist that the member states apply the directive correctly.
in writing. - the consumer credit directive will contribute to achieving a high level of consumer protection and strengthening the internal market for cross-border consumer credit, which is why i voted in favour of the directive.
in writing. − last month, unemployment in europe exceeded 25 million for the first time, and almost 80 million europeans are at risk of poverty and social exclusion. in some countries, the majority of this percentage are between 18 and 24 years of age. the situation is indeed very difficult, which is why creating new jobs has become one of the european union's top priorities. the key issues for europe's development seem to be increasing employment, especially among young people, facilitating the transition from education to employment, investing in entrepreneurship and promoting and facilitating the creation of one's own business. this will be possible, among other things, thanks to the social investment pact, which i voted for today. the pact provides for a series of actions to increase the competitiveness of european workers, significantly increasing the number of new jobs for young people by, for example, introducing graduate recruitment incentives for employers and creating good conditions for business development. thank you very much. thank you.
in writing. − social investment is essential to ensure the future of employment and to increase europe's competitiveness. since they are designed to reconcile social and economic objectives, governments should view them not only as expenditure but also as investments that will yield real returns in the future. moreover, the crisis seems to require member states to rethink their social policies and to transform the 'welfare state' into an 'activating welfare state' that invests in people and gives citizens tools and incentives, rather than just acting in response to emerging harms caused by market imperfections. in view of the above, it is necessary to ensure that social investment is an essential part of european economic and employment policies and of the eu's response to the crisis. that's why i voted yes.
in writing. - i congratulate the member of parliament danuta jazłowiecka for her excellent work. i voted with conviction to accept this report. the development of a broad social economy can be very helpful at a time when it is not only the homeless, the long-term unemployed or the disabled who are left without a job and with very limited financial means to survive. the crisis, which affects both employers and workers, is making the labour market more volatile. in times of crisis and continuous job cuts, more and more citizens are at risk of poverty. social enterprises, social cooperatives or professional activities establishments are designed to generate a profit which is then used to achieve social objectives or develop the local community. so they are effective tools to help solve social problems that are important to all of us. social entrepreneurship can also be an opportunity for young people who are unable to enter the labour market. as danuta jazłowiecka rightly pointed out in her report, social policies in eu countries need to change dynamically and introduce effective and long-term ways of tackling social problems. social investment is the best example of this and every effort should be made to ensure that it can thrive in the free market as a strong player in the future and become an effective means of preventing social exclusion.
in writing. − the right to remuneration for the resale of a work is one of the first mechanisms to harmonise intellectual property law across the union. the directive, which was not fully implemented in all member states until 1 january 2012, protects the interests of authors by guaranteeing them the continuity of the remuneration received for each subsequent professional resale of the work, and ensures that the buyer never owns the work 100% and, if he decides to sell it through a 'commercial intermediary', must share in the proceeds. the complex legal issue, which is not easily understood by ordinary citizens, has not, it seems, affected the position of the european art market, which recorded record profits of usd 11.57 billion in 2011, an increase of more than usd 2 billion compared to 2010. third countries, following this trend, are also planning to introduce uniform rules on resale law, which would in practice create a level playing field and contribute to the development of competitiveness. in this context, i support the proposal to postpone the commission's review of the directive from 2014 to 2015, 4 years after the last assessment presented in december 2011, in order to make the assessment of the applicable rates, thresholds and categories of beneficiaries clearer and more appropriate for both artists and subsequent owners of works. the main aim of the directive was to ensure that authors of works of art have a share in the economic success of their works and to harmonise the application of this right throughout the eu. as the estimated value of the european art market for 2012 is usd 12 billion, this law is meeting the challenges it faces.
in writing. − i voted in favour because there are differences between the member states in the quality of the administration of the resale right and the directive on the resale right aims to harmonise the application of this right throughout the eu and to ensure that artists have a share in the economic success of their works.

in writing. − in today's vote i voted in favour of a proposal for a directive to make all new motorcycles, three-wheelers and quads sold in the european union from 2016 safer and more environmentally friendly. under the new rules, larger motorcycles (i.e. those with engines over 125 cc) must be equipped with anti-lock braking systems (abs) and smaller ones (with engines under 125 cc) must have abs or combined braking systems (cbs). all motorcycles from 2016 will also meet the euro 4 emission standard. i believe that the new legislation we have voted on will improve road safety and reduce the number of accidents involving motorcycles and atvs. one of the main reasons why i believe that we should support the adoption of more stringent safety requirements is the alarming statistic that these vehicles, although they represent only 2% of road users, are involved in as many as 16% of fatal accidents.
in writing. - i support the report on the approval and market surveillance of two-, three- and four-wheel vehicles. these are l-category vehicles, and the number in the european union is estimated at over 30 million. in poland, too, this category of vehicles is constantly expanding, as it concerns mopeds, motorcycles and so-called quads. although these vehicles account for only 3 percent of the total mileage of public transportation, their share of fatalities is alarmingly high, as much as 16 percent. therefore, i consider it appropriate to increase the safety of these vehicles by making it mandatory to have anti-lock braking systems (abs) and automatic headlamp switches so that vehicles in this category are visible. in supporting the safety of these vehicles, i would like to draw attention to the fact that this must lead to an increase in the price of motorcycles, motorcycles and quad bikes. so the question is, is it worth it? i believe it is worth it, because the protection of human life, especially that of young people, is worth every penny.

the rapporteur. - madam president! - what are you doing? during the many months of work on this report, i have been able to hear the expertise of many scientists, engineers, practitioners and officials. my goal was to present a report that is not written from a desk, but that actually presents and discusses all aspects of the extraction process of this raw material and the technology used. i've been to shale gas drilling sites, and i've talked to politicians, environmentalists, community leaders. the experience gained was reflected in my proposal for a report. i am glad that a balanced compromise has been reached at the level of my committee on the environment, where the shadow rapporteurs have shared my cautious approach, which emphasises the highest environmental standards and stringent requirements, but at the same time gives shale a chance, a chance to be commercially viable. europe cannot afford not to use its own resources, which can not only help reduce dependence on external supplies and increase the eu's energy security, but also contribute to a policy of reducing emissions. the main message of my report is the already repeated demands for a review of current legislation at eu and national level, better implementation of current legislation, the creation of a catalogue of best available practices and techniques, the highest technological standards, continuous monitoring, full transparency of activities and the responsibility of operators. the obligation to declare the chemical composition of hydraulic fluids in accordance with reach, the minimisation of water consumption in the fracturing process, the efficient recycling of returned water and chemicals, and the careful selection of the location of wells should also be a non-discussed standard. we must not forget that the success of the whole project depends on the social acceptance and approval of the citizens. a sustained dialogue with the local community and a pan-european in writing. while congratulating the rapporteur, it is worth noting that the revolution in shale gas exploration and exploitation that is taking place before our eyes could prove to be a real boon for europe. the extraction of shale gas on the one hand means diversification of gas fuel sources, which is a prerequisite for ensuring energy security, and on the other hand it ensures the reduction of emissions from combustion, the reduction of air pollution from the energy sector and the increase of energy efficiency. the eu economy needs shale gas to recover and help create jobs, while breaking the link between economic growth and co2 emissions. shale gas means better implementation of the union's climate policy through a change in the energy balance resulting from a gradual move away from a high-carbon economy and towards greener energy sources. is it possible to extract shale gas and not lose anything? of course, this is what our colleagues are saying in the reports we are discussing today. the recipe is simple: transparent regulations, honest dialogue with the public and environmental organisations, promotion of the safest extraction technologies, dedicated monitoring of the areas where extraction takes place. europe needs good, cheap energy to keep growing, so it has been given the gift of shale gas. to reject it would be a grave mistake, to exclude our continent from being a respected player in the world energy market.
in writing. in the face of economic collapse, all steps must be taken to strengthen european competitiveness, strengthen the economies of the individual community countries and reduce the cost of living for citizens. there must be a consensus in parliament on these objectives. i don't understand the behaviour of the representatives of the european left any more. behaviour that is not only contrary to the spirit of integration, but also to common sense. the attack on shale gas the remedy for europe's energy problems is marked by the one-sided, narrow-minded viewpoint that has characterized the lobbyists of russia's gazprom the monopoly that loses the most on shale gas extraction. let me remind you that a recent cera report estimates that shale gas reserves in europe are 173 trillion cubic metres. the ability to extract and exploit up to 10% of these geological resources is a game changer for european gas security and a major boost to the european economy. this is all the more so as cera estimates that by 2025 european gas production should be between 60 and 200 billion m3. moreover, unlike russian gas, it is located within the boundaries of the european market. consequently, once europe has developed its extraction of unconventional gas and has adequately controlled its costs, it will be in strong competition with both russian gas transported from far siberia and lng produced from shale gas and imported into europe from the usa.

vice-president of the commission. − mr president, first i would like to thank madam lichtenberger for her report, her continued support and for the gentle pressure she continuously exercises on the commission in this very important area of cooperation. as we have clearly indicated in our 2010 annual report on monitoring the application of eu law, it is quite clear that our two institutions attach great importance to the correct application of eu law. i very much appreciate the opportunity to have regular exchanges of views on this subject. with regard to the issues raised in the report by ms lichtenberger, i would just like to highlight the following points. firstly, i am very pleased that parliament endorses the commission’s smart regulation approach. as an important element of this policy, the commission will continue to assist member states in their efforts to transpose directives in a timely fashion. if, despite these efforts the member states miss the transposition deadline, the commission will systematically propose financial penalties and sanctions, exactly as was highlighted and suggested by ms lichtenberger. the commission will also work with the member states to ensure that eu law is correctly implemented on the ground. i am equally grateful for the report’s positive tone with regard to the early resolution of problems related to the application of eu law. we will continue to work with the member states to try to solve the problems. the objective is for the infringement procedure to become unnecessary, since problems could be solved at an earlier stage. this would benefit, first and foremost, citizens and businesses. however, i repeat once more that, if no solution is found, the commission will vigorously use the legal instruments at its disposal. the 20th annual report underlined once again that petitions from citizens and businesses are very valuable signals highlighting possible violations of eu law. the same is true for complaints from citizens and organisations, with 4 000 complaints having been received in 2010. i take note of parliament’s remarks on procedural law under article 298 of the treaty. we consider that the complainants already benefit from the comprehensive administrative guarantees, and we will have the occasion to continue the discussion on this issue when the report by mr berlinguer is tabled in parliament’s plenary session. concerning transparency – the item raised by ms lichtenberger on infringement procedures – and especially the transparency of eu pilot projects, the commission fully complies with the rules laid down in the revised framework agreement from the very start of investigations into cases. the legal and factual elements are often unclear, and since we strive to have correct information and respect the principle of sincere cooperation with the member states, it is not possible to divulge full information at certain stages of the procedure, especially early on. the commission welcomes parliament’s interest in ensuring the correct application of eu law for the benefit of eu citizens and businesses, and the commission looks forward to continuing its work with parliament on this very important aspect of the smart regulation agenda.

the rapporteur. - mr president, commissioner, i have to ask you to leave. the multiannual plan for the conservation of baltic salmon is a very important element of the management of marine resources in the context of the common fisheries policy. i must refer to the role of the multiannual management plans and the impasse in the council which blocks their implementation. the regulation provides for a comprehensive approach to the protection of salmon in the baltic sea, covering new areas and issues not covered by the common fisheries policy. i would like to mention here that a wide-ranging consultation of stakeholders has taken place. because of time constraints, i'm going to focus on just a few. one of the main issues covered in this report is recreational fishing, which is still unregulated and has a significant impact on the state of the stocks. the lack of regulation has led to the uncontrolled growth of recreational fisheries in some countries, and the introduction of specific names for vessels, such as service vessels, has put them out of control, contributing to the growth of unreported catches of baltic salmon. there are also known cases where recreational fisheries have used advanced fishing gear such as trawls. member states have not complied with their obligations to provide adequate information on catches, which has resulted in a poor estimate of the stock of salmon in the baltic sea. the second issue not covered by the existing regulations is the impact of predators on the baltic salmon population. the commission has also concluded that the measures provided for in this decision are in accordance with the opinion of the standing committee on plants, animals, food and feed, this report shall specify the studies to be carried out in order to determine dependencies and to assess the resources correctly. another important issue is the reproduction of baltic salmon. in the current situation, we are facing a decline in salmon populations, and trying to establish rigid limits to the reproductive potential is not a good solution, because it can contribute to further decline in the population. the possibility of a flexible method of fishing adapted to the current state of the stock should be maintained. mr president, commissioner, i have to ask you to leave. the current common fisheries policy has not been a success, but rather a victim of the environment, its resources, fishermen and the coastal community. the multiannual conservation plans and, above all, the new common fisheries policy, are intended to be a solution to the current, diametrically opposed situation. this is the only way out of the crisis, which should be accepted by the commission, the council and the european parliament. only then will we be able to make a difference. now, at this point, i would like to ask the council whether we will have the chance to proceed further with the codecision procedure. will the blockade which the council is currently imposing on parliament in individual agreements continue? unfortunately, we don't have that chance, because the board has probably already made a decision and it's just not there.

in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because i believe that mutual defence and solidarity in case of aggression is the foundation of lasting peace in europe. i believe that nato is the ‘keystone in the arch’ in this regard, but the eu also has its role to play. twenty-one eu member states are also members of nato. but we also need to be prepared for situations involving non-nato eu member states or eu member states’ territories that are outside the north atlantic area and are therefore not covered by the washington treaty, or situations where no agreement on collective action has been reached within nato. i am glad that in the report, we have reminded member states of their unequivocal obligation of aid and assistance by all the means in their power if a member state is the victim of armed aggression on its territory. the definition of ‘aggression’ is also changing and i strongly agree with the statement that non-armed attacks, for instance cyber-attacks against critical infrastructure that are launched with the aim of causing severe damage and disruption to a member state and are identified as coming from an external entity, could fall under this category.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because i believe that cyber challenges, threats and attacks are growing at a dramatic pace and constitute a major threat to the security, defence, stability and competitiveness of the eu member states as well as our private sector. we all remember the three-week wave of massive cyber attacks waged against estonia in 2007. for this reason, eu institutions should develop their cyber security strategies and contingency plans to include in their risk analysis and crisis management plans the issue of cyber crisis management. this should be done in cooperation with nato and our ally, the united states. we should deepen eu-us mutual cooperation to counter cyber attacks and cybercrime, as these are threats which we can expect to increase in the future.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because i believe that it tackles a phenomenon which we are witnessing more and more. populations with deteriorating access to fresh water and foodstuffs as a result of natural catastrophes are forced to migrate, thereby overstretching the economic, social and administrative capabilities of already fragile regions or failing states and creating conflict. thus it is important that the eu, in its external action strategies, policies and instruments, takes into consideration the effects of natural disasters and changes in the climate on international security and further strengthens and develops existing instruments that can deliver humanitarian aid.

mr. chairman, please! after more than 30 years of what might have seemed impossible negotiations, we are now at the end of such an important legislative process as the patent package, which allows inventions to be protected by a single patent application covering 25 eu countries, greatly simplifying today's complex system and reducing the cost of patenting by up to 80%. the tool for increasing competitiveness and the community market is finally ready. the cost of obtaining patents in the union is now ten times higher than in the us, and the total cost of obtaining a patent covering the entire territory of the union is now estimated at around eur 25 000. with the package, these costs can be reduced by five times. until now, many european inventors could not afford such expensive protection of their intellectual property, so they often sold their technical ideas overseas. the proposed unitary patent system provides inventors with a choice of available patent protection tailored to their needs. the european union is not imposing on businesses, but is simply putting in their hands new patent protection tools - faster, cheaper and safer than before. each individual will now be able to decide for himself which solution is most advantageous to him and to choose between a national patent, a european patent valid in one or more of the contracting states of the european patent convention, or the unitary patent currently being created. this is an opportunity for all, including small and medium-sized enterprises, which can greatly benefit from this proposal, as it provides for special facilities for translation and eu programmes to support patent initiatives. after months of debate, i believe that a compromise has been reached to the satisfaction of all parties on the transfer of articles 6 to 8 of the regulation to the interinstitutional agreement (the unified patent court agreement) and thus on the maintenance of the appropriate legal basis and the operability of the text. the design is still consistent, only slightly modified from the original version. i would like to congratulate the rapporteurs, mr rapkay, mr baldassarre, mr lehne and mr barnier on a very good final document.
mr. chairman, please! we are debating today very important changes in the legal system of the european union, which, despite the extremely optimistic tone of this interesting debate, unfortunately also involve real risks that must be borne in mind, especially in relation to the small and medium-sized enterprises sector, especially from the new member states of the european union those smaller member states of the european union. the new rules give an exceptionally strong position to multinational companies, mainly from the major countries of the european union, japan and the usa. in 2011 alone, 88% of patents issued by european patent offices came from these countries. the proposed rules will allow them to better protect their patents and at the same time increase their profits by using their monopoly on their use, and it must be remembered that sometimes patent strategies are also used by these large companies to block and hinder new companies from entering the market. for example, the small and medium-sized enterprises sector in poland accounts for 76% of gdp and, according to deloitte's analysis, the cost of obtaining patents will increase very significantly, causing an increase in the costs of the polish economy of pln 28 billion over 30 years. so you have to see these doubts and think about them.
madam president! the european patent protection system was designed to stimulate innovation and facilitate access to judicial protection. the patent package, however, has the opposite effect. its introduction means that most citizens and companies will be forced to accept in bulk patents created outside their own jurisdiction in languages that are not official languages in their territory. the judgement in these cases will be transferred to foreign courts, which will conduct proceedings in foreign languages. this will increase translation, procedural and legal costs. access to justice and legal protection will be hampered. a system will be created where the strong will become stronger and the weak will be weakened. the european patent package will thus become a protectionist mechanism that will make it harder for smaller players to enter the innovation market. given that most patents are filed by companies in the small and medium-sized enterprises sector, the proposed regulations will restrict competition to the detriment of european innovation.
madam president! winston churchill once said, "every time i've been right, i've been outnumbered". i remember being in the minority in this room against sugar reform, and i was right, because it had very bad consequences. and today i am in the minority - judging by the debate so far - in opposing the uniform patent act, and i do so because in my country, poland, this act is perceived very differently by the economic circles, including by the scientists dealing with this issue. they see the cost of both obtaining and enforcing patent protection increasing, particularly for small and medium-sized enterprises. they see the regulations in the draft as subordinated to the interests of powerful users of the patent system with crossborder disputes with a large territorial reach. i would like to add that i am strongly opposed to the patenting of living organisms, plants and animals. this kind of patent protection is harmful to agriculture, it leads to the treatment of agriculture as an industry and this too is unacceptable. that's why i'm voting against the uniform patent act.
in writing. this regulation is not yet a community patent, which the union has been trying to introduce without effect for years. we have to wait for such an innovative patent, not only in terms of legal procedure but also in terms of form. this case is, in my opinion, crucial. some current patent-molochs, such as those in the field of pharmaceuticals, are as long as 800 pages! an innovative standard of patent form is needed to shorten the patent period, eliminate high translation costs and generally reduce the total cost of protection. the current patent law has been deliberately - in my opinion - so confused that it serves mainly its strongest actors rather than the real innovators. a so-called uniform patent protection system is based on the current patent law; it favours large and wealthy corporations and discriminates against small and medium-sized enterprises, especially those from central and eastern european countries. the proposed regulation is a flawed draft containing many unknowns. it does not analyse the real effects on member states' economies, but oddly expresses concern for the non-eu budget of the european patent office. why no simulation of the administrative costs of the epo and the costs of the common patent court? i suspect this project was prepared by the epo. thank you, sir.

in writing. − under the current legal system, a company wishing to protect its product throughout the union must obtain a patent from the european patent office in munich and certify it in each eu country. its costs are the payment of patent attorneys, translators and clerks. in total, to get protection in 25 eu countries, a company has to spend 41,000 euros. to this must be added eur 28 000 to ensure that the protection is valid for 10 years. the introduction of the unitary european patent will significantly reduce the cost of patent protection. the cost of obtaining patent protection in 25 european countries (excluding italy and spain) will be €5.5 thousand per patent and €7.5 thousand for its maintenance. this is a clear win for the most innovative entrepreneurs, on whom the economy should be based. so is the polish economy. it is high time for poland to invest in innovation. we certainly cannot be afraid of innovation, otherwise the so-called development drift scenario will become a real threat to poland. moreover, as analyses available to the polish ministry of economy show, the rejection of the unitary european patent will mean that the polish economy will lose pln 48 billion over the next 30 years. the work on the single european patent has been going on for over 35 years. it's time they were terminated. to the benefit of the competitiveness of the european economy.
in writing. - i strongly object to the wording of this resolution. the introduction of the single european patent is a threat to the european economy and could worsen the situation of small and medium-sized enterprises. as i mentioned earlier, they are at the heart of europe's economic development and should therefore be at the centre of our attention. these costs are enormous, especially in terms of administrative and operational costs. in the new european countries, the jurisdiction of the sme sector will increase fivefold. the cost of purchasing licences under the new system will be, depending on the scenario, between 90% and 180% higher than the current system. the cost of patent clearance will increase by as much as 40 times. it is also difficult to calculate the cost of the time spent by entrepreneurs in completing documents. all this with the constant cost of obtaining a patent and the constant cost of opening up new markets. it is therefore worth asking the question of the meaning of further development of the unitary european patent.
in writing. - i voted against the report by raffaele baldassari on the proposal for a council regulation introducing enhanced cooperation in the area of the creation of a unitary patent protection system with regard to the relevant translation arrangements, even though i know that a unitary patent is needed in europe. however, at the moment, with the design of the patent, i think the long-term costs of introducing it may outweigh the benefits.
in writing. − for nearly 50 years we have been working to introduce a common patent protection system in europe that would be able to ensure easy, cheap and fair registration of designs on a european scale. the problems we faced were the enormous costs of patent examination in a few or a dozen countries, which, because of the translation work that is usually required and the annual renewal fees, were several times higher than the patent costs in countries like the united states and japan. moreover, the legal protection of a design at union level has forced the patent holder to engage in legal disputes in many countries, on different grounds, since infringement cases were subject to national jurisdiction. today, in the quest to simplify and standardise the system, we should focus on patent holders, with particular attention to small and medium-sized enterprises, which are crucial to our economy. the documents adopted today should make a strong demand for cost reductions and simplification of administrative procedures, as well as for free translation services for those wishing to register their project abroad. the single patent system should extend the business opportunities of our entrepreneurs, not just the largest ones, to the entire european market and provide them with the legal protection they deserve. i cannot therefore accept the report as it stands, as the provisions contained therein may impose a heavy financial burden on undertakings in some member states.
in writing. the european parliament has voted on reports which introduce a number of ambiguities both as regards the definition of the patent market and the potential licensing associated with it. the market share of the 25 contracting states suggests that speculation in licences in these countries is permissible. the commission's definition of the innovation market, originally based on population, i.e. potential future demand, should also have been adopted. the regulations adopted do not protect all single market economies equally from global competition; instead, they may make it more difficult for existing smes in the weaker eu countries to operate, subjecting them both to the monopoly of large corporations from financially stronger eu countries and non-eu corporations, and reducing the innovation of those who are already merely duplicating existing solutions. on the one hand, the cost of patenting itself will be significantly reduced, while on the other hand, the cost of legal defence against real or imagined intellectual property infringement claims may be higher. the latter issue may concern mainly countries with an official language other than that adopted in the regulations. i voted against because the proposed regulations completely ignore the possibility of further reducing the cost of patenting through new standards for the preparation of patent descriptions, which would eliminate the non-transparent and very expensive patent giants. that's too bad. it was a unique opportunity to generate an innovative, cheaper than the us and japan, real european patent, in line with the existing convention.
in writing. − the single patent protection system was intended to stimulate innovation and competitiveness. unfortunately, i believe that accepting it will have the opposite effect. the big multinational companies will undoubtedly gain, and it should be remembered that very often these companies use patent strategies to block the entry of smaller companies and small and medium-sized enterprises will lose. in new eu countries such as poland, the cost of obtaining a patent will increase. the costs will include translation, procedures and legal services outside the home country. i therefore voted against the adoption of a uniform system of patent protection.

the rapporteur. - mr president! - what are you doing? i would like to thank my colleagues and counter-rapporteurs very much for the many long meetings during which we were able to discuss and reach many compromises. we're in the run-up to the ground handling vote today. contrary to what may appear, the main objective of this document is not to liberalise the groundhandling services sector. the objective of this document is to prepare the european ground handling sector for an appropriate level of global competitiveness. we all remember coming home for christmas two years ago. a lot of us are stuck at airports. why would you do that? because suddenly we ran out of liquid to de-cool the planes. not because the airports were negligent, but because the airlines were not prepared for the winter conditions. as the european parliament, we have proposed for the first time in eu legislation minimum standards, minimum quality requirements for ground handling, including a minimum amount of de-icing liquid for aircraft, so that similar situations do not happen again. each of us has had to wait more than half an hour for an airport check-in or several dozen minutes for a suitcase to be delivered, unless, of course, the suitcase was lost earlier. we've been working on that, too. once the minimum quality requirements i propose are in place, these situations will be kept to a minimum. this regulation will also introduce a single european approval for trading companies. there will therefore be no obstacle to a french company providing its services in, for example, germany. the commission notes that the airport services agreement with ryanair was signed on 28 june 2013 and that the agreement with ryanair was signed on 27 june 2013. unfortunately, the debate on what this document is really about has been dominated by the question of market opening at several european airports. i would not call this opening a liberalisation, but a further, very cautious and conservative opening of the market. for how can we talk about liberalising the services sector if we only offer one additional handling company at the largest airports? this is the case for 90% of european airports. because not two, not three, not four, not even eight companies are providing these services. many times during the discussion of this document, i heard the following arguments: the quality of services and security will decrease. the commission has not found that the measure is compatible with the internal market. if they fall below these requirements, member states at the request of the airport will be able to impose financial penalties on the companies or suspend their licence. argument two: worsening working conditions. untrue: the european commission's proposal included, among other things, the compulsory takeover of employees of the company that loses the tender and a guarantee of employment. social rights have been further strengthened by the employment committee, thanks to a report by mep thomas mann. thirdly, it will have a negative impact on european airports. untrue: the real liberalisation of the sector was carried out in 1996. there are 11 categories of ground handling services. the market for seven of them was fully liberalised over 15 years ago. however, for the four categories: ramps, baggage handling, mail, passenger handling and refuelling, there must be no less than two handling agents at the airport. ladies and gentlemen! as rapporteur, i ask you to look at this document as objectively as possible. not through the eyes of a few airports that want to maintain their monopoly position as an airport and ground handling company, but through the eyes of the tens of millions of passengers who travel from european airports every year.
the question asked by raising the blue card. this is a question for congressman klinz. what do you call radical liberalization? i understand your favorite airport is frankfurt airport. there are actually two companies providing handling services there today. one of these companies has 85% of the market, and the other has 15%. in my document and in the amendment i tabled for tomorrow's vote, i proposed three (from two to three). it is not a 100% increase, but a 50% increase, and as far as social issues are concerned, i am sure that we all had the opportunity today to see several thousand unionists in yellow jackets standing in front of parliament. i had a meeting with them right after they finished their protest. do you know what they said? they said they want this document back to the transportation commission.
mr. chairman, please! i understand the commission had good intentions, only that the road to hell is paved with good intentions. the commission intends to improve the efficiency and quality of groundhandling services by further increasing 'competition between service providers'. unfortunately, the commission did not take into account the specific conditions of the industry. these conditions mean that the re-imposition of the regulation would have the exact opposite effect to that which was intended, at least in the declarations. remember, the smaller the market share of service providers, the more so-called downtime occurs. as a result, increasing the number of service providers at the same time, in the same airport, reduces the productivity of the crew instead of increasing it. i understand that the patent that the commission has, i.e. the increase in productivity, is to be implemented by reducing wages and that is how you might intend to achieve it. well, increasing the number of competitors doesn't increase efficiency, because there's basically nothing to improve. remember, the number of competing service companies doesn't just add more planes. i met with the protesters. they want this project to be sent back to the european commission. so i turn to my esteemed foreword, mr. higgins, and i turn to mr. gross. let's make a decision tomorrow, let's vote. this project should be returned to the european commission. let's get a new design that takes into account the interests of the passengers and the need for professionalism and safety.
mr. chairman, please! i would like to refer to the discussion on the third project, namely the project to deal with airport services. this is the project that has been the most contentious among us here. it would seem that a greater opening of this market should be beneficial for passengers. but the fundamental question is, would that be the case in practice? i believe that the safety of flights and passengers is of paramount importance. we must be absolutely certain that increased competition will not lower safety standards in any given situation. i therefore have a question to the rapporteur: has this been given due consideration in the regulation? because in every situation, flight safety must be the priority.
the rapporteur. - mr president! - what are you doing? i'll try to be as quick as possible and answer the most common questions. in general, this discussion showed how difficult the subject was. and suddenly, in this discussion, the biggest liberal in this room is a conservative, and the liberal who represented the liberal faction turned out to be very conservative and very conservative. i'm glad we've been able to reach so many compromises. i hope that once this document is returned to the transport committee, these compromises will allow us to finish working on this document. many arguments were used. my liberal colleague, who i no longer see in the room, used the productivity argument as the main argument against this document. what is this productivity? that's the time when an employee doesn't have five minutes in eight hours to even drink a glass of water. 100% productivity would be if he had absolutely no time for anything else. three weeks ago, i visited narita airport in tokyo. this is an airport that is completely liberalised, there are no barriers to companies being able to do free business, i.e. between airlines and handling companies. there are nine operating handling companies, including three independent ones. i asked about productivity, what do employees do when there's no rush hour, there's what's called off-peak hours? is it to their detriment? the japanese, who are known to have a high regard for work and working time, were very surprised by this question. they told me that if they had a little time off, they could eat, they could rest, and they could even get some training. they don't have three days of training, as we want to introduce in this regulation, but they have these trainings every day, every other day, every third day, depending on whether the workers have a moment off or they don't have that moment off. it's a matter of safety and security. my colleague zemke asked about this issue among others. of course, this was one of the most important issues in the document. any handling company that is approved under this regulation will have to prove that it is a safe company and that it meets all the protection requirements. these are very important issues, indeed crucial for this regulation. and now the question which should interest my socialist colleagues, my green colleagues, my colleagues from the gue, and also my colleagues from the ppe in the frankfurt airport area, who have mentioned so many times today how important social issues are, how important the safety of workers is, how important it is today that these workers feel safe.
