in writing. – today's debate on enhanced cooperation on the financial transaction tax (ftt) marks an important milestone in the long-anticipated introduction of the policy. applying a low-rate, wide-base tax on the main financial classes, the ftt is expected to generate tens of billions of euros to the public purse, further decreasing the financial burden on ordinary eu citizens. importantly, the ftt could also be used as a tool to regulate markets, curb speculation and encourage sustainable economic growth. i would have liked to see the ftt applied throughout the entire eu; however, as that is impossible, i welcome the decision of 11 member states to introduce the ftt in the framework of enhanced cooperation on the basis of the commission proposal of september 2011. even with the participation of 11 countries, enhanced cooperation on the ftt would contribute to a stronger single market with fewer barriers and distortions. it would also ensure a fairer contribution from the financial sector, which is currently under-taxed by about €18 billion a year. i remain hopeful that more member states will consider joining the common ftt system once it has been established in order to support the eu’s internal market, financial recovery and long-term growth.
in writing. the draft financial transaction tax was strongly opposed by the european parliament from the outset. some meps saw it as a tool to punish banks for causing the crisis, a way to introduce a genuine eu tax that would directly feed the eu budget, or a way to fight speculators. the commission notes that the ftt is a tax on the supply of services and that the tax is not a tax on the supply of services. the result of this deep division is the situation we have today. eleven countries have decided to introduce the tax on their own to set an example to encourage its introduction throughout the european union and eventually the world. we should not oppose the establishment of enhanced cooperation between these countries as long as it does not disrupt the common market, which is also a requirement for the establishment of such cooperation. as we know, the debate on the structure of this tax will take place after we have given our consent, and it is therefore important that the final version of the tax does not have a negative impact on countries that have not joined it.
the rapporteur. - mr president! - what are you doing? we are living in the 21st century europe, we are not barbarians, but a civilization of people with a certain sensitivity. this sensitivity requires us to treat animals - sentient beings who experience fear and pain - in a humane way, worthy of our civilization and culture. we have regulations in the european union on the humane transport of animals, which we are paying attention to today. we have received a report from the european commission on the implementation of these transports, which are increasing. every year, almost 30 million pigs, over 4 million cows, 4 million sheep and over 150 000 horses are transported between member states, with more than two thirds of these transport journeys taking more than 8 hours, and the number of animals transported, except horses, increasing year by year. animals are transported over very long distances, for long periods of time sometimes more than 24 hours and it is very difficult to ensure effective control of these transports. the situation is ripe for serious consideration of the idea put forward by many civil society organisations and many citizens of the union to limit the transport of animals to a maximum of 8 hours. this is also the position of my report, which was adopted by a large majority in the committee on agriculture and rural development. shorter transportation times mean better welfare for animals. shorter transport times mean healthier meat, since it is known that prolonged stress deposits toxins in the animal's body. the shorter transportation also means lower costs, because long-distance transportation is very expensive, and the costs are borne by the farmer who receives less for his animals and by the consumer who pays for these transportations at a higher price for the meat he buys. shorter transportation also means fewer vehicles on the road and less co2 emissions, and it also means the possibility of developing local meat processing in rural areas, close to the farms. the current concentration of the meat industry in the big corporations is not good. the serious consideration of the idea of limiting animal transport to 8 hours, as proposed in the report, is a compromise. we're not saying it's going to happen immediately; we're not saying it's going to happen everywhere, because we're making exceptions, for example, for geographical reasons for islands or peripheral regions. we want to bring this report to the attention of the commission and we cannot remain silent to the voice of the citizens, and more than a million union citizens have signed a petition to limit the transport of animals to 8 hours. we cannot ignore the voice of those people who, out of a sense of vulnerability, are demanding such a limitation. we cannot agree with the commission which ignores these voices and says 'no because no'. we cannot put the interests of big industry and transportation companies above our civilized and cultural relationship with animals. i would therefore ask all of you to accept my report without amendment. we have worked really well in committee to reach a sensible and rational compromise, and i would like to thank all the members of the committee on agriculture and also the other colleagues from the animal welfare intergroup for their very good cooperation. mr. president, mahatma gandhi said that the greatness of a nation and its moral progress can be judged by the way it treats its animals. we use animals for our consumption and our economy, and this will probably not change in the near future. but at the present time, we should do everything in our power to reduce the suffering of animals in all the areas in which we are using them. the limiting of transport times is a concrete issue in which we can care for animals and show evidence of high-level civilisation and culture in the 21st century.
mr. chairman, please! i would like to support this initiative and this report. i would also like to thank mr wojciechowski for his contribution, for seeking a compromise but also for his constant efforts to make these rules good for animals. in 2005, the solutions that we talked about were introduced, and a lot of people were talking about it and wondering if it was worth it. today, all the research, all the experience shows that we took a good step, in a very good direction, and that step brought certain results. we have focused on animal welfare, but we have also improved economic conditions for farmers and entrepreneurs. and today is the moment when we should go even further. therefore, the reduction in the transport time of animals is a good and very sensible proposal. we're going to help strengthen local processing, local slaughter. these will be jobs in those places where they're really needed most today. and at the same time, we're going to reduce costs, which is very important. transporting animals over long distances increases costs, and at the same time, the meat that then reaches consumers is much more expensive than it could be. it is also important that today, despite the rules - and this is why we are also calling on the commission and the member states in this report to carry out veterinary inspections - that despite certain rules, these procedures, which are in place, are not fully respected. this is not just transportation, but the loading and unloading of animals. i call on the commission to do everything possible to ensure that this situation is constantly being changed in favour of improving animal welfare.
mr. chairman, please! wojciechowski is not in favour of long-distance transport of animals and is talking about limiting them to 8 hours. i'd prefer it to be six hours, that's about 500 kilometers of transportation. however, restricting the transport of animals is a very difficult problem. slaughterhouses and businesses are increasing their scale of operations, i.e. the number of animals slaughtered, in order to meet environmental requirements and improve their efficiency, and this leads to the delivery of animals from ever greater distances. i am more concerned with transport conditions, the availability of water, air and the quality of transport. longer consignments are dictated mainly by the requirements of the foreign customer. the transport of live animals is usually organised and dispatched by representatives of foreign customers and is dictated by market demand in the countries of destination. in this situation, the introduction of further restrictions to reduce transport time will hit agricultural producers who will be deprived of the opportunity to sell their products. the reduction of the journey time of animals will result in the need to load them more frequently for a journey break, which, combined with re-loading, is associated with very high stress for the animals, not to mention the possibility of unnecessary injuries and a deterioration of the safety conditions. in conclusion, the current rules governing the transport of animals over long distances represent a reasonable, albeit necessary, compromise between the need to ensure the highest possible animal welfare and economic conditions, which does not mean that there is not much more that can be done to improve the transport of animals, and i agree with the rapporteur. and i'll end with a little joke: wouldn't it be more humane to drive the animals away?
mr. chairman, please! i would like to encourage support for the report on the protection of animals during transport, which proposes to reduce the maximum journey time for animals for slaughter to 8 hours. the report also contains - from my point of view - three very important amendments which relate to improving transport conditions and the functioning of the control points. for a long time now, and i would like to stress here why the request in mr wojciechowski's report is so radical and why i support this request to limit transport to 8 hours, it is because for a long time the european commission, in its work on the implementation of the directive, has very stubbornly avoided dealing with the question of transport time for animals in general, despite many studies, very diverse studies, which indicate the need for change. i hope that the position of parliament, which will be expressed and will support this demand for the reduction of the transport time of animals, will lead to a serious debate on this subject and in the long term lead to a reduction in the practice of transporting live animals for slaughter over very long distances.
the rapporteur. - mr president! - what are you doing? i thank all the members who have spoken here. i thank you for all the votes: those who fully agreed with my report and those who had some doubts or criticisms about its content. i would like to thank in particular the shadow rapporteurs, who have been a great team to work with on this difficult report. in taking on the responsibility of producing it, i did not even realize that i was taking on a report that would stir up so much emotion and controversy. what has been presented in my report is a kind of compromise. on the one hand, we had proposals going forward with very large time restrictions on the transport of animals. there have been suggestions not to raise the issue at all. i think what has been presented is a reasonable compromise on this issue, and i would very much like to see that compromise upheld in tomorrow's vote. we're going to vote tomorrow. tomorrow is the 12th day, the 12th month, the 12th year, and at noon we will vote. i would like to see the four twelve happy with this report and that we really do take a significant step towards a real improvement in the conditions under which animal transport takes place in the european union.
in writing. harmonised implementation and enforcement of animal rights legislation is important to maintain high animal welfare standards and prevent market disturbances in the european union. the increasing concentration of slaughterhouses, driven by increasing veterinary, sanitary and environmental requirements, is extending the transport routes for animals for slaughter. given the specificity of the road infrastructure and the related speed limitations, the transport of animals may take more than 8 hours even within the borders of poland. this will undoubtedly result in a deterioration in the comfort of transport for the animals, because this situation will force the transporters to increase the transport speed to the maximum allowed. i therefore call on the member states to implement the existing rules on animal transport properly and i call on the commission to support local processing wherever possible. eu policy should aim to create short and transparent supply chains and, for longer journeys to deliver food to further regions, to ensure the best possible epizootic safety conditions, regardless of the duration of such journeys.

mr. chairman, please! i agree with the need to prepare and sign a new partnership and cooperation agreement between the union and russia. russia remains our biggest neighbor, and it borders poland directly. however, the current agreement was concluded long before my country joined the communities. the slow pace of the negotiations, which is the fault of the russians, is worrying because of the apparent lack of interest on the part of the kremlin authorities in complementary solutions. the new interim agreement should provide a forward-looking and legally binding framework for the further development of the mutual relations. in this context, the rule of law and democracy issues should be emphasised, with particular regard to the guarantee by the russian authorities of the freedom and integrity of elections in that country. it is essential to focus on improving the situation of civil society and protecting individual rights. in supporting the resolution, i also support the call on russia to withdraw its recognition of the georgian provinces of abkhazia and south ossetia and to respect the ceasefire agreement.
mr. chairman, please! the recent elections in ukraine have shown that challenges to basic electoral standards and obstacles to full transparency and democratisation remain to be taken seriously. the imprisonment of the leaders of the orange revolution certainly did not leave the opposition groups' campaign unsuccessful. in addition, the imperfections of the ukrainian electoral law have become apparent. in the context of our relations, i consider it highly desirable to continue with the signing of the association agreement. the country still has strong pro-european aspirations. however, it is necessary to establish a constructive dialogue between the ukrainian authorities and the opposition. i also hope that concrete and satisfactory solutions can be found in the case of ms yulia tymoshenko. i also support the liberalization of visa policy for ukraine, which is an expression of our deep commitment to developing contacts with the people of that country. i voted to pass the resolution.
in writing. − the debate on the multiannual framework for the european union agency for fundamental rights for the years 2013-2017 is an important topic. the fundamental rights agency does valuable work by, among other things, providing eu bodies and member states with expertise in the field of fundamental rights. its remit therefore revolves around important issues such as the fight against racism, xenophobia and all forms of discrimination. in addition, it addresses issues such as the protection of children's and immigrant rights, visa and border controls, and the protection of personal data. however, the functioning of the agency may raise doubts, in particular as regards the scope of its competences and the costs associated with its activities. therefore, an in-depth discussion of the substance of the agency's activities and the scope of its competence is needed. the debate on the possible inclusion of police and judicial cooperation in criminal matters in the agency's list of thematic areas is also important. in times of financial crisis, the need to be very cautious about spending money on the functioning of the eu institutions and agencies requires a thorough analysis of the fundamental rights agency's work planning and related expenditure.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report by mr rafal trzaskowski on written declarations and proposals for eu legal acts. i believe that the solutions proposed could have a positive impact on the process of preparing them and increase their relevance. written declarations are a tool for the european parliament to address issues of particular relevance to union citizens. the proposed changes include increasing the minimum number of members required to make a statement from five to at least 10 from at least three political groups and limiting the topics to issues falling within the exclusive competence of the eu. in addition, an electronic register of declarations and an electronic form for the submission of signatures of support were proposed. this will allow for much needed clarification of procedures and streamlining of the work of parliament in preparing statements and proposals on eu legal acts. it will also enhance the european parliament's role as a major player in the eu's institutional system.
in writing. − i decided to support the initiative aiming at a thorough reform of the system of written declarations. a tool which used to be one of the main weapons of position-taking by the ep in the past has become, with the treaty of lisbon, obsolete. it is important to reconsider its raison d’être and make the tool more meaningful, inter alia by rendering it possible to turn a wd with significant support by meps into legislative initiatives, where the eu has the right competence to do so.
in writing. - the european parliament has grown enormously over the years and today, as a co-legislator, it has real instruments at its disposal to influence what happens in the european union. written statements are a tool from a time when parliament had little influence. moreover, it is a totally ineffective tool, because studies show that these statements are rarely met with a response from the institutions to which they are addressed. limiting the use of this instrument to the increased initiative of members themselves is to adapt the ep's rules of procedure to the realities in which parliament functions today and to encourage members to take more meaningful action.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the eu's human rights strategy. in the context of this report and yesterday's debate on human rights, i would like to underline parliament's call to pay particular attention to harmful traditional practices, such as female genital mutilation, in the implementation of the strategy to combat violence against women. i call on the commission to ensure that measures to combat gender-based violence and to empower women are mainstreamed in all development policies and programmes of the union. the union must also accelerate the pace of achieving its objectives. strategy alone, even the best, is not enough. to achieve the objectives effectively, we need clear and precise guidelines for the practical implementation of the human rights strategy in every area of the union's activities. it means that every official and diplomat must know his role and responsibility in this matter. any summary of the implementation of eu policies must also include progress in the implementation of the human rights strategy.
in writing. − i welcome the appointment of a european union special representative for human rights, an office whose primary objective will be to strengthen human rights policy in all eu external policy strategies and to improve coordination between the union and its member states. it has the potential to make the union's approach to human rights violations worldwide more effective. it may also affect the respect of other fundamental human rights, such as the promotion of women's rights, children's rights and social justice. in my view, the european union should step up its efforts to protect and support human rights defenders in third countries, especially those who are in danger or living in fear because of their involvement. this will for example require changes and additional priorities in the use of the recently established european endowment for democracy. it will also require legislation requiring eu companies to significantly reduce or even stop purchasing from third countries if an audit shows that they may be contributing to conflict and gross human rights violations.
in writing. − the defence of human rights is an important element of the european union's foreign policy. however, i am missing a number of important points in the report under consideration. the protection of religious freedom in the world is of particular importance, with particular regard to the situation of christians. it is the largest and most persecuted religion in the world today. in many countries where the european community is active, such as pakistan, egypt and saudi arabia, there is mass persecution of followers of jesus. the situation in egypt is particularly dire. the report we're discussing is silent on this. but it does contain provisions that run counter to the values that underpin the european community and the greek and roman culture, such as support for adoption by same-sex couples. i can't agree to such a record, which is why i voted against it.
in writing. - good relations with russia, europe's great neighbour, are important from both a political and an economic perspective. russia is a huge market and therefore an important trading partner of the union countries, and all efforts should be made to develop and facilitate existing economic relations. the negotiations should focus on improving customs and visa rules to improve the flow of people and goods. negotiations with the russian authorities are necessary to lift the import ban on many goods originating in the union and to cancel the increase in duties on certain goods, as these measures have caused huge losses, in particular to european farmers and food producers for whom the russian market was the main market. we need to act as a unified body in dealing with russia, which will increase our bargaining power.
in writing. − russia's accession to the wto after nearly 20 years of negotiations is significant. but it is an illusion to think that this ends the trade dispute between the european union and russia. for russia, trade is also a political weapon. the third energy package will undoubtedly be the most serious source of tension in economic relations between russia and the eu. gazprom has indeed announced that it will comply with the terms of the package and separate the pipeline company from the gas sales company. he's also gonna make the pipelines available to other companies. we call on the european commission to ensure that gazprom keeps its promise. and to make sure that this process is as transparent as possible. today, russia is threatening to raise moldova's prices if it does not withdraw from the energy community. two months ago, unofficial statements by members of the russian government suggested that russia could challenge the third package provisions allowing for the forced ownership separation of distribution networks from gas and energy sales to the wto court. have the commission's legal services analysed this matter in order to be able to assess what the verdict in this case might be? russia is an important trading partner of the eu. the integration of our economies has undoubtedly increased in recent times, and you can do this by going to any russian store or, for example, the warsaw metro, which is served by trains produced in russia. but we must fight and condemn all forms of protectionism to which the russian government has resorted.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the negotiations for a new agreement between the eu and russia. the current agreement was signed in 1994 and should be replaced by a new one that reflects the changes that have taken place both in the eu and in russia. however, the pace of negotiations is very slow, russia is not particularly interested in a new comprehensive agreement and is showing a selective interest in developing common political strategies. the european parliament would like the new agreement to be legally binding and as comprehensive as possible, and to have human rights issues at its heart. the report strongly condemned the lack of rule of law and democracy in russia and called on the russian authorities to put an end to the climate of impunity and selective justice.
in writing. - i've been following the situation in ukraine with interest. given its size, geographical location and strong historical, cultural and economic links with central and eastern europe, ukraine plays a key role in the region and is an important partner of the european union. in view of ukraine's european aspirations and the prospect of the signing of an association agreement between the european union and ukraine, it is necessary to intensify efforts to better protect human rights, respect for civil liberties and fundamental freedoms, and the rule of law, including fair and impartial trials. it is also important to continue economic reforms. the european union, through, inter alia, numerous resolutions of the european parliament and statements by catherine ashton, high representative of the union for foreign affairs and security policy, has drawn attention to the existence of a number of challenges and problems faced by ukraine, such as the arrest of political opposition leaders and the violations of electoral procedures during parliamentary elections, as documented in the osce/odihr reports. however, i believe that joint efforts will overcome the difficulties and ensure effective cooperation between the european union and ukraine, to the benefit of both parties.
in writing. − parliamentary elections were held in ukraine on 28 october. in the context of the completion of the association agreement, the european union observed these elections in particular. international observation missions, including the european parliament's observation mission, have identified irregularities throughout the electoral process. while the voting itself was conducted correctly, the pre-election period was assessed negatively. the main problems are the lack of transparency in the financing of electoral campaigns, the lack of a level playing field for campaigning (leaders of the orange revolution remain in prison, lack of balanced access to the media) and the imperfections of the new electoral law. the strong support in the elections for political parties that speak of the need to move closer to the eu is evidence of the european aspirations of ukrainian society.
in writing. − i have chosen to abstain from voting on the amendment condemning the ukrainian party svoboda. it is with great concern that i am observing the growth of nationalistic and xenophobic spirits in the western part of ukraine. i realize that the group responsible for that, to a large extent, is svoboda. the party has been cultivated by the traditions of bandera, thus i, as well as europe, condemn such actions, which are destructive for ukrainian aspirations for integration to the european union. at the same time, svoboda repeatedly showed its support for european integration in the supreme council and deserves some time to change their nationalist-chauvinist politics. to be credible, the party has to refuse to use its xenophobic slogans and radically change its politics. we will continue watching closely the actions of svoboda and its european action plan, as i believe signing the eu association agreement will play a great role in establishing political and economic reforms in ukraine and will get the country closer to integration with the european community.
in writing. − the steel sector in europe is experiencing a crisis of declining competitiveness and rising production costs, largely due to the wrong decisions to adopt an energy and climate package mandating a reduction in greenhouse gases by 2020. in poland alone, the implementation of its provisions will increase unemployment by about 250 thousand people and increase energy prices. due to the increase in production costs and reduced demand, more than 600 people are now planned to be laid off in the sędzimir hut in kraków alone, and similar group layoffs are planned in sosnowiec, chorzów and warsaw. if the situation does not change, there will be further closures of large furnaces and a shift of production to ukraine and india, where no climate restrictions apply. this is all the more sad as the sector accounts for 7.5% of all european industry and is one of the largest employers in the european union industry. the steel rescue programme should therefore be based on the suspension of the provisions of the energy and climate package, which is leading to the deindustrialisation of europe. another important factor is the blocking of imports of low-priced steel from the former soviet union and china. the resolutions we are voting on do not address the threats i mentioned, which is why i abstained.
mr. chairman, please! the april congolese rebellion against the country's government forces has led to a collapse in security and an alarming humanitarian crisis in the country. the un, which accused rwanda of supporting the march 23rd movement, joined the fighting to support the congolese army and stop the rebel march. the ongoing fighting has displaced nearly 2.5 million people, with more than 400,000 fleeing to neighbouring rwanda and uganda. thousands of civilians living in the areas of conflict have been subjected to violence, torture and rape. the developments in eastern congo have caused great concern to the international community, resulting in a social, political and economic crisis in the country. first of all, all acts of aggression and flagrant violations of the basic human rights of the local population must be condemned and all lawbreakers and war criminals must be punished without mercy. the democratic republic of congo must restore stability to the country by establishing strong and independent institutions that meet international standards. the european union should continue its efforts to support the people of eastern congo in an even more coordinated and effective manner, providing medical and humanitarian assistance to all those affected by this bloody conflict.
mr. chairman, please! of course, the political situation in the great lakes region is extremely complex, and the humanitarian situation is extremely dramatic. and we can't solve these problems without easing tensions, for example, between the congo and rwanda. pressure is needed so that the leaders of both countries condemn and stop supporting any rebel groups, regardless of their origin, ethnicity or political goals. the international community, and therefore also we, the european union, must put pressure on both neighbouring countries to resume bilateral cooperation aimed at eliminating all the negative forces operating in eastern congo. the mandate of monusco should also be modified accordingly. and one last thing: international action must be taken against the illegal mining of mineral resources in eastern congo. it is worth considering the establishment of a certification mechanism modelled on the kimberley process.
the author. - mr president! - what are you doing? the caste system still exists in many parts of asia. the divisions in society are very deep and go back to the very beginning of these nations. discrimination and exclusion of different social groups is therefore practically universally accepted. the dalits, commonly called "untouchables", are the lowest caste in india. as a result, they live isolated from other groups, with limited access to services, employment, education, or land. they are victims of physical attacks and humiliation. in recent months, dalit-inhabited provinces have been hit by a wave of violence, including the rape of women and children. ninety percent of these incidents go unreported because the victims fear for their lives and further exclusion from indian society. the constitution of independent india banned caste discrimination by introducing the principle of equal opportunity in access to public services, education and employment. these regulations exist on paper, but are not sufficiently enforced by the indian authorities. the changes will not be easy to implement, as the caste system still dominates indian society, especially in rural areas. but i believe that india, as a democratic country, will be able to deal with this problem. furthermore, i hope that other countries in the region will follow india's example and take legislative action to end discrimination against parts of their own society.
